# AIGate — Capability Specification

Every item below is a capability AIGate must have. Derived from tracing
9router, but stated as a requirement of AIGate, not as a description of
9router. Suspected bugs are listed separately and must NOT be reproduced.

## API-key providers

### GET /api/providers/kilo/free-models — live fetch plus a 1-hour server-side cache of Kilo's free-tier model list

- **id:** `catalog.kilo-free-models-cache` · **module:** `catalog`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard Kilo connection setup / model-picker UI
- **Input:** none
- **Output:** { models:[{id,name,isFree,context_length}], cached } or { models:[], error } on total failure
- **Rules:**
  - The result is cached in a module-scope variable (cachedModels/cacheTimestamp) for 60 minutes — every request within that window is served from memory with zero upstream calls
  - On a fetch failure after the cache expired, a stale cached copy is still served (with a warning field) rather than erroring, as long as any cache exists at all; only a cold cache with a failing fetch returns a 502
  - Filtering to isFree===true happens server-side before caching — the cache stores only the free subset, not the full Kilo catalog
- **Errors:** `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (fetch fails or returns non-OK and no cache (even stale) exists)

### POST /api/oauth/gitlab/pat — authenticate GitLab Duo with a Personal Access Token instead of an OAuth code/device flow

- **id:** `oauth.gitlab-pat` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** Operator pastes a GitLab PAT (and optionally a self-hosted GitLab baseUrl) into the connect UI
- **Input:** { token, baseUrl? }
- **Output:** { success: true } on a verified token; 401 with the upstream error text on a bad token
- **Rules:**
  - GitLab does support a real OAuth authorize/token flow elsewhere in the registry (gitlab.js has an oauth block with authorizeUrlPath/tokenUrlPath) — this route is the alternate, code-flow-free path for users who prefer a long-lived PAT over an interactive OAuth login, verified by calling GET {baseUrl}/api/v4/user with a Private-Token header rather than any OAuth endpoint
  - baseUrl defaults to https://gitlab.com but accepts any self-hosted GitLab instance URL (trailing slash stripped) — the PAT path is also how self-hosted GitLab is supported at all through this connect flow, since PATs are the standard cross-instance credential
  - Despite bypassing OAuth entirely, the resulting connection is stored with authType: "oauth" (not "apikey") — an inconsistency with how the connection is actually authenticated (a static Private-Token header, not a bearer OAuth token), noted here as an oddity rather than a functional bug since nothing currently branches on authType==="oauth" specifically for gitlab in a way that would misbehave
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (token is missing/empty), `AUTH_ERROR` (GitLab's /api/v4/user rejects the token (non-ok response))

### POST /api/oauth/iflow/cookie — derive an iFlow API key from a pasted browser session cookie, no OAuth handshake at all

- **id:** `oauth.iflow-cookie` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** Operator pastes an iFlow browser cookie string (containing BXAuth=...) into the connect UI
- **Input:** { cookie: "BXAuth=xxx; ..." }
- **Output:** { success, connection: { id, provider, email, apiKey (masked to first 10 chars + ...), expireTime } }
- **Rules:**
  - iflow does support a standard OAuth flow through the generic route (open-sse/providers/registry/iflow.js has clientId/clientSecret/tokenUrl/authorizeUrl) — this route is a completely separate mechanism for users who only have browser session access (BXAuth cookie) and no OAuth app credential context, common for iFlow's web-only platform features
  - The flow is a two-step dance against iFlow's own web API, not an OAuth endpoint: GET /api/openapi/apikey with the cookie to read the existing key's name, then POST the same endpoint with that name to force a key refresh/rotation and get back the actual apiKey value — the cookie itself is never the stored credential, only the vehicle to mint an apiKey
  - Only the BXAuth=... segment is extracted from the (possibly larger) pasted cookie string via regex and re-normalized with a trailing semicolon before being stored in providerSpecificData.cookie — the rest of the pasted cookie header is discarded
  - The resulting connection is stored with authType: "cookie" — a third authType value distinct from both "oauth" and "apikey"/"api_key" used elsewhere in this inventory, reflecting that neither the transport.auth (raw apiKey) model nor the OAuth refresh model fits: the credential is an apiKey, but obtaining/renewing it requires re-supplying the cookie, which none of the auth.refresh-* mechanisms know how to do automatically
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (cookie is missing, not a string, or doesn't contain BXAuth=), `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (the GET or POST to iFlow's apikey endpoint returns a non-ok response), `INVALID_REQUEST` (iFlow's own API returns success:false in its JSON body (both GET and POST steps))

### POST /api/oauth/kiro/api-key — import a long-lived Kiro/Amazon Q headless API key, no OAuth or refresh token model

- **id:** `oauth.kiro-api-key` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** Operator pastes a Kiro headless API key (and optional AWS region) into the connect UI
- **Input:** { apiKey, region? }
- **Output:** { success, connection: { id, provider, email } }
- **Rules:**
  - Kiro's normal path is a full AWS SSO OIDC device/social OAuth flow (see oauth.kiro-import / oauth.kiro-social-authorize / oauth.kiro-social-exchange) — this route exists for Kiro's separate "headless auth" API-key mechanism, a completely different Amazon Q credential type with no authorization code, device code, or refresh token involved at all
  - The key is validated up front by KiroService.validateApiKey against the same Amazon Q model-catalog surface used for live inference — an invalid key is rejected before any connection row is written
  - Because API keys never expire on a fixed schedule and have no refresh token, expiresAt is hardcoded to now + 365 days purely so the proactive-refresh scheduling path (which requires a refreshToken to do anything) is naturally skipped for this connection, not because the key is contractually valid for exactly one year
  - On any validation failure, the route returns a generic "API key validation failed" message rather than echoing KiroService's actual error — the code comment marks this as deliberate SSRF hardening (don't reflect an upstream response body driven by user-supplied region/key back to the client)
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (apiKey is missing/empty), `AUTH_ERROR` (KiroService.validateApiKey rejects the key/region pair)

## Auto fallback

### What the client receives when the account loop runs out

- **id:** `fallback.accounts-exhausted-response` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** getProviderCredentials returns null or allRateLimited inside the account loop
- **Input:** credentials result, excludeConnectionIds size, lastError, lastStatus
- **Output:** 503 with Retry-After, 404, or the last upstream status
- **Rules:**
  - allRateLimited (every non-excluded account carries an active model lock): 503 `[provider/model] <lastError or stored lastError>` with a Retry-After header computed from the earliest lock expiry
  - null on the first iteration (no active connections at all): 404 `No active credentials for provider: X`
  - null after at least one account was excluded (remaining accounts neither available nor locked): lastStatus || 503 with lastError
  - Because a failed account is BOTH excluded and locked, the allRateLimited branch is what normally fires after the last account fails — so the client gets 503, not the upstream status
- **Errors:** `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (all accounts locked — 503 with Retry-After), `AUTH_ERROR` (no active connection for the provider — 404)

### Reactive 401/403 handling — refresh credentials, re-execute once

- **id:** `fallback.auth-refresh-retry` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** Upstream returns 401 or 403 and the executor is not noAuth
- **Input:** The failed response, credentials, executor.refreshCredentials
- **Output:** Either a successful retry response replacing the original, or the ORIGINAL 401/403 response continuing to error handling
- **Rules:**
  - refreshWithRetry(fn, 3): up to 3 refresh attempts with 1 s then 2 s sleeps; a null result counts as a failure and is retried
  - Rotating refresh tokens (xAI / grok-cli) are written back onto credentials between attempts so attempt 2/3 do not reuse a consumed token
  - On success: credentials are merged, onCredentialsRefreshed persists them, and the request is executed ONCE more with the full executor retry budget
  - The retry response is adopted only if response.ok; a non-ok retry (e.g. 429 after refresh) is dropped and the original 401/403 is what gets classified
- **Errors:** `AUTH_ERROR` (refresh yields nothing or the retry is not ok — original 401/403 flows to fallback.error-classification (2 min lock, next account))
- **AIGate required behavior:** A 401/403 on an account that has nothing to refresh (API-key credentials, or a provider with no refresher) fails fast to the next account

### Which upstream outcomes retry, switch account, switch combo model, or return to the client

- **id:** `fallback.error-classification` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** Any failed single-model attempt (result.success false) in handleSingleModelChat, and any non-2xx member Response in handleComboChat
- **Input:** result.status, result.error text, resetsAtMs, provider, model, the connection's backoffLevel
- **Output:** shouldFallback + a model-scoped lock; the combo engine re-runs the same classifier on the final Response
- **Rules:**
  - Q2 TABLE. Columns = in-place retry (executor, same URL) | next baseUrl | next ACCOUNT (chat.js loop, lock written) | next combo MODEL (combo.js) | returned to client immediately
  - 400 generic (bad params, context too long, schema): no | no | YES, 30 s transient lock | YES | no
  - 400 containing 'improperly formed request' (kiro): no | no | YES, 2 min lock | YES | no
  - 400 from local translation failure (chatCore translateRequest returned nothing): n/a (no upstream call) | no | YES, 30 s lock | YES | no
  - 401 / 403: no; first a 3-attempt refresh + one re-execute (fallback.auth-refresh-retry) | no | YES, 2 min lock | YES | no
  - 402: no | no | YES, 2 min lock (GitHub monthly-limit text: account-wide lock until the 1st of next UTC month) | YES | no
  - 404: no | no | YES, 2 min lock | YES | no
  - 409 / 422 / other 4xx: no (antigravity 409 triggers a live quota refresh) | no | YES, 30 s lock (antigravity with reset: RAM-only exclusion) | YES | no
  - 429: default no (antigravity x3, grok-cli x2, vercel-ai-gateway x2) | YES if another baseUrl (kiro) | YES, exponential lock 2 s..5 min, or provider resetsAtMs capped 30 min (antigravity uncapped) | YES | no
  - 500: only antigravity x3 | no | YES, 30 s lock | YES | no
  - 502: x3 @3 s | no | YES, 30 s lock | YES (combo waits first only when the cooldown is <= 5 s, i.e. only for backoff-text matches) | no
  - 503: x3 @2 s | no | YES, 30 s lock, or exponential if the text contains 'overloaded'/'capacity' | YES | no
  - 504: x2 @3 s | no | YES, 30 s lock | YES | no
  - Network error / connect timeout: x3 @3 s (502 entry) | YES if another baseUrl | YES as 502, 30 s lock | YES | no
  - Caller AbortError: no | no | YES as 499, 30 s lock | YES | no
  - 2xx with non-SSE, non-JSON content type on a streaming request: no | no | YES, 30 s lock (status is the 2xx code) | YES | no
  - 2xx then failure mid-stream: no | no | no | no | the truncated stream IS the answer (fallback.partial-stream-failure)
  - Text rules win over status rules: any status whose message contains 'rate limit', 'too many requests', 'quota exceeded', 'capacity' or 'overloaded' gets exponential backoff; 'no credentials' 2 min; 'request not allowed' 5 s
  - Returned to the client immediately (no retry, no fallback): ONLY (a) noAuth providers — markAccountUnavailable returns shouldFallback false for connectionId noauth, so the upstream error is passed straight through; and (b) errors raised before dispatch (invalid JSON, missing/invalid API key, missing model, invalid model format, no credentials 404). checkFallbackError itself NEVER returns shouldFallback false — its final line is a catch-all `{ shouldFallback: true, cooldownMs: 30 s }`
  - 'Fallback to another provider' exists only as 'next combo member' (combo.js); a single-model request never changes provider. The combo `if (!shouldFallback) return result` branch is dead code because the classifier always says true
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (upstream 400 or local translation failure — treated as an account failure: 30 s lock and next account), `AUTH_ERROR` (401/403 after refresh — 2 min lock, next account), `QUOTA_EXHAUSTED` (402, or text 'quota exceeded', or provider resetsAtMs), `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` (404 — 2 min lock, next account), `RATE_LIMIT` (429 or rate-limit text — exponential lock, next account), `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (5xx / network — after in-place retries, 30 s lock, next account), `TIMEOUT` (connect timeout — handled as a 502 network error)
- **AIGate required behavior:** Terminal, request-caused errors (400 invalid request, 404 unknown model, local translation failure, 499 client abort) are returned to the client once, without locking the account (behavioral.md §20: no blind fallback)

### In-place retry (tryRetry) and computeRetryDelay, and the end-to-end retry ceiling

- **id:** `fallback.executor-retry-budget` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** A response status or network error for which retryConfig[status] has attempts > 0
- **Input:** HTTP status (network errors use key 502), DEFAULT_RETRY_CONFIG merged with the provider's transport.retry
- **Output:** Same URL retried after a delay, or the response handed back to the caller
- **Rules:**
  - DEFAULT_RETRY_CONFIG: 429 {0 attempts}, 502 {3, 3000 ms}, 503 {3, 2000 ms}, 504 {2, 3000 ms}; every other status 0. A numeric entry means attempts with the legacy 2000 ms delay
  - Provider overrides: antigravity 429/500/503 x3; grok-cli 429 x2 @2000, 502/503 x2 @1500; vercel-ai-gateway 429 x2 @2000; kiro 429 x0
  - The attempt counter is per URL and shared across status codes: attempts for the CURRENT status are compared against the combined count, so one URL gets at most max(attempts) retries in total
  - Delay is fixed per status (no exponential backoff, no jitter) unless the executor defines computeRetryDelay — only antigravity does
  - Antigravity computeRetryDelay: Retry-After header, then retry hints in the error body; a hint <= 10 s is used, > 10 s vetoes the retry (return false -> fallback); no hint -> non-transient status/message vetoes; transient -> min(1000 * 2^attempt, cap) with cap 10 s for 429 and 15 s otherwise. So computeRetryDelay IS bounded: at most 15 s per wait
  - Retries happen before any status classification — they are purely status-code driven; no idempotency or body inspection in the base executor
- **Errors:** `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (502/503/504 or network error — retried in place up to the configured attempts), `RATE_LIMIT` (429 — no in-place retry by default; antigravity/grok-cli/vercel-ai-gateway retry)

### BaseExecutor.execute — multi-baseUrl loop and connect timeout

- **id:** `fallback.executor-url-loop` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** Every executor.execute call (all executors that do not fully override execute)
- **Input:** model, body, stream, credentials, signal (streamController.signal), proxyOptions
- **Output:** { response, url, headers, transformedBody } for the first URL that is not retried away, or a thrown error
- **Rules:**
  - For each urlIndex: buildUrl, then transformRequest, then buildHeaders (note the order — buildUrl runs BEFORE transformRequest)
  - Connect timeout: a per-attempt AbortController aborts after config.timeoutMs or FETCH_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS (env, default 60000 ms) if response HEADERS have not arrived; the timer is cleared as soon as fetch resolves, so it never bounds body reading
  - The connect signal is merged with the caller signal via AbortSignal.any
  - Moving to the next baseUrl happens only for (a) HTTP 429 when another URL exists (shouldRetry) or (b) a network error / connect timeout after in-place retries are exhausted; a 5xx after its retries is RETURNED, never tried on the next URL
  - A caller-initiated AbortError (not the connect timeout) is re-thrown immediately with no retry
  - Loop exhaustion throws the last error, or `All N URLs failed with status S`
- **Streaming:** yes
- **Errors:** `TIMEOUT` (no response headers within the connect timeout — converted to a retryable network error (502 retry config)), `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (network error on the last URL after retries — thrown, becomes 502 in chatCore), `RATE_LIMIT` (429 with another baseUrl available — next URL (kiro has 3))

### Upstream failure after tokens have already reached the client

- **id:** `fallback.partial-stream-failure` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** The upstream SSE body errors, resets, or stalls after the streaming Response has been returned
- **Input:** Upstream read error (ECONNRESET, socket hang up, ETIMEDOUT, EPIPE, UND_ERR_SOCKET, AbortError from the stall watchdog, or any other error)
- **Output:** A truncated stream — closed cleanly or errored, never resumed on another account
- **Rules:**
  - Q5: there is no mid-stream retry or fallback. handleSingleModelChat already returned result.response when headers were ok, so the account loop and the combo loop have both exited
  - Network-class errors and aborts (including the stall watchdog, which marks the controller disconnected before aborting) close the client stream cleanly; only Responses-API passthrough gets a synthesized response.failed + [DONE] terminal
  - Any other error while still connected calls controller.error(), so the client sees a broken chunked response
  - onRequestSuccess has already fired at header time, so the account's error state and locks are cleared even though the answer was cut off
- **Streaming:** yes
- **Errors:** `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (upstream connection resets after first byte — stream closed gracefully, no error event, no [DONE] on OpenAI/Claude formats), `TIMEOUT` (stall watchdog fires mid-stream — treated as a graceful close), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (non-network error while connected — controller.error(), client connection errors)
- **AIGate required behavior:** A stream cut off mid-answer is signalled to the client as an error (error event or missing terminal it can detect), and the account is not marked healthy

### Turning an executor exception or non-2xx response into an error result

- **id:** `fallback.upstream-error-result` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** executor.execute throws, or the (possibly refreshed) response is not ok
- **Input:** The thrown error or the upstream Response
- **Output:** { success: false, status, error, resetsAtMs, response } via createErrorResult
- **Rules:**
  - Thrown AbortError -> status 499 "Request aborted"; any other throw -> 502 with message `[502]: <message> (cause: <code>)`
  - Non-2xx: parseUpstreamError reads the body once; an executor parseError override may return a different status and a resetsAtMs (e.g. codex usage_limit_reached); default message is error.message || message || error || raw body text
  - The upstream status is preserved into the client error (e.g. upstream 400 -> result.status 400) and the body is re-wrapped in the OpenAI error shape {error:{message,type,code}} using ERROR_TYPES
  - Every failure path writes a request-detail row with status error and zero tokens; appendRequestLog is called too but is a no-op
- **Errors:** `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (executor throws (network, connect timeout after retries, buildUrl throw) — 502), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (AbortError from the caller signal — 499)

### Per-provider account loop — select, execute, classify, exclude, repeat

- **id:** `routing.account-fallback-loop` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** Every resolved {provider, model} pair (once per combo member)
- **Input:** provider, model, the growing excludeConnectionIds set
- **Output:** The first successful Response, a non-fallback error Response, or an exhaustion error (fallback.accounts-exhausted-response)
- **Rules:**
  - while(true): getProviderCredentials(provider, excludeConnectionIds, model) picks one account; locked (modelLock_*) and excluded accounts are filtered out inside the selector (see account.select-locked-and-excluded-filter)
  - The quota check happens here, not before dispatch: the only pre-dispatch quota signal is an active modelLock_* written by a previous failure, plus the Antigravity live-quota cache — there is no proactive quota query for other providers
  - On a failed result the account's fate is decided by markAccountUnavailable (fallback.error-classification). shouldFallback -> add connectionId to excludeConnectionIds, remember lastError/lastStatus, loop. Not shouldFallback -> return result.response to the client
  - Antigravity special case: a 409/429 triggers a live quota refresh; if it yields a reset time the account is excluded WITHOUT writing a persistent modelLock (RAM cache only)
  - The loop is bounded only by the number of active connections for the provider — each iteration excludes one more account
- **Errors:** `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (every account is excluded/locked — see fallback.accounts-exhausted-response)

## CLI Tools

### all-statuses batches 13 per-tool GETs into one response

- **id:** `clitools.all-statuses-batch` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard "Integrations" page load (or refresh) fetching combined tool status
- **Input:** none (GET, no query params)
- **Output:** JSON object keyed by toolId → that tool's own GET response body (or null if its handler threw)
- **Rules:**
  - STATUS_GETTERS re-imports the GET function of exactly 13 of the 19 cli-tools route files (claude, codex, opencode, droid, openclaw, hermes, cowork, cline, kilo, deepseek-tui, jcode, grok-build, devin) and calls each in-process — not over HTTP
  - The other 6 route.js files are deliberately excluded: antigravity-mitm and antigravity-mitm/alias (proxy/DNS control, not an installed-tool status card), copilot-settings (no install-detection step to batch — see clitools.copilot-settings-array-upsert), cowork-mcp-registry and cowork-mcp-tools (MCP marketplace helpers, not tool-status cards), and all-statuses itself
  - Each per-tool getter is invoked via Promise.all so all 13 run concurrently; a getter that throws is caught per-entry and mapped to null rather than failing the whole batch
- **Errors:** `INTERNAL_ERROR` (an individual tool's GET handler throws (e.g. unreadable settings file); that tool's slot becomes null, other 12 slots are unaffected)

### Start/stop the local MITM server, toggle per-tool hosts-file DNS interception, and manage per-tool model-alias rewrite mappings

- **id:** `clitools.antigravity-mitm-control` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard "MITM" card — GET/POST/DELETE/PATCH on the base route; GET/PUT on the alias sub-route
- **Input:** POST { apiKey, sudoPassword, mitmRouterBaseUrl, forceKillPort443 }; PATCH { tool, action, sudoPassword }; alias PUT { tool, mappings }
- **Output:** Status objects (running/pid/cert/dnsStatus/isAdmin) or { success, ... }
- **Rules:**
  - Not a CLI config-file writer like the other 18 routes: this manages 9router's OWN local MITM proxy process and the machine's hosts file/DNS state for the tool hostnames in src/shared/constants/mitmToolHosts.js, plus a Root CA install into the OS trust store
  - Privilege model: on Windows, checkIsAdmin probes `net session`; on other platforms, root or a cached/stored sudo password is required unless isSudoPasswordRequired() is false. POST/PATCH refuse with 403 if the caller lacks the needed privilege
  - startServer's 409 PORT_443_BUSY error carries a portOwner so the caller can offer to force-kill whatever is squatting on 443 (forceKillPort443 flag)
  - DELETE (stop) kills the MITM server process first, THEN (inside stopServer, manager.js) strips every tool hostname from the OS hosts file in one unconditional pass — not just whichever tools the DB recorded as currently enabled — so a stop always undoes every tool's interception, not just the ones the caller named
  - The per-tool DNS enable/disable state and cached sudo password are persisted via initDbHooks(getSettings, updateSettings) into 9router's own SQLite settings row (mitmRouterBaseUrl, dnsStatus) — not a user CLI config file
  - The alias sub-route's PUT requires DNS to already be enabled for that tool (403 otherwise) before it will accept model-alias rewrite mappings for that tool's intercepted traffic
  - Alias mappings are persisted twice: source of truth in SQLite (aliasRepo's mitmAlias kv scope, via getMitmAlias/setMitmAliasAll) AND mirrored into a JSON read-replica file (src/lib/mitmAliasCache.js) so the standalone MITM server process — which has no SQLite binding — can read it. That mirror write DOES use the atomic temp-file+rename pattern (writeAtomic), unlike every cli-tools config write covered by clitools.write-not-atomic
- **Errors:** `AUTH_ERROR` (start/stop/DNS-toggle attempted without admin (Windows) or without a valid sudo password when one is required — 403), `INVALID_REQUEST` (POST missing apiKey, PATCH missing tool/action, or alias PUT missing tool/mappings — 400), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (port 443 already in use by another process on start — 409 with portOwner)

### Each POST handler independently appends (or strips) a literal "/v1" suffix before writing baseUrl

- **id:** `clitools.baseurl-v1-suffix-normalization` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** Every write-capable cli-tools POST handler, before the baseUrl value is written into that tool's own config format
- **Input:** baseUrl string supplied by the dashboard (normally the 9router base URL the user is pointing the tool at)
- **Output:** baseUrl string with (or without) a trailing /v1, as that specific tool's config format expects
- **Rules:**
  - Q4 rule, reimplemented independently (not shared code) in at least 9 route files: `baseUrl.endsWith("/v1") ? baseUrl : baseUrl + "/v1"`. Because the check is an exact suffix match, re-running Apply on a baseUrl that already ends in /v1 is a no-op — nothing extra is appended. That is the direct answer to 'what breaks if a base URL already ends in /v1': nothing, the check is idempotent for the exact string
  - cline-settings does the INVERSE (`endsWith("/v1") ? baseUrl.slice(0, -3) : baseUrl`) because, per its own comment, 'Cline expects base WITHOUT /v1'
  - This is a client-config-generation concern only — separate from how 9router's own executor builds its OUTBOUND upstream URLs. That path (open-sse/executors/base.js, see routing.build-url in 05-routing-and-fallback.yaml) does a single-trailing-slash strip and appends an endpoint path with NO /v1 detection at all; the two normalisation rules exist for unrelated reasons and must not be conflated during parity design

### GET/POST/DELETE for ~/.claude/settings.json env vars plus the exa MCP toggle in ~/.claude.json

- **id:** `clitools.claude-settings-config` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard "Claude Code" card — GET on load, POST on Apply, DELETE on Reset
- **Input:** POST body { env: {ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, ...}, exaMcpEnabled, maxContextTokens }
- **Output:** GET: { installed, settings, has9Router, exaMcpEnabled, settingsPath }. POST/DELETE: { success, message }
- **Rules:**
  - checkClaudeInstalled tries `where`/`which claude` first, falls back to checking settings.json existence — either satisfies 'installed'
  - ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is normalised to end in exactly "/v1" before being written (endsWith check, append if missing) — see clitools.baseurl-v1-suffix-normalization for the shared rule and its edge case
  - env fields are merged into the existing settings.env object (spread), not replaced — unrelated existing env keys survive an Apply
  - CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS is set only when maxContextTokens is truthy; a falsy value (0, empty, 'Default') deletes the key so Claude Code falls back to the model's own context window
  - The exa MCP toggle is written to a DIFFERENT file, ~/.claude.json, under mcpServers.exa — because 'Claude Code CLI reads mcpServers from ~/.claude.json (NOT settings.json)' (source comment); the entry itself is reused verbatim from coworkPlugins.DEFAULT_PLUGINS' exa definition
  - DELETE removes a fixed RESET_ENV_KEYS list from settings.env (not the whole env object) and unconditionally strips the injected exa entry from ~/.claude.json, regardless of whether it toggled it on originally
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (POST body has no env object (or env is not an object) — 400), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (any fs read/write throws unexpectedly (not ENOENT) — 500)

### Split write across globalState.json (provider/model) and secrets.json (API key)

- **id:** `clitools.cline-settings-dual-file` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard "Cline" card — GET/POST/DELETE
- **Input:** POST body { baseUrl, apiKey, model }
- **Output:** { success, message, globalStatePath }
- **Rules:**
  - Detection (has9RouterConfig) requires BOTH actModeApiProvider/planModeApiProvider === 'openai' AND openAiBaseUrl containing localhost/127.0.0.1/'9router'
  - Applying sets both actMode and planMode provider to 'openai' and writes openAiBaseUrl/openAiModelId/planModeOpenAiModelId into globalState.json, then writes the plaintext API key into a SEPARATE file, secrets.json, as openAiApiKey — mirroring Cline's own on-disk split between non-secret state and secrets
  - DELETE only clears the 9Router-related fields (and flips the provider back to 'cline') when actModeApiProvider was 'openai' — if the user had switched Cline to a different provider in between, Reset leaves that provider untouched but still deletes secrets.openAiApiKey unconditionally
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (baseUrl, apiKey or model missing from POST body — 400), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (unexpected fs error on either file)

### CodeWhale and ForgeCode TOML configuration

- **id:** `clitools.codewhale-forge-toml` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** GET, POST, or DELETE on either tool's settings route
- **Input:** POST { baseUrl, apiKey?, model? }; DELETE has no body
- **Output:** GET installation/config status; POST/DELETE success or 400/500 error
- **Rules:**
  - Both detect an installed binary with where/which, then fall back to config-file existence. GET parses TOML and reports whether 9Router is configured.
  - POST requires baseUrl, appends /v1 if absent, merges an openai section into existing TOML, and writes the final file directly.
  - DELETE removes only the openai section; if no sections remain, it removes the config file.
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (POST JSON is invalid or baseUrl is missing), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (file or TOML operation fails outside tolerated read errors)

### TOML config.toml (model/provider) plus a static bearer header carrying the API key, separate auth.json cleanup

- **id:** `clitools.codex-settings-toml-split-secret` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard "Codex" card — GET/POST/DELETE
- **Input:** POST body { baseUrl, apiKey, model, subagentModel }
- **Output:** { success, message, configPath }
- **Rules:**
  - Uses the confbox library to parse/stringify TOML (unlike deepseek-tui's hand-rolled regex parser)
  - The API key is NOT written into config.toml's provider section as an api_key field — Codex's custom-provider auth.json mechanism is bypassed entirely by putting the key directly into a static `http_headers.Authorization: Bearer <key>` header on the provider entry, because (per comment) 'Custom providers ignore auth.json — the key must travel as a static header'. This means the API key is stored in PLAINTEXT inside config.toml itself, not in the more restrictively-named auth.json
  - agents.subagent (legacy key) is deleted and replaced by agents.default_subagent_model on every Apply
  - DELETE only removes the root model/model_provider fields if model_provider is currently exactly '9router' (so switching Codex to a different provider first prevents 9router's Reset from clobbering it), but ALWAYS deletes model_providers.9router and the subagent keys regardless
  - DELETE also strips OPENAI_API_KEY and auth_mode from auth.json (a file this integration never wrote to), deleting the whole file if it becomes empty
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (baseUrl, apiKey or model missing — 400), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (unexpected fs/TOML error)

### Array-based upsert into chatLanguageModels.json, and a missing install-detection step

- **id:** `clitools.copilot-settings-array-upsert` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard "Copilot" card — GET/POST/DELETE
- **Input:** POST body { baseUrl, apiKey, models[] }
- **Output:** { success, message, configPath }
- **Rules:**
  - Config is an array of provider entries (not a keyed object like every other tool); the 9Router entry is found/replaced/appended by name === '9Router'
  - vendor is hardcoded to 'azure' and each model entry is given a fixed toolCalling:true, vision:false, maxInputTokens:128000, maxOutputTokens:16000 regardless of the model's real capabilities
  - apiKey defaults to the literal string 'sk_9router' when the caller supplies none
  - URL is built as `${baseUrl}/chat/completions#models.ai.azure.com` — a different suffix convention than the /v1 rule used by every other tool (see clitools.baseurl-v1-suffix-normalization), because VS Code's Copilot Chat model picker keys entries by this azure-style URL fragment
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (baseUrl missing or models[] empty — 400), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (unexpected fs error)
- **AIGate required behavior:** Like every other cli-tools GET handler (claude, codex, cline, droid, kilo, etc.), Copilot's GET should reflect a real detection check — a `where`/`which` lookup or a marker-file probe — before reporting installed: true, so the dashboard only shows Copilot as available on a machine that actually has it.

### Registry fetch (with in-memory cache) and per-server tool-list probe (with SSRF guard), consumed by McpMarketplaceModal

- **id:** `clitools.cowork-mcp-marketplace-fetch` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** McpMarketplaceModal opening (registry fetch) and expanding a server row (tools probe)
- **Input:** registry: none (optional ?refresh=1); tools: POST { url }
- **Output:** registry: { cached, servers[], total }; tools: { tools[] } or { requiresAuth:true } or { error }
- **Rules:**
  - cowork-mcp-registry paginates Anthropic's public MCP registry (api.anthropic.com/mcp-registry/v0/servers) up to 20 pages of 500, filters to isDirectConnect entries only (excludes mcp.claude.com-mediated and api.anthropic.com/mcp entries, and any URL containing a template placeholder < or {), dedupes by url, and caches the result in a module-scope globalThis map for 1 hour unless ?refresh=1 is passed
  - cowork-mcp-tools probes an arbitrary caller-supplied MCP server URL with a 3-step handshake (initialize → notifications/initialized → tools/list), handling both a plain JSON response and an SSE-framed one (parsing `data:` lines), under an 8s AbortController timeout
  - A 401/403 from the probed server at either the initialize or tools/list step is reported back as { requiresAuth:true, tools:[] } rather than an error — this is what lets the modal show 'OAuth required — add now, discover tools later' instead of failing the add flow
  - SSRF guard (assertPublicUrl) is applied to the tools probe ONLY when the request is not local (isLocalRequest check) — the dashboard's own same-origin calls skip the guard entirely since the browser calling its own localhost server is treated as trusted
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (tools probe: url missing, not a string, or blocked by the SSRF guard for a non-local caller — 400), `TIMEOUT` (tools probe: any of the three HTTP calls exceeds 8s — reported as error:'timeout'), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (registry fetch fails outright (non-ok on the first page) — 500 with empty servers)

### Per-instance configLibrary/<uuid>.json write, deploymentMode bootstrap in the real Claude Desktop config, and managed MCP server assembly

- **id:** `clitools.cowork-settings-desktop-mcp` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard "Claude Desktop (Cowork)" card — GET/POST/DELETE
- **Input:** POST body { baseUrl, apiKey, models[], plugins[], localPlugins[], customPlugins[] }
- **Output:** { success, bootstrapped, message, configPath, skipApprovals, localMcp }
- **Rules:**
  - Claude Desktop's '3p' (third-party provider) mode stores its actual active config under an OS-specific 'Claude-3p' or 'Claude' configLibrary directory, keyed by a UUID (_meta.json's appliedId) — a NEW uuid is minted only if no _meta.json/appliedId is found anywhere on read OR write side
  - bootstrapDeploymentMode reads/writes the REAL Claude Desktop app config (claude_desktop_config.json under Library/Application Support/Claude or APPDATA/Claude) to flip deploymentMode to '3p' — this is a write to the actual first-party desktop app's own settings file, not just 9router's derived config
  - Every Apply also unconditionally applies a SECURITY_RELAX profile (coworkEgressAllowedHosts:['*'], all telemetry disabled, unsigned desktop extensions allowed, etc.) merged into the same config object — this is a broad, silent security-posture change bundled into what the UI presents only as 'Cowork settings applied'
  - managedMcpServers = DEFAULT_PLUGINS (remote exa/tavily, from coworkPlugins.js, built via buildManagedMcpServers) + local stdio bridge entries (one per name in localPlugins[], pointing at this app's own /api/mcp/<name>/sse — see mcp.stdio-sse-bridge) + custom URL-only entries supplied by the caller (e.g. from McpMarketplaceModal via cowork-mcp-marketplace-fetch) — three different sources merged into one array on every Apply
  - Local-bridge and custom entries get an x-9r-cli-token header injected (derived from getConsistentMachineId, cached module-scope) ONLY when their url starts with this app's own local /api/mcp/ prefix — remote plugins (exa/tavily) never get this header
  - writeSkipApprovals writes a SEPARATE config.json with operonSkipMcpApprovals set to true for every managed server name, so Claude Desktop auto-approves tool calls from all of them with no per-tool prompt
  - cleanup1pLegacy best-effort removes any of LOCAL_STDIO_PLUGINS' names from the FIRST-PARTY (1p) claude_desktop_config.json's mcpServers, in case an older 9router version wrote stdio entries there directly
  - DELETE does not remove the instance file or _meta.json; it overwrites the active configLibrary/<uuid>.json with an empty object {} — Cowork keeps pointing at the same (now-empty) instance
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (baseUrl/apiKey missing, or models[] resolves empty — 400), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (unexpected fs error on any of the four files touched)

### Crush, Pi, and Smelt JSON configuration

- **id:** `clitools.crush-pi-smelt-json` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** GET, POST, or DELETE on the respective settings route

  - Pi resolves ~/.pi/agent/models.json before ~/.pi/models.json and accepts a model descriptor list or a single default model.

### Both POST and DELETE replace the entire config.toml with a fixed template, discarding unrelated content

- **id:** `clitools.deepseek-tui-full-overwrite` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard "DeepSeek TUI" card — GET/POST/DELETE
- **Input:** POST body { baseUrl, apiKey, model }
- **Output:** { success, message, configPath }
- **Rules:**
  - GET uses a hand-rolled regex TOML parser (parseToml) rather than a real TOML library (contrast with codex-settings and jcode-settings, which use confbox) — it only understands flat `key = "value"` lines and `[section]` headers, storing dotted-section content under a single flat key like config['providers.openai'] rather than a nested object
  - POST does NOT read the existing config.toml at all before writing: build9RouterConfig() returns a brand-new fixed template string (`provider = "openai"\n[providers.openai]\n...`) that is written verbatim, replacing the entire file
  - DELETE writes the hardcoded DEFAULT_CONFIG string (`provider = "deepseek"\n`) verbatim, again replacing the entire file
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (baseUrl or model missing — 400), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (unexpected fs error)
- **AIGate required behavior:** Like every other tool's Apply/Reset in this set (codex, droid, opencode, openclaw, grok-build, hermes, jcode, kilo, cline, cowork all read-merge-write or perform a targeted key removal), DeepSeek TUI's POST should merge 9router's fields into whatever config.toml already contains, and DELETE should remove only what 9router added — preserving any other DeepSeek TUI settings the user configured.

### The one tool in the set with GET only — no config file is ever written

- **id:** `clitools.devin-settings-detect-only` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard "Devin" card — GET only (no POST/DELETE exported)
- **Input:** none
- **Output:** { installed, source, version, message } or { installed:false, message, installUrl }
- **Rules:**
  - Detection first tries PATH lookup (`where`/`which devin`), then falls back to a hardcoded list of known installer paths per OS (mirrors, per its own comment, the executor's resolveDevinBin discovery so dashboard status matches what the runtime actually spawns)
  - There is no config to write: the comment states the Devin binary handles its own auth via `devin auth login`, so this route only ever detects and reports — it is the only one of the 19 route files with no POST or DELETE export at all
- **Errors:** `INTERNAL_ERROR` (unexpected error during detection — 500)

### customModels array rebuild with reorder-to-front default selection

- **id:** `clitools.droid-settings-custommodels` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard "Droid" card — GET/POST/DELETE
- **Input:** POST body { baseUrl, apiKey, model | models[], activeModel }
- **Output:** { success, message, settingsPath }
- **Rules:**
  - Accepts either legacy single `model` (string) or `models` (array); normalises to modelsArray
  - Every Apply first strips ALL existing entries whose id starts with 'custom:9Router' before rebuilding — prevents unbounded duplicate accumulation across repeated Applies
  - activeModel selects which of the rebuilt entries is moved to index 0 (droid's 'default' convention appears to be array position); an explicit empty-string activeModel means 'no default', leaving index 0 as whichever model happened to be pushed first
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (baseUrl missing or no models resolved — 400), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (unexpected fs error)

### Surgical TOML section editing with a marker-comment mechanism to remember and restore the user's prior default/subagent config

- **id:** `clitools.grok-build-settings-restore-on-reset` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard "Grok Build" card — GET/POST/DELETE
- **Input:** POST body { baseUrl, apiKey, model, contextWindow, subagentModels }
- **Output:** { success, message, configPath, modelSlot: '9router' }
- **Rules:**
  - Delegates all TOML editing to src/lib/grokBuildConfig.js — a regex-based section reader/writer (not a general TOML library) that edits only `[model.9router]`, `[model.9router-<subagent-type>]` and the `default`/`subagents.models.<type>` keys, leaving all other TOML content untouched
  - Before overwriting models.default (or a subagent mapping) with 9router's slot, rememberPreviousDefault/rememberPreviousSubagent insert a `# 9router-prev-default = "..."` (or per-type) marker COMMENT recording what the value was beforehand — but only if no such marker already exists (idempotent across repeated Applies)
  - resetGrokBuildConfig restores the remembered previous default/subagent values from those markers (falling back to GROK_BUILTIN_DEFAULT = 'grok-build' if none was recorded) and removes the 9router model sections — this is the one tool in the set that round-trips the user's PRE-9router configuration on Reset rather than just deleting 9router's own additions
  - getCapabilitiesForModel (open-sse/providers/capabilities.js) supplies a default context_window when the caller doesn't specify one, tying this integration to the shared model-capability registry
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (baseUrl or model missing — 400), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (unexpected fs error)

### Regex-based YAML model-block upsert plus a separate .env file for the API key

- **id:** `clitools.hermes-settings-regex-block` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard "Hermes Agent" card — GET/POST/DELETE
- **Input:** POST body { baseUrl, apiKey, model }
- **Output:** { success, message, configPath }
- **Rules:**
  - config.yaml is edited with a hand-written regex (MODEL_BLOCK_RE) that matches the top-level `model:` block up to the next non-indented line and replaces it wholesale — everything else in the YAML file is left untouched as raw text (no YAML parser is used at all)
  - The written model block always references the key via `${OPENAI_API_KEY}` (a literal YAML env-var placeholder), while the actual secret is upserted into a SEPARATE .env file via a simple `KEY=value` regex line replace — apiKey is only written to .env when the caller supplies one; omitting it on a later Apply leaves the previous key in .env untouched
  - DELETE removes the model: block from config.yaml entirely (removeModelBlock) but does not touch .env — OPENAI_API_KEY is left in .env after a Reset
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (baseUrl or model missing — 400), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (unexpected fs error)

### confbox TOML provider entry plus a separate quoted-KEY=VALUE env file for the API key

- **id:** `clitools.jcode-settings-env-split` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard "jcode" card — GET/POST/DELETE
- **Input:** POST body { baseUrl, apiKey, models[] }
- **Output:** { success, message, configPath }
- **Rules:**
  - has9RouterConfig detects either an explicit providers['9router'] entry OR any provider whose base_url contains 'localhost:20128' — a looser heuristic than most other tools' name-only checks
  - config.toml gets a providers['9router'] entry with api_key_env: 'JCODE_9ROUTER_API_KEY' and env_file: 'provider-9router.env' pointing at where the actual key lives; the key never appears in config.toml itself
  - The env file path is derived from XDG_CONFIG_HOME (falling back to ~/.config), independent of the jcode config directory itself (~/.jcode) — two different base directories for the two files
  - default_model falls back to a hardcoded 'cc/claude-opus-4-7' if models[] is empty
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (baseUrl or apiKey missing — 400), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (any error thrown is passed through as error.message with a 500)

### auth.json write plus a best-effort, error-swallowed VS Code settings.json write

- **id:** `clitools.kilo-settings-dual-file` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard "Kilo Code" card — GET/POST/DELETE
- **Input:** POST body { baseUrl, apiKey, model }
- **Output:** { success, message, authPath }
- **Rules:**
  - Primary write is auth.json's 'openai-compatible' entry (type, apiKey, baseUrl, model)

### Oh My Pi YAML model discovery and optional auth database update

- **id:** `clitools.omp-yaml-and-auth-db` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** GET, POST, or DELETE /api/cli-tools/omp-settings
- **Input:** POST { baseUrl, apiKey? }; DELETE has no body
- **Output:** GET installation/has9Router status; POST/DELETE success or 400/500 error
- **Rules:**
  - GET checks the omp binary, agent.db, or models.yml, then looks for a 9router provider in YAML.
  - POST requires baseUrl, writes a 9router provider block under providers in models.yml with proxy discovery, then best-effort replaces the auth_credentials row if better-sqlite3 is available.
  - DELETE removes the 9router provider block from models.yml, deleting the file if only providers: remains; it does not remove auth_credentials from agent.db.

### Main openclaw.json plus one models.json per agent, written in a non-transactional fan-out

- **id:** `clitools.openclaw-settings-per-agent-fanout` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard "OpenClaw" card — GET/POST/DELETE
- **Input:** POST body { baseUrl, apiKey, model, agentModels: { [agentId]: modelId } }
- **Output:** { success, message, settingsPath }
- **Rules:**
  - agent.model may be stored by OpenClaw as either a plain string or { primary, fallbacks }; resolveAgentModel() normalises both forms to a string for internal `.startsWith()` checks, and the GET response coerces every agent's model field the same way before returning it
  - POST rebuilds agents.defaults.model.primary, the agents.defaults.models allowlist (all old '9router/*' keys dropped, fresh ones added for every unique model referenced across the default and all per-agent overrides), and updates each named agent's model field in agents.list
  - For every agent in agents.list that has an agentDir, a SEPARATE models.json file under that agent's own directory is written with that agent's resolved provider/model config — one extra fs.writeFile per agent, all fired via Promise.all, BEFORE the main openclaw.json write happens
  - DELETE performs targeted removal only (9router provider entry, 9router/* allowlist keys, agents.defaults.model.primary if it points at 9router) — preserves all unrelated openclaw settings, unlike clitools.deepseek-tui-full-overwrite
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (baseUrl or model missing — 400), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (unexpected fs error on the main file or any per-agent file)

### provider.models map merge, active-model selection, and an always-rewritten subagent entry

- **id:** `clitools.opencode-settings-provider-map` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard "OpenCode" card — GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE
- **Input:** POST body { baseUrl, apiKey, model | models[], activeModel, subagentModel }; PATCH { clearActiveModel }; DELETE ?model=<id>
- **Output:** { success, message, configPath }
- **Rules:**
  - provider['9router'].models is a map merged with existing entries (models not in the current request are preserved), unlike tools that fully rebuild their model list on each Apply
  - config.agent.explorer is unconditionally (re)written on every successful POST to point at effectiveSubagentModel (subagentModel if given, else the first requested model) — even if the caller only intended to change the base URL
  - PATCH supports a narrow clearActiveModel-only operation that blanks config.model without touching the provider/models map
  - DELETE supports removing a single model (?model=<id>) — if it was the active model, the first remaining model becomes active; if models becomes empty, the whole provider entry and config.model are removed. With no ?model, the whole 9router provider and agent.explorer subagent are removed
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (baseUrl missing or no models resolved on POST — 400), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (unexpected fs/JSON error on any of GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE)

### Every cli-tools write is a single non-atomic fs.writeFile with no on-disk backup

- **id:** `clitools.write-not-atomic` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** Any POST/DELETE/PATCH across all 13 write-capable cli-tools routes
- **Input:** Any tool-config write triggered by that tool's own POST/DELETE/PATCH handler
- **Output:** The write either lands intact or, on a mid-write failure, leaves the target file truncated/corrupted with no recovery path
- **Rules:**
  - Q2 answer: the write is NOT atomic. Every route (claude-settings, cline-settings, codex-settings, copilot-settings, cowork-settings, deepseek-tui-settings, droid-settings, grok-build-settings, hermes-settings, jcode-settings, kilo-settings, openclaw-settings, opencode-settings — including openclaw's per-agent models.json files and cowork's per-instance configLibrary/*.json) calls fs.writeFile(path, content) directly on the FINAL path. None use a temp-file-then-rename swap, and none write a recoverable .bak copy of the previous content
  - The codebase already has an atomic-write helper for this exact purpose elsewhere: src/lib/mitmAliasCache.js's writeAtomic() writes to '<file>.tmp' then fs.renameSync()s over the real file — that pattern is simply not used for any of the user's own CLI/IDE config files
- **Errors:** `INTERNAL_ERROR` (process dies, disk fills, or power is lost between fs.writeFile's buffer flush and the OS completing the write)
- **AIGate required behavior:** Given every one of these writes targets the user's own IDE/CLI configuration file (not 9router's own data), and one of the affected routes' own comment explicitly promises 'Backup old fields and write new settings', a crash mid-write should not be able to corrupt or truncate that file — either via a temp-file-then-rename swap (the exact pattern already implemented in this codebase at src/lib/mitmAliasCache.js:15-21 for 9router's own alias cache) or an actual on-disk backup copy.

## Combo / Vision Adapter

### augmentModelsWithCapacityAdapter prepends adapter models first — the file's own header comment says the opposite

- **id:** `capacity.augment-models-priority-prepend` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** routing.capacity-adapter-solo (single model) or routing.combo-dispatch (combo members) when none of the original models satisfy a required hard capability
- **Input:** models (original combo members, or the single requested model), requiredCapabilities Set, settings
- **Output:** [...pool, ...models] when augmentation applies, otherwise `models` returned unchanged
- **Rules:**
  - No-op (returns models unchanged) when there are no required hard capabilities, models is not a non-empty array, OR at least one original model already satisfies every required hard capability — reorderByCapabilities (combo.reorder-by-capabilities-tiers), not this function, handles floating an already-present capable member to the front in that case
  - When augmentation does apply: `pool` is built from getCapacityAdapterModels filtered to models not already in the list AND that satisfy the hard capabilities, then the function returns `[...pool, ...models]` — pool models come FIRST, original models follow as fallback
  - The module's own top-of-file comment (capacityAdapter.js line 5) describes the pool as being 'appended... behind whatever models were already going to be tried', with reorderByCapabilities supposedly floating a pool model to the front only as needed — this describes the OPPOSITE of what the code does. The function's own docstring immediately above it (line 88, 'Adapter models go FIRST (priority); the original models follow as fallback') correctly matches the implementation. The file header is stale relative to the code

### Per-capability adapter pool config (enabled/roundRobin/models) with legacy-array back-compat and empty-pool fallback

- **id:** `capacity.capability-pool-config` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** Any augmentModelsWithCapacityAdapter or getActiveAdapterStrategy call — i.e. every combo dispatch and every capacity-adapter-solo check
- **Input:** settings.capacityAdapter[cap] for cap in vision/pdf/audioInput/videoInput
- **Output:** {enabled, roundRobin, models} for that capability
- **Rules:**
  - normalizeCapEntry accepts two shapes: the legacy bare array [{model, enabled}] (treated as enabled:true, roundRobin:false, models mapped from entry.model||entry), or the current object shape {enabled, roundRobin, models}; anything else (undefined, wrong type) normalizes to fully disabled with an empty pool
  - Object-shape `enabled` defaults to true unless explicitly `false` (entry.enabled !== false) — an object with no 'enabled' key at all is treated as enabled
  - getCapacityAdapterConfig upgrades an enabled-but-empty-models pool to models:[DEFAULT_FALLBACK_MODEL] ('oc/mimo-v2.5-free') so turning the toggle on is never a silent no-op

### Flattened deduped adapter pool across all 4 capabilities, and active-strategy resolution

- **id:** `capacity.pool-models-and-strategy` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** augmentModelsWithCapacityAdapter needs the pool; routing.combo-dispatch needs the active strategy for a solo-adapter combo
- **Input:** settings.capacityAdapter (all 4 capability keys)
- **Output:** getCapacityAdapterModels -> one ordered, deduped model list; getActiveAdapterStrategy -> "fallback" | "round-robin"
- **Rules:**
  - getCapacityAdapterModels iterates CAPABILITY_KEYS in the fixed order [vision, pdf, audioInput, videoInput], including a capability's models only if that capability's pool is enabled; a model already seen from an earlier capability in that fixed order is skipped, so a model listed under both 'vision' and 'pdf' pools appears once, at its 'vision' position
  - getActiveAdapterStrategy scans the request's required HARD capabilities in whatever order detectRequiredCapabilities happened to add them to the Set, and returns the strategy ('round-robin' if enabled+roundRobin, else 'fallback') of the FIRST capability whose pool is both enabled and non-empty — it does not consider every required capability's strategy, only the first eligible one, defaulting to 'fallback' if none qualify

### stripHistoryForContext — the exact token-budget formula, what is always kept, and what is dropped first

- **id:** `capacity.strip-history-budget-formula` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** withCapacityAdapterStripping wraps a call to a model that is a member of the adapter pool, immediately before invoking handleSingleModel for it
- **Input:** body (any client format with messages/input/contents), contextWindow (from getCapabilitiesForModel(provider, model) for that specific adapter model)
- **Output:** The original body unchanged, or a new body whose array is [systemMsgs..., trimmedHead..., tail]
- **Rules:**
  - Budget formula: budgetChars = (contextWindow || 200000) * 0.8 * CHARS_PER_TOKEN(4) — 80% of the adapter model's token context window (falling back to 200000 tokens if contextWindow is falsy), converted to characters at a fixed 4 chars/token estimate (no real tokenizer); length is measured by blockLength — string length for plain text, or the sum of text-block lengths plus a flat 50-char placeholder per non-text block (e.g. an image) for array content
  - ALWAYS kept, unconditionally, regardless of budget: every system/developer-role message (systemMsgs), and the 'tail' — every message from the current user turn onward (the trailing run after the last assistant/model-role message) — which is exactly where the media that triggered the capacity-adapter switch lives
  - The middle ('older' = everything between the system messages and the tail) is handled in two passes. Pass 1 (unconditional, budget-independent): only the FIRST HEAD_KEEP=6 messages of `older` (headKept) are even candidates to survive — everything in `older` beyond the first 6 is dropped outright, before any length check runs
  - Pass 2 (only if systemMsgs+headKept(6)+tail still exceeds budgetChars): messages are popped off the END of headKept one at a time — i.e. the 6th kept message first, working backward toward the 1st — dropping the ones CLOSEST to the tail/middle first and preserving the very earliest instructions longest, until the total fits or headKept is empty
  - If nothing was actually dropped (head.length === older.length, meaning `older` already had <=6 messages), the ORIGINAL body object is returned unchanged, not a copy
  - Only messages/input/contents array shapes are recognized (checked in that order); a body using none of them is returned unmodified

### withCapacityAdapterStripping — per-call wrapper that strips history only for models actually drawn from the adapter pool

- **id:** `capacity.wrap-stripping-per-model` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** Every handleSingleModel invocation inside a capacity-adapter-augmented combo (produced by routing.capacity-adapter-solo, or a combo augmented via combo-dispatch)
- **Input:** the base handleSingleModel callback, adapterModels (the pool list that was prepended)
- **Output:** A wrapped callback with the identical (body, modelStr, ...rest) signature
- **Rules:**
  - Returns the original handleSingleModel completely UNCHANGED (not even wrapped) when adapterModels is empty — a pure passthrough when there is no adapter pool in play for this request
  - For a non-empty pool, the wrapper strips history via stripHistoryForContext only when modelStr is a member of adapterSet — the client's originally-requested model (or any other non-pool combo member) never has its history stripped by this wrapper, only the adapter-added fallback candidates do
  - contextWindow for the strip budget is looked up fresh per call via getCapabilitiesForModel(provider, model) for that specific modelStr, so each adapter-pool model can be trimmed to a different budget

### /api/combos CRUD routes — name validation, a duplicate pre-check race, and reuse outside the chat lane

- **id:** `combo.api-crud` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** GET/POST /api/combos; GET/PUT/DELETE /api/combos/[id]
- **Input:** {name, models, kind} body for POST/PUT; id path param for the [id] routes
- **Output:** Combo JSON on success, or 400 (bad name format / missing name / duplicate name), 404 (not found), 500 (unhandled)
- **Rules:**
  - Name format is restricted to [a-zA-Z0-9_.-]+ (VALID_NAME_REGEX, duplicated verbatim in both route files) — combo lookups elsewhere (getComboModels, getComboModelsFromData) do not re-validate this charset, they trust whatever string is already stored
  - POST's duplicate check (getComboByName) is a separate SELECT from the later INSERT: under a race, two POSTs with the same name can both pass the pre-check; the DB's UNIQUE constraint (combo.storage-shape) then rejects the second INSERT, which createCombo does not special-case, so that request's outer try/catch returns the generic 500 'Failed to create combo' instead of the friendlier 400 'Combo name already exists'
  - PUT's duplicate check excludes the current id (existing.id !== id), so renaming a combo to its own current name is allowed and is not treated as a collision
  - Combos are consumed not only by the chat lane (routing.combo-dispatch) but also by src/sse/handlers/fetch.js and search.js via getComboModelsFromData — this CRUD surface is shared across modalities, not chat-only
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (POST/PUT name fails VALID_NAME_REGEX, POST is missing name, or POST/PUT name collides with an existing combo per the pre-check), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (any thrown error in the route's try/catch, including a UNIQUE-constraint violation the pre-check race missed)

### detectRequiredCapabilities scans only the trailing user turn for modality requirements

- **id:** `combo.detect-required-capabilities` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** Every combo dispatch (handleComboChat's autoSwitch) and every capacity-adapter-solo check — called once per incoming request
- **Input:** body.messages / body.input / body.contents, whichever array the client's format uses
- **Output:** A Set drawn from {vision, pdf, audioInput, videoInput} ("search" is recognized in the code's design but not currently emitted)
- **Rules:**
  - trailingUserItems walks backward from the end of the array until it hits an assistant/model-role item, then returns everything after that boundary — i.e. only the messages contributed since the model's last reply
  - Recognizes modality hints across many client shapes within that trailing run: OpenAI/Claude/Gemini content blocks (image_url/image/input_image, input_audio/audio_url/audio, input_video/video_url/video, file/document/input_file with mime sniffing), Ollama/Hermes m.images array, Vercel AI SDK/Hermes attachments, direct message-level image_url/audio_url fields, Gemini inlineData/fileData mimeType, and string content containing an embedded data: URI
  - A generic file/document block with no recoverable mime defaults to 'pdf' (mime sniffing is tried first via addByMime; the pdf default only fires when no mime could be determined)
  - 'search' capability detection is explicitly disabled — a code comment marks it 'temporarily disabled in auto-switch (feature not wired yet)'

### Fusion fan-out has no explicit concurrency cap independent of panel size

- **id:** `combo.fusion-panel-concurrency-unbounded` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** Every fusion request with more than one panel member
- **Input:** panel array — length is whatever an admin configured as the combo's members
- **Output:** One outbound handleSingleModel call per panel member, all started in the same synchronous Array.map, i.e. all in parallel
- **Rules:**
  - handleFusionChat builds `calls` via `panel.map((m) => withTimeout(handleSingleModel(panelBody, m, true), cfg.panelHardTimeoutMs))` — every panel member's call is invoked immediately and unconditionally; there is no batching, queueing, or semaphore anywhere in the fan-out
  - The only limit on simultaneous in-flight upstream calls for one fusion request is how many models the combo lists — there is no server-side concurrency cap independent of combo size
- **Note:** 9router's mechanism here is an accident of its stack. Behavior required, mechanism not.

### Judge model synthesizes one final answer from anonymized panel responses

- **id:** `combo.judge-prompt-synthesis` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** Fusion panel produced 2 or more usable answers
- **Input:** answers=[{model,text}] in panel order, judgeModel override (comboStrategies[name].judgeModel), the ORIGINAL body
- **Output:** handleSingleModel(judgeBody, judge) — an ordinary single-model call, so the judge's answer streams/uses tools per the client's original request
- **Rules:**
  - buildJudgePrompt labels each answer '[Source N]' in panel order — the judge is never told which underlying model produced which answer, to avoid brand-reputation bias skewing its analysis
  - The judge is instructed to internally analyze consensus / contradictions / partial coverage / unique insights / blind spots, THEN write one answer — per the design comment, it does not merge or vote; most of fusion's quality lift is attributed to this synthesis step
  - judgeModel falls back to panel[0] (the first CONFIGURED panel member, not the fastest responder or the actual judge answerer) whenever comboStrategies[name].judgeModel is unset or blank after trim
  - appendUserTurn appends the judge prompt as a new trailing user turn onto the ORIGINAL body (not panelBody) — preserving the client's original conversation, system prompt, tools and stream flag for the judge call; it branches on messages/input/contents, or synthesizes a fresh single-message array if the body has none of those three
- **Streaming:** yes

### "Fallback" strategy — sequential try-until-success across combo members

- **id:** `combo.mode-fallback` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** A combo dispatch (routing.combo-dispatch) resolves to comboStrategy "fallback" (the default) or any non-"round-robin"/"fusion" value
- **Input:** rotatedModels (post rotation + capability auto-switch), body, handleSingleModel callback
- **Output:** The first successful (2xx) member Response, or an aggregate error/503 Response after every member is exhausted
- **Rules:**
  - handleComboChat tries rotatedModels[0], [1], ... in order; it moves to the next model when handleSingleModel throws, OR when the non-2xx result's checkFallbackError classification says shouldFallback:true
  - checkFallbackError's shouldFallback:false path (per fallback.error-classification: noAuth connections, or pre-dispatch validation errors) returns that failing Response to the client immediately — the remaining combo members are never tried
  - A 502/503/504 whose classifier cooldownMs is > 0 and <= 5000 ms is awaited in-process (await new Promise(setTimeout)) before moving to the next model, giving a briefly-overloaded member one grace window; longer cooldowns are not waited on before falling through
  - When every member fails: the returned status is the last member's status (or 503 if none set one), UNLESS the last error text contains 'no credentials' (case-insensitive), which forces status 503 regardless of what the last member actually returned
  - retryAfter in the final aggregate error is the earliest of any member's parsed retryAfter across the whole loop, not just the last member's
- **Streaming:** yes
- **Errors:** `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (handleSingleModel throws, or returns a non-2xx result the classifier says to fall back from, for every model in rotatedModels), `INVALID_REQUEST` (the first attempted member's classifier returns shouldFallback:false (e.g. a pre-dispatch validation error) — returned to the client immediately without trying later members)

### Fusion panel body shaping and graceful degradation by number of surviving answers

- **id:** `combo.mode-fusion-degrade` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** handleFusionChat invoked for a fusion-strategy combo
- **Input:** body (client format), panel models
- **Output:** 400 (no models), a direct handleSingleModel passthrough (1 configured model, or exactly 1 surviving answer), 503 (0 surviving answers), or a judge-synthesized Response (>=2 surviving answers)
- **Rules:**
  - panel.length===0 -> 400 'Fusion combo has no models' before any network call is made
  - panel.length===1 -> handleSingleModel(body, panel[0]) is called directly with the ORIGINAL body: no flattening, no forced non-streaming, no fan-out — a true single-model passthrough, not a 1-member fusion round
  - For panel.length>1: tools/tool_choice/stream_options are stripped and stream is forced false for every panel call; messages/input arrays go through flattenToolHistory first (panelBody)
  - answers.length===0 (every panel call failed, timed out, threw, or returned unparseable/empty content) -> 503 'All fusion panel models failed'
  - answers.length===1 -> handleSingleModel(body, thatModel) is invoked AGAIN with the ORIGINAL body (streaming/tools intact), rather than returning the already-fetched non-streaming panel Response — the sole surviving model answers the prompt a second time so the client gets its real streaming/tool behavior
  - answers.length>=2 -> judge synthesis (combo.judge-prompt-synthesis)
- **Streaming:** yes
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (fusion combo configured with zero models), `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (every panel member fails, times out, throws, or returns unparseable/empty content)

### "Fusion" strategy — panel completion rule (minPanel quorum, straggler grace, hard timeout)

- **id:** `combo.mode-fusion-panel-completion` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** comboStrategy resolves to "fusion" and models.length > 1 (single-model fusion short-circuits — see combo.mode-fusion-degrade)
- **Input:** panel model list, body, cfg = FUSION_DEFAULTS merged with comboStrategies[name].fusionTuning
- **Output:** A sparse `out` array from collectPanel — each slot is a Response, {__timeout:true}, {__error}, or left undefined (never settled in time)
- **Rules:**
  - minPanel is clamped to between 2 and panel.length via Math.min(Math.max(2, cfg.minPanel), panel.length) — a configured minPanel of 0 or 1 is silently raised to 2 (or to panel.length if the panel itself has only 2 members)
  - The panel is considered complete at the FIRST of: (a) every call has settled, (b) at least minPanel calls have succeeded (ok>=minPanel) AND the stragglerGraceMs grace timer — started the instant quorum is first reached — has elapsed, or (c) panelHardTimeoutMs elapses from panel start, regardless of how many succeeded
  - Each panel call is independently wrapped in withTimeout(call, panelHardTimeoutMs) as well, so an individual call can resolve to {__timeout:true} using the same panelHardTimeoutMs constant that also bounds collectPanel's own hard timer
  - Only one grace timer is ever started (guarded by `!graceTimer`) since `ok` only increases monotonically
  - A call that resolves after finish() has already fired is not observable to the fusion caller (collectPanel's promise resolves exactly once) — but the underlying handleSingleModel call itself is not aborted, it keeps running to completion unused

### "Round-robin" strategy — sticky rotation of the starting member across requests

- **id:** `combo.mode-round-robin` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** comboStrategy resolves to exactly "round-robin" (per-combo comboStrategies[name].fallbackStrategy, else global settings.comboStrategy) and models.length > 1
- **Input:** models array, comboName (rotation key), stickyLimit (settings.comboStickyRoundRobinLimit, default 1)
- **Output:** rotatedModels — same members, rotated so the current rotation index is first; handleComboChat then falls through them exactly like the fallback strategy
- **Rules:**
  - getRotatedModels no-ops (returns models unchanged) when models.length<=1 or strategy isn't exactly 'round-robin' — any other strategy string is treated as plain fallback ordering
  - Rotation state per combo name is {index, consecutiveUseCount}; normalizeStickyLimit parses stickyLimit and falls back to 1 for any non-finite or non-positive input
  - consecutiveUseCount counts requests served at the CURRENT index; once it reaches normalizedStickyLimit, the index advances (mod models.length) and the counter resets to 0 for the next request — otherwise the counter increments and the index holds
  - Every request still tries the FULL member list on failure: round-robin only changes which member is tried first (rotateModelsFromIndex rotates the whole array), it never removes a member from the fallback chain
  - Legacy state shape: an existing Map value that is a bare number (older format) is treated as {index: thatNumber, consecutiveUseCount: 0}
  - The read-modify-write of the Map entry is synchronous (no await inside getRotatedModels), so two requests for the same combo processed back-to-back on Node's single event-loop thread cannot interleave mid-update — each call completes atomically relative to the others
- **Streaming:** yes

### reorderByCapabilities — 3-tier stable sort of combo/pool members by capability fit

- **id:** `combo.reorder-by-capabilities-tiers` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** handleComboChat's autoSwitch (default true, always true from current chat.js call sites) with a non-empty required Set, run after rotation and before the fallback loop
- **Input:** rotatedModels, required Set (hard = vision/pdf/audioInput/videoInput; soft = any other capability, currently unreachable — see edgeCases)
- **Output:** The same models, stably reordered into 3 tiers; no member is ever dropped
- **Rules:**
  - Tier 0: satisfies every required HARD capability AND every required SOFT capability
  - Tier 1: satisfies every required hard capability but not all required soft capabilities
  - Tier 2: fails at least one required hard capability — pushed to the back but never removed from the list
  - No-op short-circuits when required is empty/absent, models is not an array, or models.length<=1
  - The sort is stable via an explicit index tiebreaker (a.i-b.i in addition to a.t-b.t) — members within the same tier keep their pre-sort relative order, so a round-robin rotation's ordering survives a capability reorder on top of it

### comboRotationState Map — ownership, every reset trigger, and non-durability across restart

- **id:** `combo.rotation-state-lifecycle` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** Any of: a settings PATCH touching comboStrategy/comboStickyRoundRobinLimit/comboStrategies (settings.combo-rotation-reset); a combo PUT (any field, not just a rename); a combo DELETE
- **Input:** comboName, or none for a full clear
- **Output:** One Map entry removed, or the whole Map cleared
- **Rules:**
  - comboRotationState is a module-level `const comboRotationState = new Map()` inside open-sse/services/combo.js — process memory only, never written to the DB
  - resetComboRotation(comboName) deletes just that key; resetComboRotation() with no argument clears every combo's rotation state at once (used by the settings-PATCH path, settings.combo-rotation-reset)
  - PUT /api/combos/[id] calls resetComboRotation(prev.name) unconditionally after ANY successful update — even one that only changes the models array, not the name — and additionally calls resetComboRotation(combo.name) when the name actually changed, so a rename resets both the old and new name's state
  - DELETE /api/combos/[id] calls resetComboRotation(prev.name) after the row is removed, so a later combo re-created with the same name always starts rotation fresh
  - Not durable: a process restart (deploy, crash, Next.js module re-evaluation) wipes the Map entirely with no reload-from-DB step — every combo's round-robin sequence silently restarts at index 0 on the next boot

### Preview and create missing Cursor or Claude combo aliases

- **id:** `combo.source-presets` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** GET or POST /api/combos/presets with source cursor or claude
- **Input:** GET query source; POST JSON { source }
- **Output:** GET { source, items, toCreate, toSkip }; POST { source, created, skipped, createdCount, skippedCount }
- **Rules:**
  - Only cursor and claude are accepted sources. GET previews and does not write; POST creates each missing combo sequentially and skips names already present.
  - Cursor presets prefer live models resolved from the first active cursor connection; if that lookup fails or has no models, static cu registry models are used. Claude presets use static cc registry models plus configured Claude Code aliases.
  - Each preset name is the client-native model ID, while its member is the prefixed provider model; only names matching letters, numbers, underscore, period, or hyphen are included.
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (source is missing or not cursor/claude; returns 400), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (preset resolution or createCombo throws; returns 500)

### Combo persistence shape — id / unique name / kind / models(JSON) / timestamps

- **id:** `combo.storage-shape` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** Any combosRepo call (getCombos, getComboById, getComboByName, createCombo, updateCombo, deleteCombo)
- **Input:** {name, models, kind} for create/update; id or name for lookups
- **Output:** A combo row with `models` parsed back from JSON into a real array
- **Rules:**
  - combos.name carries a DB-level UNIQUE NOT NULL constraint (schema.js) — this is the actual backstop against duplicate names, not just the API layer's getComboByName pre-check (see combo.api-crud)
  - models is stored as a JSON TEXT column; parseJson(row.models, []) defaults to an empty array on parse failure or a null/missing cell, so a corrupted models value degrades to 'no members' rather than throwing on read
  - kind is stored and returned by every read path but is not consumed anywhere in the combo dispatch/fallback/fusion logic traced in this file — it is metadata with no traced runtime effect on request routing
  - updateCombo runs inside a single db.transaction: it re-reads the current row, merges the incoming `data` on top of it (untouched fields survive a partial PUT body), and writes the merged result — two concurrent PUTs to the same id serialize at the DB transaction boundary rather than lost-update racing in application code

### flattenToolHistory converts tool_use/tool_result/tool_calls turns to prose before panel calls

- **id:** `combo.tool-history-flatten` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** A fusion panel call (panel.length>1) whose panelBody has an array messages or input field
