- **Input:** messages/input array in OpenAI tool-role, Claude tool_use/tool_result content-block, or assistant.tool_calls shapes
- **Output:** A same-length array with every tool-bearing turn rewritten as plain assistant text
- **Rules:**
  - A role 'tool' or 'function' message becomes {role:'assistant', content:'[Tool result: <extracted text>]'}; extractTextContent's fallback to String(content) means even a non-text tool result still produces some text rather than an empty string
  - An assistant message with a tool_calls array has that array stripped entirely (the rest of the message is spread without it) and gets a '[Called tools: name1, name2]' suffix appended to its text content
  - Claude-style content-block arrays containing type:'tool_use' or type:'tool_result' blocks are rebuilt into one string: all text blocks joined first, then one combined '[Called tools: ...]' line, then one combined '[Tool result: ...]' line — this discards the original interleaved block ordering
  - A message with neither shape (plain text, or an array with no tool_use/tool_result blocks) passes through completely unchanged

## Console Log

### Batched SSE flush timer and log line formatting (ANSI strip, arg serialization)

- **id:** `console.batched-flush-and-formatting` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** Each console.* call while capture is patched; a debounced flush fires at most every 100ms or immediately once 50 pending lines accumulate
- **Input:** console.*(...args) call arguments (strings, Errors, objects)
- **Output:** A formatted, ANSI-stripped string line pushed to state.logs and state.pendingLines, eventually emitted as a 'lines' event on the shared EventEmitter for /console-logs/stream subscribers
- **Rules:**
  - formatArg() strips ANSI escape codes (terminal color codes) from strings, Error stacks/messages, and JSON-stringified objects alike (src/lib/consoleLogBuffer.js) so the dashboard playground never renders raw \x1b[...m sequences
  - scheduleFlush() debounces at FLUSH_INTERVAL_MS=100ms via setTimeout, but appendLine() bypasses the debounce and flushes immediately once pendingLines reaches MAX_BATCH_LINES=50 in the same call, clearing any pending timer first — a burst of 50+ log lines in one microtask flushes as one large 'lines' batch instead of waiting out the 100ms window
  - The flush timer is unref()'d (scheduleFlush) so a pending flush never keeps the Node process alive on its own — an intentional 'this is debug tooling, not a durability guarantee' choice
- **Streaming:** yes

### Why the ring buffer lives on global._* and the hot-reload guard that protects it

- **id:** `console.global-state-hot-reload-guard` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** Module (re-)evaluation of src/lib/consoleLogBuffer.js — normally once per process, but can happen more than once under Next.js dev-mode hot module reload / Turbopack fast refresh
- **Input:** none
- **Output:** A single shared state object (logs, emitter, patched flag) surviving across module re-evaluations
- **Rules:**
  - state is stored on global._consoleLogBufferState specifically because Next.js (especially dev-mode HMR/Turbopack) can re-evaluate a module's top-level code more than once per OS process — a plain module-scope `const state = {...}` would silently reset to a fresh empty buffer/emitter on every reload, dropping all buffered logs and detaching every already-open SSE subscriber from the old emitter instance
  - The guard is two-layered: the whole state object is created only `if (!global._consoleLogBufferState)`, and a second, narrower guard re-creates just `state.emitter` if a stale global survived a reload but somehow lost its EventEmitter — the inline comment 'handles hot reload with stale global' makes the intent explicit
  - This is a framework artifact (Next.js module re-evaluation semantics), not a business requirement — AIGate does not need to reproduce the global._* mechanism itself, only the underlying requirement it protects: exactly one console-log ring buffer + emitter for the process lifetime
- **Note:** 9router's mechanism here is an accident of its stack. Behavior required, mechanism not.

### Ring buffer capacity enforcement and overflow behavior

- **id:** `console.ring-buffer-capacity` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** Any console.log/info/warn/error/debug call anywhere in the Next.js process once initConsoleLogCapture() has patched the console object (triggered by importing api/translator/console-logs or console-logs/stream — see translator.playground-console-logs)
- **Input:** Arbitrary console.*(...args) call from anywhere in the process
- **Output:** Line appended to the in-memory logs array; oldest lines evicted once CONSOLE_LOG_CONFIG.maxLines (200) is exceeded
- **Rules:**
  - The cap is enforced only in appendLine() on the server (src/lib/consoleLogBuffer.js): every push checks state.logs.length > maxLines and, if so, replaces the array with logs.slice(-maxLines) — a hard 200-line ring, not a rolling window with a separate write cursor
  - Overflow is a silent drop: slice(-maxLines) simply discards the oldest lines with no counter, flag, or 'N lines truncated' marker surfaced to callers of getConsoleLogs() or to /api/translator/console-logs' GET response
  - There is no client-side cap — the dashboard playground renders whatever the server hands it (buffered GET array or streamed SSE lines); nothing tells the client what was dropped, so a long-lived tab that has accumulated lines across multiple 'lines'/'line' SSE events could display more than 200 lines until it re-syncs via a fresh 'init' replay

### Console-log routes live under /api/translator/ instead of a dedicated /api/console-log path

- **id:** `console.route-path-naming-accident` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** Any client (dashboard translator playground) calling GET/DELETE /api/translator/console-logs or GET /api/translator/console-logs/stream
- **Input:** none
- **Output:** Same buffered-log / SSE-stream responses already documented under translator.playground-console-logs — this entry records the path/placement choice, not new request/response behavior
- **Rules:**
  - translator.playground-console-logs (docs/discovery/feature-matrix/11-translation-i18n.yaml) already traces the full request/response/SSE behavior of these two routes end to end — this entry does not re-derive it, only records why the path is /api/translator/console-logs and not something like /api/console-log or /api/system/logs
  - Nothing in the route handlers or in consoleLogBuffer.js is translator-specific: initConsoleLogCapture() patches the process-wide console object and captures every console.* call in the entire Next.js process, not just calls made during a translation request — the capability is a general-purpose debug console viewer that happens to have been built for, and nested under, the translator playground UI
  - The naming/placement is a historical/organizational accident (the feature shipped as a debugging aid for the translator playground page and inherited that page's route prefix), not a deliberate API design choice — record this so AIGate does not copy the /api/translator/console-logs path for what is really a general process-console-log capability; if the capability is kept at all, a fresh AIGate design should place it under its own diagnostics/tooling path
- **Streaming:** yes
- **Note:** 9router's mechanism here is an accident of its stack. Behavior required, mechanism not.

## Endpoint & API Key

### Permanently remove a key (DELETE /api/keys/[id])

- **id:** `apikey.delete-key` · **module:** `apikeys`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard delete action on a key row
- **Input:** id path param
- **Output:** 200 { message } or 404 if nothing was deleted
- **Rules:**
  - Deletion is immediate and permanent — no soft-delete, no grace period; any in-flight request already validated against this key is unaffected (validation is per-request, not per-connection)
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (id does not correspond to an existing key (res.changes === 0)), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (DB DELETE throws)

### Create a new API key (POST /api/keys)

- **id:** `apikey.generate-key` · **module:** `apikeys`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard/API client calls POST /api/keys with a name
- **Input:** { name: string }
- **Output:** 201 { key, name, id, machineId } — full key returned once, in plaintext
- **Rules:**
  - machineId is never taken from the request body — the server always calls getConsistentMachineId() itself
  - Key format is sk-{machineId}-{keyId}-{crc8}: a random 6-char keyId, and an 8-char HMAC-SHA256(machineId+keyId) truncated as a checksum, keyed by API_KEY_SECRET (default 'endpoint-proxy-api-key-secret' if unset)
  - New key defaults isActive: true
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (name is missing from the request body), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (DB insert throws)

### Legacy sk-{random8} keys and the never-invoked CRC/format validation

- **id:** `apikey.legacy-format-unenforced` · **module:** `apikeys`
- **Trigger:** A request bearing a pre-machineId-era key, or any hand-crafted string
- **Input:** sk-{random8} (2 dash-separated parts) or any other string
- **Output:** Accepted iff the exact string exists as an active row in apiKeys; format is never inspected
- **Rules:**
  - parseApiKey() recognizes two shapes (4-part new format with CRC check, 2-part legacy format with no CRC) and isNewFormatKey/verifyApiKeyCrc build on it, but grepping the whole src tree shows none of the three is called from anywhere except inside apiKey.js itself — apiKeysRepo.createApiKey calls generateApiKeyWithMachine (write path only), and validateApiKey (read/auth path) never imports apiKey.js at all
  - Legacy sk-{random8} keys are therefore accepted for as long as their row remains in the apiKeys table with isActive true — there is no migration, expiry, or forced-rotation step
- **Errors:** `AUTH_ERROR` (a malformed/tampered key does not match any DB row)
- **AIGate required behavior:** Given generateCrc/parseApiKey/verifyApiKeyCrc exist specifically to bind a key to a machineId and detect tampering, the request-time auth path (validateApiKey / isValidApiKey) calls verifyApiKeyCrc (or parseApiKey) to reject a key whose embedded CRC doesn't match its machineId+keyId before or in addition to the DB lookup

### List all API keys (GET /api/keys)

- **id:** `apikey.list-keys` · **module:** `apikeys`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard loads the API keys page
- **Input:** none
- **Output:** 200 { keys: [{ id, key, name, machineId, isActive, createdAt }, ...] } ordered by createdAt ASC
- **Rules:**
  - The full plaintext key is returned in the list response — there is no masking of previously-issued keys
- **Errors:** `INTERNAL_ERROR` (DB query throws)
- **AIGate required behavior:** A key-management list endpoint masks or omits the secret value after initial issuance (standard practice, and consistent with GET /api/settings stripping password/oidcClientSecret)

### Toggle a key's isActive flag (PUT /api/keys/[id])

- **id:** `apikey.update-key-status` · **module:** `apikeys`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard revoke/reactivate action on a key row
- **Input:** { isActive: boolean }
- **Output:** 200 { key: <updated row> } or 404 if id not found
- **Rules:**
  - Only isActive is accepted from the body — name/key/machineId cannot be changed through this route even though updateApiKey would happily merge them
  - isActive === undefined is a no-op for that field (explicit undefined check, not truthiness), so isActive: false is correctly applied
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (id does not correspond to an existing key), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (DB transaction throws)

### Validate an inbound key string against stored keys

- **id:** `apikey.validate-lookup` · **module:** `apikeys`
- **Trigger:** Every /v1 request while settings.requireApiKey is true (via isValidApiKey)
- **Input:** Raw key string extracted from the request
- **Output:** true if a row exists with that exact key AND isActive; false otherwise
- **Rules:**
  - validateApiKey does a single SQL lookup: SELECT isActive FROM apiKeys WHERE key = ? — the comparison is a plain SQL '=' string equality done by the DB engine, not a constant-time comparison in application code
  - An inactive key (isActive false/0) is rejected even though the row matched — the query fetches isActive and the caller re-checks it explicitly rather than filtering isActive in the WHERE clause
- **Errors:** `AUTH_ERROR` (no row matches the key string), `AUTH_ERROR` (row matches but isActive is false/0)

### Gate chat requests behind settings.requireApiKey

- **id:** `endpoint.enforce-require-api-key` · **module:** `apikeys`
- **Trigger:** Any POST that reaches handleChat, after body/model parsing but before combo/account resolution
- **Input:** Parsed request body, request headers, current settings
- **Output:** 401 with 'Missing API key' or 'Invalid API key' body, or falls through to continue processing the chat request
- **Rules:**
  - The gate is skipped entirely when settings.requireApiKey is false — no key is required, no key is even logged as an error (only a debug 'local mode' line)
  - When requireApiKey is true: missing key → 401 before any DB lookup; present-but-invalid key → 401 after one DB lookup via isValidApiKey
  - The check happens after JSON body parsing and model-marker stripping but before model-existence, combo, or bypass-request checks — an unauthenticated caller cannot trigger those heavier code paths
- **Errors:** `AUTH_ERROR` (requireApiKey is true and no key was supplied), `AUTH_ERROR` (requireApiKey is true and isValidApiKey(key) resolves false)

### Extract the inbound API key from request headers

- **id:** `endpoint.extract-header-order` · **module:** `apikeys`
- **Trigger:** Every call into handleChat (and any other handler that imports extractApiKey)
- **Input:** Authorization header and/or x-api-key header
- **Output:** The bearer token string, the x-api-key string, or null
- **Rules:**
  - Authorization: Bearer <key> is checked first; only if absent (or not prefixed 'Bearer ') does it fall back to the Anthropic-style x-api-key header
  - If neither header is present, extractApiKey returns null and does not throw

### URL rewrite lanes that expose the API-key-gated router under multiple client-compatible paths

- **id:** `endpoint.rewrite-lanes` · **module:** `apikeys`
- **Trigger:** Any inbound HTTP request to one of the five rewritten path prefixes
- **Input:** Request path: /v1/*, /v1/v1/* (double-prefixing clients), /v1beta/* (Gemini-native), /codex/* and /responses (OpenAI Responses-shaped clients)
- **Output:** Internally rewritten to /api/v1/*, /api/v1beta/*, or /api/v1/responses before Next.js route matching — all funnel through the same requireApiKey gate in their respective handlers
- **Rules:**
  - AIGate must accept all five client-compatible lanes: /v1/* (standard), /v1/v1/* (clients that double-prefix), /v1beta/* (Gemini-native clients), and /codex/* plus the bare /responses path (OpenAI Responses-API-shaped clients) — each is a real, distinct client-compatibility requirement, not incidental
  - /codex/* and the bare /responses path both collapse onto the single /api/v1/responses handler regardless of the trailing path segments — /codex/:path* discards :path*, so any suffix a Codex-shaped client appends is intentionally dropped rather than forwarded
  - /v1beta and /v1 both have a path-less exact-match rule in addition to the /:path* rule, so a request to exactly '/v1' or '/v1beta' (no trailing slash/segment) still reaches its handler — the bare-path case is a deliberate, separate rule, not a fallthrough

### Derive the stable per-install machineId embedded in new API keys

- **id:** `identity.machine-id-derivation` · **module:** `identity`
- **Trigger:** Any call to getConsistentMachineId — from POST /api/keys (key generation) or CLI auth
- **Input:** Optional salt string; defaults to process.env.MACHINE_ID_SALT or the literal 'endpoint-proxy-salt'
- **Output:** 16-char lowercase hex string, stable across process restarts
- **Rules:**
  - Raw machine id is read from a persisted file (DATA_DIR/machine-id) first; only falls back to node-machine-id, then crypto.randomUUID(), if the file is missing or unreadable
  - The raw id is written back to disk (mode 0o600) the first time it is computed, so it survives node-machine-id giving inconsistent values across runtimes
  - A second secret (DATA_DIR/auth/cli-secret) is mixed in only when the caller passes the special CLI_AUTH_SALT ('9r-cli-auth'), producing a different, unguessable hash for CLI-to-server auth than for API-key machineId embedding
- **Errors:** `INTERNAL_ERROR` (both the machine-id file and node-machine-id fail (rare))

### POST /api/auth/login password check with progressive per-client lockout

- **id:** `identity.password-login-lockout` · **module:** `identity`
- **Trigger:** POST /api/auth/login with { password }
- **Input:** JSON body { password }, the client's bucket key from getClientIp(), the stored bcrypt hash (or INITIAL_PASSWORD/'123456' when none is stored)
- **Output:** 200 { success: true } plus the auth_token cookie; 401 with remainingBeforeLock; or 429 with Retry-After while locked
- **Rules:**
  - A locked bucket is refused with 429 and a Retry-After header before the password is even compared
  - Every failed comparison counts against the bucket; the 5th consecutive failure locks it, for 30s, then 2m, 10m, and 30m on each later lock (the last step repeats)
  - The failure count resets 1h after the last failure when the bucket is not locked, and immediately on a successful login
  - A failed attempt that does not yet lock answers 401 and tells the client how many attempts remain before lockout
  - The bucket key is a proxy-stamped real IP only when the custom server proves it set the header, X-Forwarded-For only when TRUST_PROXY=true, and otherwise the single bucket 'unknown', so a client cannot rotate a spoofed header to escape its lockout
- **Errors:** `AUTH_ERROR` (the password does not match (401)), `RATE_LIMIT` (the client's bucket is locked (429 with Retry-After))

## MCP

### The two /api/mcp/[plugin]/* routes spawn an allowlisted local MCP server process and bridge it over SSE

- **id:** `mcp.stdio-sse-bridge` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** An MCP client (Claude Desktop, wired up via clitools.cowork-settings-desktop-mcp's local bridge entries) opening a GET SSE stream to /api/mcp/<plugin>/sse, then POSTing JSON-RPC frames to /api/mcp/<plugin>/message
- **Input:** GET: plugin name (route param). POST: a JSON-RPC message body + sessionId (query param, implied by the SSE handshake)
- **Output:** GET: an SSE stream (endpoint handshake frame, then message frames). POST: 202 Accepted (the real reply arrives asynchronously over the SSE stream, not in the POST response)
- **Rules:**
  - Q6 answer — what the 2 routes do: GET /sse validates the plugin name against findPlugin (LOCAL_STDIO_PLUGINS allowlist), spawns the plugin's child process on first use (getOrSpawn, one process shared across all sessions for that plugin name), registers a per-connection send callback, and immediately sends an `event: endpoint` frame telling the client where to POST (`/api/mcp/<plugin>/message?sessionId=<sid>`) — this hand-implements the HTTP+SSE MCP transport variant (separate stream/POST endpoints keyed by session id), not the newer single-endpoint streamable-HTTP transport
  - POST /message validates the same allowlist, then writes the raw JSON-RPC body straight to the spawned child's stdin (sendToChild) and returns 202 with no correlation to a specific response — the actual JSON-RPC reply comes back later over the child's stdout, broadcast to all sessions currently registered for that plugin over their SSE streams
  - Only names present in the hardcoded LOCAL_STDIO_PLUGINS constant (currently just 'browsermcp', spawning `npx -y @browsermcp/mcp@latest`) may be spawned — per the source comment, this is deliberate RCE prevention: no user-supplied command can ever reach spawn(). This is exactly why cowork-settings' buildCustomEntries (for plugins added via the marketplace modal) only accepts URL-based (remote HTTP/SSE) custom entries and has no stdio path for user input
  - The child process is reused across all SSE sessions for that plugin name and is killed automatically once the last session disconnects (unregisterSession — 'avoid idle orphan process leak'); killAllBridges() is the app-shutdown hook that force-kills any still-running bridges
  - Outbound tool-result text content over 2000 chars is passed through smartFilterText/collapseRepeated before being broadcast — truncating to 50000 chars and collapsing runs of ≥30 same-role sibling lines down to a head/tail sample — a bandwidth/token-shaping transform local to this bridge, separate from and unrelated to open-sse/rtk's token saver pipeline
  - Q6 answer — where MCP server defs get written: NOT here. This pair of routes only serves already-spawned local plugins; the actual managedMcpServers list (which combines these local bridge entries with remote DEFAULT_PLUGINS and marketplace-modal custom entries) is written to Claude Desktop's own config by clitools.cowork-settings-desktop-mcp
  - Q6 answer — what the marketplace modal reads: McpMarketplaceModal.js does NOT call either of these two routes at all — it calls /api/cli-tools/cowork-mcp-registry (catalog) and /api/cli-tools/cowork-mcp-tools (tool-list probe), both traced under clitools.cowork-mcp-marketplace-fetch. This bridge is consumed only by whatever MCP client cowork-settings wired a bridge URL into (Claude Desktop itself), never directly by the dashboard UI
- **Streaming:** yes
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (plugin name not found in LOCAL_STDIO_PLUGINS — 404 on both GET and POST), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (POST called while no session/process is running for that plugin (Bridge not running) — 500)

## Media Providers

### What every non-chat lane genuinely shares with the chat lane vs. what each lane independently re-implements

- **id:** `media.account-loop-shared-vs-duplicated` · **module:** `media`
- **Trigger:** Any of the 7 non-chat entry handlers processing a request
- **Input:** none
- **Output:** none
- **Rules:**
  - Genuinely SHARED (same imported functions, same module, same DB fields): getProviderCredentials, markAccountUnavailable, clearAccountError (src/sse/services/auth.js) and checkAndRefreshToken/updateProviderCredentials (src/sse/services/tokenRefresh.js) — every one of embeddings.js, imageGeneration.js, tts.js, stt.js, videoGeneration.js, search.js, fetch.js imports these from the exact same files the chat lane's handleChat uses; the modelLock_*/testStatus persistence model (account.lock-storage-persistence) is identical across all 8 lanes (7 media + chat)
  - DUPLICATED (independently re-implemented per file, not shared as a function): the outer while(true) retry-and-rotate loop itself. All 7 non-chat handlers hand-write their own copy of: init excludeConnectionIds/lastError/lastStatus, call getProviderCredentials, branch on allRateLimited vs exhausted vs found, call the core handler, branch on result.success, call markAccountUnavailable, and continue-or-return — this is the same ~25-30 line shape rewritten 7 times rather than factored into one shared helper (e.g. runWithAccountFallback(provider, model, coreFn))
  - Combo expansion (open-sse/services/combo.js's handleComboChat/getComboModels) is shared code but inconsistently WIRED: present in tts, webSearch, webFetch; absent in embeddings, image generation, stt, video generation — video generation is the only lane that explicitly rejects a combo model with its own error message, the other three combo-less lanes simply treat a combo name as an unresolvable provider id

### COMBO_KINDS is a permanently-empty Set — combo creation/listing UI for image and tts kinds is unreachable, and the code that would render it is dead

- **id:** `media.dashboard-combo-kinds-disabled` · **module:** `media`
- **Trigger:** MediaProviderKindPage render for kind=image or kind=tts
- **Input:** none
- **Output:** supportsCombo is always false for every kind on this page (COMBO_KINDS.has(kind) can never be true since COMBO_KINDS is new Set([]))
- **Rules:**
  - The page's own comment says why: "Kinds that support combos (currently disabled for image/tts — temporarily hidden)" — COMBO_BASE_NAMES still names image/tts explicitly (image-combo/tts-combo), confirming those two kinds are the intended-but-disabled members of an empty set, not an accidentally-never-populated generic mechanism
  - Because supportsCombo is always false: the combos fetch effect never runs, the "Create Combo" button never renders, handleCreateCombo is defined but never callable from the UI, and the ComboList component (defined in this file) never renders — four pieces of working code made permanently unreachable by one empty Set literal
  - This is NOT a blanket disable of media combos: /dashboard/media-providers/web (webSearch/webFetch) has its own independent, unconditional Create-Combo button and ComboList, wired with no COMBO_KINDS gate at all, and /dashboard/media-providers/combo/[id] (the combo detail/editor page) still fully supports webSearch, webFetch, image, and tts kinds via its own KIND_LABELS/EXAMPLE_PATHS maps — an image or tts combo created before this gate existed (or by any other client of POST /api/combos, which accepts kind:"image"/"tts" with no restriction) remains fully editable by direct URL, only its creation/listing entry point on this one page is blocked
- **Note:** 9router's mechanism here is an accident of its stack. Behavior required, mechanism not.

### getEffectiveStatus displays a stale "unavailable" testStatus as "active" once its lock has actually expired

- **id:** `media.dashboard-effective-status-stale` · **module:** `media`
- **Trigger:** Any media-providers [kind] dashboard page render, computing each connection's displayed status badge
- **Input:** A connection row's testStatus field plus its modelLock_* fields
- **Output:** "active" (displayed as Connected) instead of the DB-stored "unavailable", specifically when no modelLock_* field still has a future timestamp
- **Rules:**
  - The exact condition: `conn.testStatus === "unavailable" && !isCooldown ? "active" : conn.testStatus` — isCooldown is true only if some modelLock_${x} field's value parses to a Date strictly in the future; any other testStatus value (active/error/expired) passes through unchanged
  - This exists because testStatus is only ever written back to "active" by clearAccountError (src/sse/services/auth.js), which runs solely on a successful request to that connection — a connection whose cooldown already expired but which has not yet been re-selected for a live request stays testStatus:"unavailable" in the DB indefinitely; getProviderCredentials's own selection logic checks the live lock expiry directly (not testStatus), so the connection IS actually eligible for selection again even while its stored testStatus still says otherwise
  - getEffectiveStatus is purely a display-layer correction for this staleness — it never writes back to the DB; the next real request through that connection is what will eventually reconcile testStatus via clearAccountError, this function just prevents the dashboard from showing a permanently-stuck error badge in the meantime

### POST /v1/embeddings — account-selection loop + embeddingsCore provider dispatch

- **id:** `media.embedding-lane` · **module:** `media`
- **Trigger:** POST /v1/embeddings
- **Input:** { model: "provider/model", input: string|string[], encoding_format?, dimensions? }
- **Output:** OpenAI-shaped embeddings response, or an error body
- **Rules:**
  - handleEmbeddings resolves provider/model via getModelInfo, then runs its own while(true) credential+fallback loop (getProviderCredentials / markAccountUnavailable / clearAccountError / checkAndRefreshToken, all imported from the same src/sse/services/auth.js and tokenRefresh.js the chat lane uses) before calling handleEmbeddingsCore once per attempt
  - embeddingsCore dispatches to a per-provider adapter (open-sse/handlers/embeddingProviders/{id}.js); a misconfigured adapter (e.g. selfhosted-embedding with no baseUrl) throws inside buildUrl/buildHeaders/buildBody, which is caught and turned into a 400 naming the reason rather than escaping as a 500 or hanging request — an explicit design choice called out in the handler's own comment
  - On success, usage is only recorded when exactEmbeddingUsage() can derive an exact (non-estimated) token count from the provider's raw usage block (prompt_tokens/input_tokens present, completion_tokens===0, total_tokens===prompt_tokens) — an estimated or malformed usage object silently skips saveRequestUsage entirely rather than recording an approximate figure
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (missing model or input, or input is neither string nor array), `AUTH_ERROR` (no credentials at all for the provider (excludeConnectionIds empty)), `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (all accounts rate-limited/locked (credentials.allRateLimited)), `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (every account exhausted after rotation (excludeConnectionIds non-empty, no credentials left))

### POST /v1/images/generations — account-selection loop + imageGenerationCore provider dispatch, including codex's SSE streaming path

- **id:** `media.image-lane` · **module:** `media`
- **Trigger:** POST /v1/images/generations
- **Input:** { model, prompt, n?, size?, output_format? }, Accept: text/event-stream (opt-in streaming), ?response_format=binary (opt-in raw bytes)
- **Output:** OpenAI-shaped images response (JSON with data[].b64_json/url); raw image bytes when binaryOutput; an SSE Response passthrough for codex when streamToClient is requested and codex's adapter honors it
- **Rules:**
  - wantsStream is derived purely from the inbound Accept header (Accept: text/event-stream) and passed through as streamToClient; imageGenerationCore only actually streams when the selected provider's adapter.parseResponse returns { sseResponse } — codex is the only adapter observed doing so, every other provider ignores streamToClient and returns a normal JSON/binary Response regardless of the client's Accept header
  - binaryOutput (?response_format=binary) decodes the first result's b64_json (or fetches its url and base64-encodes it) into raw bytes, returned with a Content-Type matching output_format (png/jpeg/webp) — this happens after normalize(), so it applies uniformly across every adapter's already-OpenAI-shaped output
  - Adapters that set useExecutor/executeViaExecutor skip the generic buildUrl/buildHeaders/buildBody/fetch path entirely and instead reuse that provider's full chat executor (401/403 refresh handling included) — a second, executor-driven dispatch style distinct from the generic adapter path most providers use
- **Streaming:** yes
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (missing prompt, or adapter.buildUrl/buildBody/buildHeaders throws (e.g. bad size for that provider)), `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (all accounts rate-limited/locked)

### imageToText has no dedicated request lane — it is a catalog label for vision-capable chat models, served entirely through /v1/chat/completions

- **id:** `media.image-to-text-routes-via-chat` · **module:** `media`
- **Trigger:** A client calling /v1/chat/completions with a model whose registry entry declares "imageToText" in serviceKinds
- **Input:** Standard chat-completions body with an image content part
- **Output:** Standard chat-completions response — imageToText is never its own request shape
- **Rules:**
  - 11 providers (anthropic, gemini, groq, kimchi, minimax, mistral, openai, openrouter, vercel-ai-gateway, vertex, xai) declare "imageToText" in serviceKinds; none declares an imageToTextConfig block (0 files), because there is nothing kind-specific to configure — the request is an ordinary chat completion
  - GET /v1/models filters imageToText models into the LLM list when the caller also requested the llm kind (kindFilter.includes(LLM_KIND)) — imageToText-kind models are presented to clients as vision-capable chat models, not as a separate catalog of image-understanding endpoints
  - The dashboard still gives imageToText its own MEDIA_PROVIDER_KINDS entry, page route, and provider-card grid (getProvidersByKind("imageToText")) purely for discoverability/UI grouping — the underlying request that a click on "Try it" builds is a chat completion, not a call to a dedicated imageToText backend (see media.kind-endpoint-map-mismatch for where that UI wiring is actually broken)

### Two independently-maintained kind→endpoint maps disagree for imageToText and webFetch

- **id:** `media.kind-endpoint-map-mismatch` · **module:** `media`
- **Trigger:** GET /v1/models/info (builds a model's endpoint field from KIND_ENDPOINT); the media-providers connection detail page's GenericExampleCard (builds a curl example AND performs a live "Try it" fetch from MEDIA_PROVIDER_KINDS[kind].endpoint)
- **Input:** kind id (imageToText or webFetch)
- **Output:** Two different, both-consumed path strings for the same kind
- **Rules:**
  - MEDIA_PROVIDER_KINDS.imageToText.endpoint.path is "/v1/images/understanding" — a path that does not exist anywhere else in the codebase (grep for "understanding" across src/ and open-sse/ finds only this one declaration); the real route imageToText models resolve to is /v1/chat/completions, which models/info/route.js's own independently-hand-written KIND_ENDPOINT map gets right
  - KIND_ENDPOINT.webFetch is "/v1/fetch" (missing the /web/ segment); the real route is /v1/web/fetch (src/app/api/v1/web/fetch/route.js), which MEDIA_PROVIDER_KINDS.webFetch.endpoint.path gets right — the mismatch runs the opposite direction from the imageToText case (here it's models/info that's wrong)
  - GenericExampleCard.js's handleRun doesn't just render a curl string for imageToText: it actually calls fetch(`/api${apiPathWithQuery}`, { method: kindConfig.endpoint.method, ... }) using MEDIA_PROVIDER_KINDS' path — so the dashboard's "Try it" button for any imageToText-kind provider/model POSTs to /api/v1/images/understanding, a route that returns 404, not the working /v1/chat/completions
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (GenericExampleCard's "Try it" is used against an imageToText-kind provider — the built request 404s against a route that was never implemented)
- **AIGate required behavior:** MEDIA_PROVIDER_KINDS and models/info's KIND_ENDPOINT should agree, and both should name a route that actually exists, for every kind.

### MEDIA_PROVIDER_KINDS — the 9 kinds, their labels/icons, and each kind's declared REST endpoint

- **id:** `media.kind-registry-and-endpoints` · **module:** `media`
- **Trigger:** Any dashboard media-providers page render, or GET /v1/models/info building a per-model endpoint field
- **Input:** none
- **Output:** A static array of 9 { id, label, icon, endpoint:{method,path} } objects: embedding, image, imageToText, tts, stt, webSearch, webFetch, video, music
- **Rules:**
  - getProvidersByKind(kind) is the single lookup every dashboard media page and the /v1/models listing route uses to turn a kind id into a provider list: it defaults a provider's kinds to ["llm"] when serviceKinds is absent, excludes hidden providers, and additionally excludes a provider from just that one kind via hiddenKinds — a provider can be hidden from one kind's listing while still appearing under another
  - Every kind's endpoint.path in MEDIA_PROVIDER_KINDS is a second, independently hand-maintained copy of the same routing fact also encoded in src/app/api/v1/models/info/route.js's own KIND_ENDPOINT map — the two are not derived from one source, so they can (and do, see media.kind-endpoint-map-mismatch) drift apart
  - 9 kinds are declared but only 7 have a live request-handling lane (embedding, image, tts, stt, webSearch, webFetch, video); imageToText has no lane of its own (see media.image-to-text-routes-via-chat) and music has none at all (see media.music-kind-dead-config)

### The "music" kind is fully declared in shared config/UI scaffolding but has zero implementing code anywhere

- **id:** `media.music-kind-dead-config` · **module:** `media`
- **Trigger:** none — no request path reaches this kind
- **Input:** none
- **Output:** none
- **Rules:**
  - music is a full MEDIA_PROVIDER_KINDS entry (label "Music", icon music_note, endpoint POST /v1/audio/music) and musicConfig is a recognized key in both providers/index.js's MEDIA_KEYS build set and src/shared/constants/providers.js's MEDIA_ENTRY_KEYS mirror, and is read defensively in /api/providers/validate/route.js's connectivity-test config picker — but grep -rl musicConfig open-sse/providers/registry/*.js returns zero files: no provider declares it
  - There is no /v1/audio/music route file, no music core handler under open-sse/handlers/, and no src/sse/handlers/music.js entry handler — every other kind's three-layer stack (registry config key -> core handler -> route) is entirely absent for music except the config-key plumbing itself
  - Because no provider ever sets musicConfig, getProvidersByKind("music") always returns an empty array — the dashboard's music kind page (if navigated to directly by URL) would render its own "No providers support Music yet" empty state, the one path where this dead kind is even visible
- **Note:** 9router's mechanism here is an accident of its stack. Behavior required, mechanism not.

### POST /v1/audio/transcriptions — noAuth bypass, then account-selection loop + sttCore provider dispatch

- **id:** `media.stt-lane` · **module:** `media`
- **Trigger:** POST /v1/audio/transcriptions (multipart form)
- **Input:** multipart form: model, file (required); optional per-provider fields
- **Output:** OpenAI Whisper-compatible transcription JSON
- **Rules:**
  - CREDENTIALED_PROVIDERS is computed once from serviceKinds.includes("stt") && !noAuth && sttConfig.authType !== "none" — a provider absent from that set (e.g. a local/self-hosted STT with no auth) skips the entire account-selection loop and calls handleSttCore directly with no credentials object at all, the only media lane with an unconditional no-credential fast path rather than a noAuth virtual-connection inside getProviderCredentials
  - 6 providers declare sttConfig; sttCore.js dispatches per-provider (assemblyai's async submit+poll, others are single-call) but all funnel through the same upstreamError() helper for non-ok responses
  - maxDuration = 300 is set on the route module itself (Next.js route segment config) specifically to allow up to 5 minutes for large audio file processing — this is route-level config, not something sttCore or the handler enforces itself
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (missing model or file, or invalid model format), `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (all credentialed accounts rate-limited/locked)

### POST /v1/audio/speech — combo expansion + account-selection loop + ttsCore provider dispatch

- **id:** `media.tts-lane` · **module:** `media`
- **Trigger:** POST /v1/audio/speech
- **Input:** { model, input: string, language?, style? }, ?response_format=mp3|json
- **Output:** Raw audio bytes (default) or { audio: base64, format } JSON
- **Rules:**
  - model may name a combo, not just a provider/model pair: getComboModels(modelStr) expands it and the request is dispatched through handleComboChat (open-sse/services/combo.js) across the combo's member models before the single-provider account-selection loop ever runs — the same combo-expansion module the chat lane uses, reused here rather than duplicated
  - handleTtsCore first tries a special-case adapter (getTtsAdapter — google-tts, edge-tts, local-device, elevenlabs, openai, openrouter, gemini, xiaomi-mimo); providers without one instead go through synthesizeViaConfig, a generic config-driven path keyed off the registry's ttsConfig (hyperbolic, deepgram, nvidia, huggingface, inworld, cartesia, playht, coqui, tortoise, qwen, ...) — two independent implementation strategies for the same endpoint, chosen per-provider
  - response_format=json wraps the synthesized audio as base64 in a JSON body instead of returning it as a binary response — both code paths funnel through the same createTtsResponse formatter regardless of which adapter/config path produced the audio
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (missing model or input), `INVALID_REQUEST` (provider has neither a special-case adapter nor synthesizeViaConfig support)

### Voice listing — one generic credential-free route plus four dedicated per-provider routes that require a stored connection

- **id:** `media.tts-voice-listing` · **module:** `media`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard TTS provider/model picker loading available voices
- **Input:** GET /api/media-providers/tts/voices?provider=edge-tts|local-device|elevenlabs&apiKey=... ; GET /api/media-providers/tts/{deepgram|elevenlabs|inworld|minimax}/voices
- **Output:** { voices, languages, byLang } (generic route) or { languages, byLang } (dedicated routes)
- **Rules:**
  - The generic /api/media-providers/tts/voices route dispatches through VOICE_FETCHERS[provider] (re-exported from ttsCore.js) and needs no stored connection for edge-tts/local-device; for elevenlabs it instead reads apiKey from the query string, not from a stored providerConnections row — the only voice route that accepts a credential as a request parameter rather than looking one up
  - The four dedicated routes (deepgram, elevenlabs, inworld, minimax) all read the FIRST active connection for that exact provider id via getProviderConnections({ provider, isActive: true }) and 400 with "No <Provider> connection found" if none exists — no account rotation, no mutex, and no fallback to a second connection of the same provider if the first one's key is invalid
  - GET /v1/audio/voices (the OpenAI-style public listing) proxies to a hardcoded PROVIDER_API map covering elevenlabs/deepgram/inworld/edge-tts/local-device but omits minimax — minimax's own dedicated voices route exists and works when called directly, but is not reachable through the public /v1/audio/voices listing endpoint
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (generic route's provider query param has no matching VOICE_FETCHERS entry), `AUTH_ERROR` (dedicated route's provider has no active stored connection), `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (the upstream voices/models call itself fails (non-ok response))

### POST /v1/videos/{generations,edits,extensions} + GET /v1/videos/[id] — async job proxy, xAI-only in practice

- **id:** `media.video-lane` · **module:** `media`
- **Trigger:** POST /v1/videos/generations|edits|extensions, or GET /v1/videos/{request_id} to poll
- **Input:** JSON or multipart body forwarded byte-for-byte (model may carry a provider/ prefix); x-connection-id header pins polling to the creating account
- **Output:** Upstream JSON passed through verbatim (request_id/status/video.url/error), with x-9router-connection-id echoed back on create so the client can pin subsequent polls
- **Rules:**
  - Only xai declares both serviceKinds:["video"] and a videoConfig block; DEFAULT_VIDEO_PROVIDER="xai" is the fallback target for a bare model id with no provider prefix — the handler's own comment states "Video generation is xAI-only today"
  - Creation POSTs are treated as billable and are NEVER auto-retried on a network error (the job may already exist upstream) — the only retry is a single auth-refresh-and-resend on 401/403/429 (CREATE_ROTATION_STATUSES), which only fires before the upstream could have created the job
  - GET polls are pinned to the creating account (x-connection-id) with explicitly no cross-account rotation, since a video job lives only on the account that created it — this is a materially different fallback shape from every other media lane's per-request account rotation
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (model resolves to a provider with no videoConfig and the model string included an explicit provider/ prefix), `INVALID_REQUEST` (model resolves to a combo (combos are not supported for video generation)), `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (all xai accounts rate-limited/locked on create)
- **AIGate required behavior:** A model the catalog lists with kind:"video" should be reachable through the video-generation lane (or should not be listed as kind:video at all).

### POST /v1/web/fetch — URL extraction, account-selection loop scoped to a webfetch-specific lock key

- **id:** `media.webfetch-lane` · **module:** `media`
- **Trigger:** POST /v1/web/fetch
- **Input:** { provider|model, url, format?, max_characters? } — provider IS the model, same shape convention as webSearch
- **Output:** { url, title, format, text, links, metrics:{response_time_ms, upstream_latency_ms} }
- **Rules:**
  - 5 providers declare fetchConfig (dispatches to firecrawl, jina-reader, tavily, exa, ollama per the handler's own header comment); each returns a normalized shape regardless of provider
  - fetchLockKey = `webfetch:${providerId}` exists for the same reason as webSearch's lock scoping: the handler's own comment names ollama explicitly — Ollama uses the same connection for chat and fetch, so an upstream fetch failure must not take that account offline for chat requests too
  - assertPublicUrlResolved (an SSRF guard) is applied to the target URL before any fetch is attempted — the only media lane in this task whose own entry handler performs an SSRF check itself rather than relying solely on a downstream fetch wrapper
  - Combo expansion is present here too (getComboModelsFromData + handleComboChat), matching the webSearch/tts lanes but not embeddings/image/stt/video — combo support was added per-lane individually rather than as a shared property all media lanes get automatically
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (missing provider/model or url, or url fails the SSRF public-resolution check), `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (all accounts (own connection) rate-limited/locked under the webfetch lock key)

### POST /v1/search — combo expansion, credential-fallback-to-chat-provider, dedicated-API vs chat-wrapped search with cross-mode failover

- **id:** `media.websearch-lane` · **module:** `media`
- **Trigger:** POST /v1/search
- **Input:** { provider|model, query, search_type?, max_results? } — provider IS the model, there is no separate model field for a non-combo request
- **Output:** Unified search-result envelope: { results:[{title,url,snippet,...}], metrics:{response_time_ms,...} }
- **Rules:**
  - A provider can declare searchConfig (dedicated search API — 12 providers: brave-search, exa, firecrawl, glm, google-pse, jina-reader, linkup, ollama-search, ollama, searchapi, ...), searchViaChat (wrap a chat-completions call as search — 9 providers: antigravity, gemini, kimi, minimax, openai, perplexity-agent, perplexity, vercel-ai-gateway, xai), or both; handleSingleProviderSearch prefers the dedicated API when providerConfig is set, falling back to handleChatSearch only when no dedicated config exists
  - When a provider has BOTH searchConfig and searchViaChat, a dedicated-API failure that is retriable (status not in NON_RETRIABLE = {400,401,403,404}) and still within GLOBAL_TIMEOUT_MS (15s) triggers an automatic same-request failover to the chat-wrapped search for that same provider — a second live upstream attempt inside one /v1/search call, distinct from and in addition to the outer account-rotation loop
  - credentialFallback lets a search-only provider reuse a related chat provider's stored credentials (ollama-search reuses ollama's key, zai-search reuses glm's) when the search provider itself has no connection; markAccountUnavailable is scoped to a synthetic searchLockKey = `websearch:${providerId}` rather than the shared provider's default lock, specifically so a websearch failure on a borrowed key does not take that key offline for its owning chat provider too
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (missing provider/model or query), `INVALID_REQUEST` (resolved provider has neither searchConfig nor searchViaChat), `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (all accounts (own + credentialFallback) rate-limited/locked under the websearch lock key)

## Model mapping

### Disabling a model only hides it from listing endpoints — an alias (or a direct provider/model string) pointing at a disabled model still routes normally

- **id:** `catalog.alias-disabled-model-bypass` · **module:** `catalog`
- **Trigger:** A chat request whose resolved { provider, model } matches an entry in the disabledModels table
- **Input:** alias or direct model string resolving to a disabled model id
- **Output:** request proceeds to the provider exactly as if the model were not disabled
- **Rules:**
  - getDisabledModels()/getDisabledByProvider() (disabledModelsRepo.js) is imported and consulted ONLY by listing/management code: /api/models (dashboard model list), /api/models/disabled (CRUD), and /v1/models (client-facing catalog) — never by src/sse/handlers/chat.js or any open-sse handler
  - handleSingleModelChat's only post-resolution gate is 'is provider non-null' — there is no disabled-model check anywhere on the chat request path before dispatch
  - A user-defined alias created via the alias-management endpoint that points at a disabled model.id resolves normally through resolveModelAliasFromMap and is dispatched exactly like any other model
- **AIGate required behavior:** A model marked disabled in the dashboard should be rejected if a request targets it — directly or via an alias — mirroring how it disappears from every model-listing endpoint ("disable" implies block, not just hide)

### Two different routes write the same modelAliases KV scope with opposite key/value conventions

- **id:** `catalog.alias-dual-convention-collision` · **module:** `catalog`
- **Trigger:** PUT /api/models/alias vs PUT /api/models, both described as 'update model alias'
- **Input:** PUT /api/models/alias body { model, alias } -> setModelAlias(alias, model); PUT /api/models body { model, alias } -> setModelAlias(model, alias)
- **Output:** a write into the same 'modelAliases' KV scope, but keyed in opposite directions depending on which route was called
- **Rules:**
  - aliasRepo.js's own contract, per its header comment, is 'modelAliases: key=alias, value=modelString' and setModelAlias(alias, model) implements exactly that
  - /api/models/alias's PUT calls setModelAlias(alias, model) — matches the documented contract (key=alias)
  - /api/models's PUT calls setModelAlias(model, alias) — passes the real model string into the 'alias' parameter position and the real alias into the 'model' position, storing the row inverted (key=modelId, value=aliasName)
  - The actual chat-routing consumer, resolveModelAliasFromMap(parsed.model, aliases), does aliases[parsed.model] and expects the key to be a short alias name and the value to be a 'provider/model' string — that only matches rows written by /api/models/alias's PUT; rows written by /api/models's PUT (keyed by full model id) are structurally invisible to routing
  - /api/models's own GET reads modelAliases[fullModel] to populate the display-only 'alias' column — self-consistent with its own inverted PUT, but that means a routable alias set via /api/models/alias's PUT never shows up as that model's display label, and a display label set via /api/models's PUT never resolves as a routable alias during a chat request
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (model or alias missing from either route's request body)
- **AIGate required behavior:** Both endpoints described as setting 'the alias for a model' should write the same KV shape so a value set through either surface is visible to the other, and to actual chat routing

### A user-defined model alias resolves to a real provider/model pair before any capability lookup or dispatch happens

- **id:** `catalog.alias-resolve-before-capability` · **module:** `catalog`
- **Trigger:** A chat request whose body.model is not in provider/model form
- **Input:** raw body.model string (candidate alias)
- **Output:** resolved { provider, model } pair, which is what flows into capability lookup and the executor
- **Rules:**
  - handleSingleModelChat calls getModelInfo(modelStr) before doing anything else with the model string — this resolves aliases via resolveModelAliasFromMap against the modelAliases DB table
  - The resolved { provider, model } pair is what flows down into chatCore.js; getCapabilitiesForModel(provider, model) is only ever called there, on the ALREADY-RESOLVED pair — capability lookup structurally cannot see an unresolved alias string
  - If the string is also a registered combo name, combo lookup runs before/alongside alias resolution and takes priority (a null provider from getModelInfo triggers a combo-name check, not an alias re-check)
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (the resolved provider is null and the string isn't a valid combo name either)

### Background models.dev sync — daily refresh, cross-gateway majority vote, tolerance band, fail-open

- **id:** `catalog.capability-catalog-sync-majority-vote` · **module:** `catalog`
- **Trigger:** Server startup (60s delay), then every 24h, or a manual POST /api/models/catalog-sync
- **Input:** https://models.dev/api.json (external feed, 145 providers / 4000+ models per capabilities.js's own doc comment)
- **Output:** installed catalogSource consumed by capabilities.js's refine(); a slimmed CATALOG_FILE and raw CATALOG_RAW_FILE written to disk
- **Rules:**
  - A modality is only accepted when at least MIN_SHARE=50% of the gateways models.dev aggregates for a given model agree it's present — a single mislabelling reseller cannot flip a capability on
  - A context/maxOutput limit difference under LIMIT_TOLERANCE=10% is ignored (gateways round 200000 vs 202752) — avoids replacing a stable value over rounding noise
  - A PROVIDER_ALIASES table translates 9router's internal provider ids (glm, kimi, qwen, zhipu, hunyuan...) to models.dev's differently-named providers (zai, moonshotai, alibaba, tencent...) purely for the limits lookup — a provider absent from the map falls back to whatever the local PATTERN_CAPABILITIES table already resolves
  - Sync failures are swallowed deliberately (per the module's own header comment) — a stale or missing catalog file just means refine() has nothing extra to apply; it is never surfaced as a request-time error
- **Errors:** `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (the models.dev fetch fails or times out)

### refine() may only turn a capability ON, never OFF

- **id:** `catalog.capability-refine-additive-only` · **module:** `catalog`
- **Trigger:** Every getCapabilitiesForModel call that reaches tier 3 (pattern match) or tier 4 (floor)
- **Input:** base caps object from a matched pattern (tier 3) or null (tier 4), plus provider and model
- **Output:** merged caps object with modality flags possibly flipped to true, and contextWindow/maxOutput possibly raised — never lowered or flipped to false
- **Rules:**
  - refine()'s modality loop only ever executes `result[key] = true` when the synced catalog positively asserts a modality — there is no matching branch that sets a key to false, so a hand-written tier-3 pattern's true value can never be overwritten to false by the catalog
  - The vision-name heuristic follows the same rule: `if (!result.vision && looksLikeVisionModel(model)) result.vision = true` — it is only even evaluated when vision is still false, and can only flip it on
  - Tiers 1-2 (PROVIDER_CAPABILITIES, MODEL_CAPABILITIES) never reach refine() at all, since getCapabilitiesForModel returns before refine() is called for those tiers — additivity only matters for the tier-3/4 path
  - Why additive-only: the synced catalog is an unverified third-party feed (models.dev, refreshed daily and voted on across disagreeing gateways — see catalog.capability-catalog-sync-majority-vote). If refine() could remove a capability, a bad sync or a majority of mislabelling resellers could silently strip vision/tools/search from a model a maintainer hand-verified and shipped correctly in the tier-3 pattern table — a false POSITIVE (turning a capability on that isn't real) fails safely (the provider errors or ignores the extra field), but a false NEGATIVE (removing a real one) fails unsafely: chatCore.js's stripUnsupportedModalities would silently drop client-sent media for a model that actually supports it, producing a wrong response with no error surfaced anywhere

### getCapabilitiesForModel's 4-tier priority chain — first match wins, no cross-tier merge

- **id:** `catalog.capability-tier-fallback` · **module:** `catalog`
- **Trigger:** Every call to getCapabilitiesForModel(provider, model) — chatCore.js modality stripping, /api/models and /v1/models listings
- **Input:** provider id/alias, raw model id (optionally vendor-prefixed, e.g. anthropic/claude-opus-4.7)
- **Output:** capabilities object, always merged over DEFAULT_CAPABILITIES so every field is present
- **Rules:**
  - Tier 1: PROVIDER_CAPABILITIES[provider][model] (exact model, then the vendor-prefix-stripped baseModel) — provider-specific override tables (NVIDIA, Codex, Kiro, CodeBuddy.cn, Qoder, Poolside)
  - Tier 2: MODEL_CAPABILITIES[baseModel] then MODEL_CAPABILITIES[model] — canonical exact-id exceptions that a pattern would mis-match
  - Tier 3: PATTERN_CAPABILITIES — an ordered glob list (specific families before generic, e.g. glm-4.6v before the generic glm-4 pattern); the first pattern to match baseModel OR the raw model string wins, then the result is passed through refine()
  - Tier 4: refine(null, provider, model) — the DEFAULT_CAPABILITIES floor, also routed through refine() so even a completely uncatalogued model can still pick up a synced-catalog or vision-name signal
  - Each tier RETURNS immediately inside its own if-block — there is no merging across tiers. When two tiers disagree, the higher-priority tier wins outright: a provider override with vision:false takes precedence even if the same model's exact-id or pattern entry says vision:true, because tier 1 short-circuits before tier 2/3/4 ever run

### NOT_VISION is tested before VISION_NAME in looksLikeVisionModel, and can only turn vision on

- **id:** `catalog.capability-vision-pattern-order` · **module:** `catalog`
- **Trigger:** Tier 3/4 refine() fallback for a model absent from every hand-written table and the synced catalog
- **Input:** model id string
- **Output:** boolean vision flag (additive only — see catalog.capability-refine-additive-only)
- **Rules:**
  - looksLikeVisionModel tests NOT_VISION FIRST and returns false immediately on a match, before VISION_NAME is even evaluated — any model id containing an image-generation, embedding, rerank, guard/moderation, or audio keyword can never be classified as vision-input-capable by this heuristic, even if it also contains a vision-sounding token
  - If the order were reversed (VISION_NAME checked first), a real registry entry — NVIDIA's 'nvidia/llama-nemotron-embed-vl-1b-v2:free', an EMBEDDING model (kind:"embedding" in openrouter.js's registry, not a vision-input chat model) — would match VISION_NAME on its 'vl' token and be misclassified as vision-capable, when NOT_VISION's 'embed' keyword correctly identifies it as a non-chat model first

### GET /api/tags — fixed two-entry fixture list mimicking Ollama's model-discovery response, used by Ollama-compatible tools before they call the ollama chat lane (05's routing.ollama-lane-transform)

- **id:** `catalog.ollama-tags-listing` · **module:** `catalog`
- **Trigger:** An Ollama-compatible client's startup/model-discovery probe against GET /api/tags before it sends a chat request
- **Input:** none
- **Output:** { models: [{ name, modified_at, size, digest, details:{format,family,parameter_size,quantization_level} }, ...] } — always exactly the same two hardcoded entries (llama3.2, qwen2.5)
- **Rules:**
  - The entire response is a static, hand-authored object (open-sse/config/ollamaModels.js) — it does not read providerConnections, PROVIDER_MODELS, customModels, modelAliases, or disabledModels, so it is completely disconnected from the real, routable model catalog every other listing endpoint (v1/models, v1beta/models) derives from those sources
  - A repo-wide grep for the two fixture names finds llama3.2 also hardcoded in src/app/api/v1/api/chat/route.js (the ollama chat lane, routing.ollama-lane-transform) as modelName's fallback default when the request body's own model field is missing or fails to parse — but that is a response-label default for the outgoing {model, message, done} shape, not a resolution/routing mechanism (handleChat still dispatches on the real, unmodified request body). Neither llama3.2 nor qwen2.5 maps to any real provider/model id, alias, or ollama-local static entry anywhere — the fixture list still names nothing a chat request can actually resolve to
- **AIGate required behavior:** The model names an Ollama-compatible client discovers via GET /api/tags are names it can actually use in a subsequent chat request on the Ollama lane (POST /v1/api/chat, routing.ollama-lane-transform) — a discovery endpoint's contract is that its results are usable

### POST /v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent and :streamGenerateContent — per-model invocation route under the v1beta/models path, translating to/from the internal OpenAI-shaped pipeline

- **id:** `catalog.v1beta-generate-content-dispatch` · **module:** `catalog`
- **Trigger:** A Gemini-native client (Gemini CLI, the @google/genai SDK) invokes a specific model by path+action suffix
- **Input:** Path segments [provider?, model:action] (catch-all), Gemini-format request body (contents/systemInstruction/generationConfig)
- **Output:** Gemini GenerateContentResponse JSON (non-streaming), or a Gemini-shaped SSE stream (streaming) — never the raw OpenAI shape
- **Rules:**
  - Streaming is decided purely by the URL action suffix (:generateContent vs :streamGenerateContent), never by a body field — generationConfig.stream is explicitly called out in the source as not a real Gemini API field, so honoring a stream flag in the body would silently diverge from every real Gemini client's actual behavior
  - A TTS-shaped request (audio response modality requested, or the model id matches the known Gemini TTS model set) is detected and diverted entirely to forwardGeminiNativeRequest — a direct passthrough to Google's own Gemini API (not through handleChat/the internal routing pipeline at all), with its own account-fallback loop over gemini credentials, markAccountUnavailable/clearAccountError, and a dedicated timeout (GEMINI_NATIVE_TTS_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS)
  - Every other request is converted to the internal OpenAI body shape (convertGeminiToInternal) and dispatched through the same handleChat used by the standard /v1 lane, then the OpenAI response/stream is converted back to Gemini's candidates/usageMetadata shape (or Gemini SSE chunks) on the way out — this route is a pure format adapter around the shared chat pipeline for the non-TTS case, but a fully separate direct-passthrough implementation for the TTS case
  - The TTS passthrough path validates the client's API key itself (validateGeminiNativeClientKey, gated on settings.requireApiKey) because it bypasses handleChat's own endpoint.enforce-require-api-key gate entirely — the non-TTS path relies on handleChat's gate instead
- **Streaming:** yes
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (TTS path: model id fails GEMINI_NATIVE_MODEL_PATTERN (blocks path traversal in the upstream URL)), `AUTH_ERROR` (TTS path: requireApiKey true and the client key is missing/invalid), `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (TTS path: every gemini connection is exhausted (allRateLimited or no credentials)), `TIMEOUT` (TTS path: upstream fetch aborts after GEMINI_NATIVE_TTS_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS, classified 504)

### GET /v1beta/models — Gemini-format static model catalog for Gemini-native clients (e.g. Gemini CLI, the @google/genai SDK)

- **id:** `catalog.v1beta-models-listing` · **module:** `catalog`
- **Trigger:** A Gemini-native client lists models before calling :generateContent — reachable via 01's endpoint.rewrite-lanes /v1beta/* -> /api/v1beta/* rewrite
- **Input:** none
- **Output:** { models: [{ name, displayName, description, supportedGenerationMethods, inputTokenLimit, outputTokenLimit }, ...] }
- **Rules:**
  - Built directly from the static PROVIDER_MODELS table — unlike GET /v1/models (catalog.model-listing-live-override), it does NOT read providerConnections at all, so every configured model for every provider is listed regardless of whether that provider has an active connection, and it does NOT call getDisabledModels — a model disabled via the dashboard still appears here even though it is hidden from /v1/models and /v1/models/{kind} (the same gap catalog.alias-disabled-model-bypass documents for the chat/routing path, but here it affects a listing endpoint specifically, which is the one place that bug's own expectation says filtering SHOULD happen)
  - Every model is exposed twice under two name shapes: models/{provider}/{model.id} (provider-qualified) always, plus a second bare models/{model.id} entry specifically when provider === gemini — the bare form exists so a client asking for a plain Gemini model name (no provider prefix) still resolves
  - inputTokenLimit/outputTokenLimit are hardcoded constants (128000 / 8192) for every model regardless of that model's real context window — unlike /v1/models' context_length/max_completion_tokens fields (catalog.model-listing-live-override), which are derived per-model from getCapabilitiesForModel
  - supportedGenerationMethods is always [generateContent] except the bare gemini-provider entries, which also declare streamGenerateContent — this is what a Gemini SDK checks before offering the streaming call

## Model registry

### /api/models/availability — dashboard-facing, model-centric aggregation of per-connection cooldown/unavailable locks, plus a manual clear-cooldown action

- **id:** `catalog.model-availability-lock-state` · **module:** `catalog`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard "model availability" panel (GET), or an operator clicking "clear cooldown" for a specific provider+model (POST)
- **Input:** GET — none. POST { action: 'clearCooldown', provider, model }
- **Output:** GET — { models:[{provider, model, status:'cooldown'|'unavailable', until?, connectionId, connectionName, lastError}], unavailableCount }. POST — { ok: true } or 400 on an invalid action
- **Rules:**
  - The underlying per-model lock write/read primitives (the modelLock_{model} connection fields, the '__all'-model connection-wide lock, and testStatus/lastError bookkeeping) are already traced in 03-accounts-multiaccount.yaml (account.mark-unavailable-lock-reasons, account.lock-storage-persistence, account.clear-error-on-success) — this entry documents only the two things THIS route adds on top of that state: a flat, model-scoped view across every connection, and a manual override action
  - GET flattens every connection's active modelLock_* fields into one array via getActiveModelLocks — a lock is only included while new Date(value).getTime() > now (already-expired locks are silently dropped, not surfaced or cleaned up here)
  - A connection with testStatus:'unavailable' but zero active model-specific locks is reported once as a single model:'__all' row — connection-wide unavailability and per-model cooldown are two distinct rows in the same response shape
  - POST clearCooldown scopes to connections matching { provider } and only touches ones that actually have the modelLock_{model} field truthy; clearing the lock ALSO resets testStatus/lastError/backoffLevel back to active if the connection's overall status was 'unavailable' — a per-model clear can silently clear the connection's whole unavailable status, not just the one model's lock
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (POST action is not 'clearCooldown' or provider/model is missing)

### /api/models/test — synchronous per-model connectivity probe, self-dispatched through 9router's own /v1/* endpoints

- **id:** `catalog.model-connectivity-test` · **module:** `catalog`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard "test this model" action
- **Input:** POST { model, kind }  — kind ∈ llm (default) | embedding | image | stt
- **Output:** { ok: boolean, latencyMs, status, error?, note? }
- **Rules:**
  - pingModelByKind does not call the upstream provider directly — it issues a real HTTP request to 9router's OWN /api/v1/{chat/completions|embeddings|images/generations|audio/transcriptions} endpoint on 127.0.0.1, so the probe exercises the full request path (alias resolution, capability lookup, account selection, translation, upstream call) exactly like a real client would, not just a raw upstream ping
  - The internal self-call authenticates with a real active API key (first isActive!==false row from getApiKeys()) plus an x-9r-cli-token machine-id header — the probe is indistinguishable from an ordinary authenticated client request
  - Every probe kind has a 15000ms hard timeout (AbortSignal.timeout(15000)) and classifies success/failure from the RESPONSE BODY shape, not just HTTP status: e.g. embedding requires a non-empty data[0].embedding array, image requires a non-empty data array, stt requires non-empty trimmed text, llm requires a non-empty choices array
  - LLM probes use max_tokens:1024, not a smaller probe size, specifically because reasoning models spend their token budget on chain-of-thought before an answer (issue #3010 cited in the code) — a tiny max_tokens would starve the answer and produce a false failure
  - A reasoning model that hits finish_reason:'length' with empty visible content but non-empty reasoning/thinking text is treated as a SOFT PASS ({ ok:true, note:'reasoning-only response (length-limited)' }) rather than a failure — the probe distinguishes 'the connection works but the budget ran out' from 'the connection is broken'
  - stt probes synthesize a real (silent) 250ms 16kHz WAV file in-process rather than shipping a fixture asset, so the test has no external file dependency
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (model is missing from the POST body), `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (the internal /v1/* call returns a non-OK HTTP status or a provider-shaped error body), `TIMEOUT` (the internal call exceeds 15000ms and the AbortSignal fires)

### /api/models/custom — operator-added custom models, atomic upsert that preserves unset fields

- **id:** `catalog.model-custom-registration` · **module:** `catalog`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard "add custom model" form
- **Input:** POST { providerAlias, id, type, name, caps }
- **Output:** { success: true, added: boolean }
- **Rules:**
  - sanitizeCaps whitelists only boolean-valued keys present in CAPACITY_META (vision, reasoning) — any other key, or a non-boolean value, is silently dropped rather than rejected
  - addCustomModel's re-add path (row already exists for the same composite key) merges { ...prev, ...(name?{name}:{}), ...(caps?{caps}:{}) } — re-adding an existing custom model updates only the fields actually supplied in this call, never resets an omitted field
  - The composite key `${providerAlias}|${id}|${type}` lets the same id exist as two different custom models under two different types (e.g. llm vs embedding) for the same provider without colliding
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (providerAlias or id missing)

### /api/models/disabled — per-provider disable/enable list with an atomic merge inside a DB transaction

- **id:** `catalog.model-disabled-crud-api` · **module:** `catalog`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard "hide model" toggle
- **Input:** POST { providerAlias, ids }; DELETE ?providerAlias=&id=
- **Output:** { success: true } or a 400/500 error body
- **Rules:**
  - disableModels merges new ids into the existing array via new Set([...current, ...ids]) dedup, entirely inside a single db.transaction (no JS yield mid-transaction) — two concurrent disable calls for the same provider cannot lose one caller's ids to a race
  - enableModels with an empty resulting list DELETEs the row entirely rather than storing an empty array, avoiding an ever-growing table of empty rows
  - DELETE with no ?id= param passes an empty ids array into enableModels, which is the same 'clear the whole provider's disabled list' code path as an id-array wipe — 'remove one id' and 'clear everything' share one function, distinguished only by the argument
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (providerAlias missing on GET/DELETE, or providerAlias/ids[] missing on POST)

### /v1/models replaces the static per-provider model list with a live per-connection fetch when available, falling back to static on failure

- **id:** `catalog.model-listing-live-override` · **module:** `catalog`
- **Trigger:** GET /v1/models (or /v1/models/{kind})
- **Input:** none — reads the caller's own active provider connections
- **Output:** OpenAI-format { object:"list", data:[{ id, object, owned_by, capabilities?, context_length?, max_completion_tokens? }] }
- **Rules:**
  - Only the FIRST active connection per provider id feeds the listing (activeConnectionByProvider Map keyed by provider, first-write-wins) — a second account on the same provider with a different enabledModels allow-list or live catalog is invisible to /v1/models even though account-selection/fallback can still dispatch chat requests to it
  - For providers in LIVE_MODEL_RESOLVERS (kiro, qoder, kimchi, github, clinepass, grok-cli, cursor, zed — chosen because they return per-account dynamic model variants) a successful live fetch REPLACES rawModelIds outright rather than merging with PROVIDER_MODELS; on a thrown error, or when the connection has an explicit providerSpecificData.enabledModels allow-list, it falls back to that instead
  - OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible custom providers with zero static or enabled models call fetchCompatibleModelIds to hit the account's own {baseUrl}/models endpoint directly — a second, independent live-list source with its own 5s timeout and a recursion-guard header for chained 9router-to-9router calls
  - Live-catalog entries usually carry only { id, name } — no capability metadata — so context_length/max_completion_tokens are backfilled from the same static getCapabilitiesForModel(provider, modelId) pattern table used for static models, specifically so a live 372K-context model isn't guessed at a larger static default and silently overruns upstream
- **Errors:** `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (a live resolver throws or returns no models)

### providerModelsFetcher.js — dashboard-only "suggested models" fetch, cached 10 minutes, never consulted for validity or routing

- **id:** `catalog.model-live-vendor-fetch-ui-only` · **module:** `catalog`
- **Trigger:** Opening a provider's detail page in the dashboard when the provider registry entry declares a modelsFetcher
- **Input:** { url, type } from PROVIDER_MEDIA[id].modelsFetcher
- **Output:** array of { id, name, contextLength? } suggestions rendered in the 'add model' UI
- **Rules:**
  - fetchSuggestedModels proxies through /api/providers/suggested-models (server-side, avoiding browser CORS) and caches the result in an in-memory Map keyed by fetcher.url for 10 minutes
  - This is the ONLY call site of fetchSuggestedModels in the codebase — it feeds a dropdown of suggestions when an operator adds a custom model; it never writes into PROVIDER_MODELS, never affects isValidModel, and is never consulted on the chat/routing path
  - When a vendor's live list disagrees with the static PROVIDER_MODELS table (a reseller like openrouter/venice/tokenrouter ships a new model id before registry/*.js is regenerated), the disagreement is invisible to the router: isOpenAICompatibleProvider/passthrough providers already accept any model id unconditionally (isValidModel short-circuits to true), while a non-passthrough provider with a curated static list simply never offers the live-only id as a request-ready alias anywhere except this manual suggestion box — an operator must explicitly register it via /api/models/custom (catalog.model-custom-registration) before it becomes routable through the alias/model-list path
- **Errors:** `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (the proxy fetch fails or returns a non-OK response)

### PROVIDER_MODELS / AI_MODELS are a single global, per-process table — not scoped per connection or account

- **id:** `catalog.model-registry-global` · **module:** `catalog`
- **Trigger:** Any lookup of a provider's static model list (getProviderModels/isValidModel/getModelsByProviderId, or a page building /api/models)
- **Input:** providerAlias or providerId
- **Output:** array of model descriptor objects { id, name, kind?, ... } — identical for every connection to that provider
- **Rules:**
  - PROVIDER_MODELS is imported directly from open-sse/providers/index.js (built once from the static REGISTRY at module load — see catalog.registry-build in 02-providers-auth.yaml) and re-exported verbatim by open-sse/config/providerModels.js and src/shared/constants/models.js; there is no per-connection or per-account copy of it
  - AI_MODELS (src/shared/constants/models.js) is a flat array built once via Object.entries(PROVIDER_MODELS).flatMap — every account/connection to the same provider sees the identical static list
  - getModelsByProviderId/getProviderModels index the table by provider ALIAS, not by connection id — two connections to the same provider (e.g. two separate OpenAI accounts) resolve to the exact same PROVIDER_MODELS[alias] array reference

### GET /v1/models/{kind} and GET /v1/models/{provider}/{model} — kind-filtered listing and single-model lookup on the OpenAI-compatible lane

- **id:** `catalog.v1-single-model-lookup` · **module:** `catalog`
- **Trigger:** A client GETs /v1/models/<something> — either one of the 6 known kind slugs (image/tts/stt/embedding/image-to-text/web) or a provider/model id
- **Input:** Catch-all path segments after /v1/models/
- **Output:** A kind slug returns { object: list, data:[...] } (same shape as GET /v1/models, filtered); anything else returns the single matching model object, or a 404 model_not_found error body
- **Rules:**
  - A single path segment is checked against KIND_SLUG_MAP first; only on a miss does the route treat the full joined path as a provider/model identifier — so a kind name can never be misread as a literal model id, and a model id colliding with a kind slug is the only ambiguous case
  - The single-model lookup path reuses buildModelsList([LLM_KIND]) (the same list catalog.model-listing-live-override builds for GET /v1/models) and does a linear find() by id — no separate single-model resolution logic, so it inherits every filter that list already applies: active-connection scoping, enabledModels allowlisting, and isDisabled hiding (catalog.alias-disabled-model-bypass's finding that this filtering exists only in listing endpoints, never the chat/routing path, means this lookup correctly hides a disabled model exactly like the plain list does)
  - The catch-all param is required (rather than a single dynamic segment) specifically because provider-prefixed model ids contain a slash (e.g. openai/gpt-4)
- **Errors:** `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` (the joined identifier matches neither a kind slug nor any id in the LLM-kind model list)

## Multi-account

### In-memory Antigravity live-quota cache that pre-filters accounts before a request is even attempted

- **id:** `account.antigravity-quota-prefilter` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** getProviderCredentials() for provider antigravity with a model specified; the cache is populated/updated separately whenever a live 409/429 occurs
- **Input:** connectionId, model; cache keyed connectionId -> { [model]: { remainingPercentage, resetAt } }
- **Output:** A connection is excluded from availableConnections if its cached entry for that model shows remainingPercentage <= 0 and an unexpired resetAt
- **Rules:**
