  - The cache is lazy: getAntigravityQuotaCache() is only consulted, never proactively populated, by the selection filter — a connection with no cache entry yet (cold start, or never having hit 409/429) is always let through regardless of its true upstream quota state
  - The cache lives entirely in process memory (a module-scope Map in antigravityQuota.js, not global._-prefixed), separate from the persisted modelLock_* mechanism — a cache hit skips upstream calls without ever writing a DB lock, so this filtering is invisible to any code that only inspects the connection row
  - A strike-based circuit breaker layered on top of the same cache (STRIKE_THRESHOLD=3 429s within a 60s window) additionally blocks a connection+model pair for 15 minutes when the optimistic quota reading disagrees with repeated live 429s — this is a second, independent reason a connection can be filtered here beyond the plain remainingPercentage<=0 check
- **Note:** 9router's mechanism here is an accident of its stack. Behavior required, mechanism not.

### Whether two concurrent requests against the same connection can both trigger a token refresh

- **id:** `account.concurrent-refresh-race` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** Two client requests routed to the same provider+model close enough together that both select the same connection (most likely under fill-first, the default strategy) while its token is expired or the upstream returns 401/403
- **Input:** Two independent in-memory credentials snapshots for the same connectionId, each captured by a separate call to getProviderCredentials/checkAndRefreshToken
- **Output:** Both requests independently call the provider's refresh endpoint with their own copy of refreshToken; for providers whose refresh token is single-use and rotates on every call, the second call's refresh fails
- **Rules:**
  - There is no per-connection refresh lock anywhere in this path: getProviderCredentials()'s selectionMutex only wraps the SELECTION step and releases before the caller even starts using the credentials (see account.select-mutex-global-scope) — nothing serializes the subsequent refresh-and-retry, at either the proactive layer (checkAndRefreshToken, called unconditionally after every selection in src/sse/handlers/chat.js line 253) or the reactive layer (chatCore.js's 401/403 handler, line 402)
  - Fill-first (the default strategy) always returns the same top-priority connection to every concurrent caller as long as it's available — it does not mark a connection 'checked out', so two requests arriving within the same tens-of-milliseconds window before either has refreshed routinely receive identical credentials.refreshToken values
  - Each caller mutates only its own local `credentials` object across refreshWithRetry's internal retry attempts (chatCore.js lines 404-413, explicitly commented as fixing rotation WITHIN one call's own retries) — this local mutation does nothing for a second, separate concurrent request, which still holds the pre-refresh refreshToken value it captured at selection time
  - The DB write itself (updateProviderCredentials -> connectionsRepo.updateProviderConnection) is atomic per call (read-merge-write inside one db.transaction), so the stored row is never corrupted — the race is entirely about which in-memory refreshToken each concurrent request's refresh call sends upstream, not about a corrupted database write
- **Errors:** `AUTH_ERROR` (a provider with single-use rotating refresh tokens (the code names xAI/grok-cli explicitly) receives a second concurrent refresh call using a refreshToken already consumed by the first — the provider returns invalid_grant and refreshWithRetry's 3 attempts all fail on the stale token)
- **AIGate required behavior:** Two concurrent requests hitting an expired/rejected token on the same connection should converge on one valid refreshed token — either serialized so the second reuses the first's fresh token, or each refresh is independently idempotent regardless of which refreshToken value it started from

### Distinguishing 'no accounts configured' from 'all accounts temporarily locked', with retry-after computed from the earliest lock

- **id:** `account.select-all-unavailable-response` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** getProviderCredentials() finds availableConnections.length === 0 after filtering
- **Input:** connections (the pre-filter list, still containing the locked ones)
- **Output:** Either { allRateLimited: true, retryAfter, retryAfterHuman, lastError, lastErrorCode } when at least one connection has a computable future expiry, or plain null when connections exist but none carry an expiry (or there were zero connections to begin with)
- **Rules:**
  - The earliest expiry is computed across two independent sources merged into one list: modelLock_* expiries (getEarliestModelLockUntil per locked connection) and, for Antigravity, live quota-cache resetAt entries that are still in the future — the two are concatenated and sorted lexicographically (ISO-8601 strings sort correctly this way) before taking [0]
  - lastError/lastErrorCode on the allRateLimited response come from lockedConns[0] (the first connection found to be locked in filter order), not necessarily the connection with the earliest expiry — the displayed error message and the displayed retry-after can reference two different accounts
  - connections.length === 0 (no rows for the provider at all) returns plain null, same as 'all locked but no computable expiry' — callers distinguish 'never configured' from 'temporarily exhausted' only via the allRateLimited flag being absent in both cases, by checking excludeConnectionIds.size at the call site (src/sse/handlers/chat.js line 244) rather than anything in this function's return value
- **Errors:** `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (all accounts for the provider are model-locked (or, for Antigravity, quota-cache-blocked) with a computable future expiry), `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (no accounts exist for the provider at all, or none of the locked accounts carry a computable expiry)

### fill-first strategy — the default when no round-robin override applies

- **id:** `account.select-fill-first-default` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** getProviderCredentials() reaches strategy selection with no preferredConnectionId match and settings.fallbackStrategy (or providerOverride.fallbackStrategy) not equal to \"round-robin\"
- **Input:** availableConnections (already priority-sorted by getProviderConnections)
- **Output:** availableConnections[0] — the lowest-priority-number available connection
- **Rules:**
  - fill-first does no work of its own: it relies entirely on getProviderConnections() already returning the list sorted by ascending priority (connectionsRepo.js line 79), so 'fill-first' means 'always try the highest-priority account that is currently available, only overflow to the next when the first is excluded/locked'
  - fill-first never writes lastUsedAt or consecutiveUseCount — those fields are round-robin-only bookkeeping
  - Per-provider strategy override (settings.providerStrategies[providerId].fallbackStrategy) takes precedence over the global settings.fallbackStrategy, which itself defaults to "fill-first" when unset

### Filtering candidates by exclude-set, active model lock, and (Antigravity only) cached live quota before any strategy runs

- **id:** `account.select-locked-and-excluded-filter` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** Every getProviderCredentials() call, right after connections are loaded, before fill-first/round-robin/pin decide among what's left
- **Input:** connections (isActive=true rows for the provider); excludeConnectionIds; model; for antigravity, the in-process quota cache
- **Output:** availableConnections — the subset eligible for this attempt
- **Rules:**
  - A connection is dropped if its id is in excludeSet (the caller's retry-with-next-account list), OR isModelLockActive(c, model) is true (an unexpired modelLock_${model} or the account-wide modelLock___all key), OR — Antigravity + model only — the in-memory quota cache says remainingPercentage <= 0 and resetAt is still in the future for that exact model
  - isModelLockActive checks the model-specific key first, falling back to the account-wide '__all' key — either being unexpired blocks the connection for that model
  - The Antigravity quota-cache check is a pure pre-filter: it never touches the DB and is populated lazily only after that account has already returned a 409/429 once (see account.antigravity-quota-prefilter) — a cold cache lets an about-to-fail account through until the first real failure updates the cache

### Mutex scope around getProviderCredentials

- **id:** `account.select-mutex-global-scope` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** Every call to getProviderCredentials() — one call per account-selection attempt on any /v1 lane, for any provider
- **Input:** provider, excludeConnectionIds, model, options.preferredConnectionId
- **Output:** A selected credentials object, an allRateLimited descriptor, or null — see the other account.select-* entries
- **Rules:**
  - selectionMutex is a single module-scope `let`, not keyed by provider or connection — every call to getProviderCredentials, for every provider, awaits the same chained Promise before doing anything else, and the whole function body (DB reads, settings read, and for round-robin the updateProviderConnection write) runs inside the held mutex
  - The actual invariant that needs protecting is per-provider: round-robin's 'pick least-recently-used' read-then-write (lines 154-189) races if two concurrent picks for the SAME provider both read stale lastUsedAt before either writes it back, potentially double-assigning the same account. A per-connection or per-provider mutex would close that race; a single global mutex additionally serializes selection across every unrelated provider in the process
- **Note:** 9router's mechanism here is an accident of its stack. Behavior required, mechanism not.

### "Public" virtual connection injected for noAuth providers

- **id:** `account.select-noauth-virtual-connection` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** getProviderCredentials() called for a provider whose FREE_PROVIDERS entry has noAuth true
- **Input:** provider id; settings.providerStrategies[providerId].rotateStrategy and .proxyPoolId; active proxy pools
- **Output:** A synthetic credentials object — id "noauth", connectionName "Public", accessToken the literal string "public", no real token fields at all
- **Rules:**
  - noAuth providers never read the providerConnections table — there is no stored connection to select, so the function short-circuits before getProviderConnections() is even called
  - Instead of a credential, the virtual connection carries proxy configuration: a rotateStrategy ("none"/round-robin/random, defaulting to "none") picks a proxyPoolId from the provider's active pools via pickProxyPoolId(), then resolveConnectionProxyConfig() resolves the actual proxy URL/no-proxy list/Vercel relay URL into providerSpecificData
  - accessToken: "public" is a placeholder token, never sent upstream as a real bearer credential — executors for noAuth providers must not treat it as one

### options.preferredConnectionId pins selection to one connection, bypassing fill-first/round-robin

- **id:** `account.select-preferred-pin` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** Caller of getProviderCredentials() passes { preferredConnectionId } and that connection is in availableConnections
- **Input:** options.preferredConnectionId
- **Output:** The matching connection object, or falls through to the normal strategy if not found/not available
- **Rules:**
  - The pin is a soft preference, not a hard requirement: availableConnections.find() only searches already-filtered (non-excluded, non-locked) connections, so a locked or excluded preferred connection silently falls through to fill-first/round-robin rather than erroring
  - When the pin succeeds, neither lastUsedAt nor consecutiveUseCount is touched — round-robin bookkeeping is skipped entirely for a pinned selection, so a pinned request does not affect subsequent round-robin rotation state

### Round-robin strategy with sticky-session limit, and what clears stickiness

- **id:** `account.select-round-robin-sticky` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** getProviderCredentials() reaches strategy selection, no preferredConnectionId match, and the effective fallbackStrategy is \"round-robin\"
- **Input:** availableConnections; providerOverride.stickyRoundRobinLimit or settings.stickyRoundRobinLimit (default 3)
- **Output:** Either the same connection as last time (sticky continuation) or the least-recently-used available connection (rotation), with lastUsedAt/consecutiveUseCount updated in the DB before returning
- **Rules:**
  - availableConnections is sorted by lastUsedAt descending to find the 'current' candidate — the most recently used connection is the sticky candidate, not an explicit session id
  - Sticky continuation condition: current exists AND current.lastUsedAt is set AND current.consecutiveUseCount < stickyLimit — while true, the same connection keeps being returned and consecutiveUseCount increments by 1 each call
  - Stickiness clears in exactly one way: once consecutiveUseCount reaches stickyLimit, the else branch runs instead — it re-sorts availableConnections by lastUsedAt ascending (oldest/never-used first, using priority as a tiebreak for two never-used connections) and picks that one, resetting consecutiveUseCount to 1 for the new connection. A never-used connection (no lastUsedAt) is also picked over any used one, since !a.lastUsedAt sorts it first in the ascending sort
  - Locking a connection out of availableConnections (model lock or exclude-set) also implicitly breaks stickiness: if the current sticky connection becomes unavailable, it is filtered out upstream and round-robin's 'current' becomes whichever remaining connection has the most recent lastUsedAt
  - Both the stick-with-current and the rotate-to-oldest branches await updateProviderConnection() before returning, so the DB write for bookkeeping happens synchronously with selection, not fire-and-forget

## OAuth providers

### Browser-assisted desktop login start and status polling

- **id:** `connection.xiaomi-mimo-login-session` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** POST /api/oauth/xiaomi-mimo/login/start, then GET /api/oauth/xiaomi-mimo/login/status
- **Input:** Start { region? }; status query state plus httpOnly 9r_mimo_login cookie
- **Output:** Start { success, state, pageUrl, region }; status pending/done/expired/error with identity only on done
- **Rules:**
  - Start restricts region to cn/sgp/ams/ru/in, probes a local HTTP proxy for non-CN egress, follows two upstream redirects, then returns a same-origin login page path.
  - Session state and upstream cookie jar ride an httpOnly 15-minute cookie, not the URL. Status checks the state, refreshes the cookie while pending, returns passToken identity once done, then clears the cookie.
  - A completed browser login only yields identity; saving a provider connection is a separate import step.
- **Errors:** `AUTH_ERROR` (session cookie absent or state mismatch; status returns expired/404), `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (upstream redirect chain lacks expected locations; start returns 502)

### POST /api/oauth/codex/bulk-import — import many pre-obtained codex OAuth token JSON blobs in one call

- **id:** `oauth.codex-bulk-import` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** Operator pastes an array (or single object, or {accounts:[...]}) of previously-exported codex account JSON into the bulk-import UI
- **Input:** Array | single object | { accounts: [...] } — each item needs at least accessToken; email/chatgptAccountId/chatgptPlanType are optional
- **Output:** { success, failed, results: [{ index, ok, id? , error? }] } — one outcome per input item, never a single all-or-nothing result
- **Rules:**
  - The generic [provider]/[action] exchange/poll routes only ever create ONE connection per call, driven by an interactive browser/device flow; bulk-import exists specifically because an operator migrating N already-authenticated codex accounts (e.g. from another tool's local storage) has no authorization code or device code to feed the generic route at all — only the resulting token JSON
  - The import loop is intentionally SERIAL, not Promise.all — the code comment explains createProviderConnection reads max(priority) and reorders rows inside a transaction, so parallel calls would race on priority assignment
  - Server-controlled fields (id, provider, authType, createdAt, updatedAt) are stripped from each incoming item before it's merged into the createProviderConnection call, so a malicious or stale export can't set its own id or spoof authType
  - Missing email/chatgptAccountId/chatgptPlanType are best-effort backfilled per item from the JWT in idToken (or accessToken if no idToken) via extractCodexAccountInfo — a failure to decode just leaves those fields absent rather than failing the item
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (body is not valid JSON, or normalizes to an empty/non-array account list), `INVALID_REQUEST` (an individual item is not an object or is missing accessToken)

### POST /api/oauth/codex/import-token — import a single ChatGPT access token, bypassing the OAuth refresh flow entirely

- **id:** `oauth.codex-import-token` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** Operator pastes a ChatGPT access token (created from chatgpt.com account settings) into the import UI
- **Input:** { accessToken, name? }
- **Output:** { success, connection: { id, provider, email, name, workspace, plan } }
- **Rules:**
  - The generic route's exchange action needs an authorization code + PKCE verifier from a live browser redirect; this route exists because a chatgpt.com-issued access token has neither — it is a standalone bearer credential the user copies manually, with no refresh token and no OAuth handshake to perform
  - The connection is stored with authType: "access_token" (not "oauth") specifically because there is no refreshToken to pair with it — refreshCredentials()'s early `if (!credentials.refreshToken) return null` guard means this connection can never be silently refreshed; it must be re-imported by hand once it expires
  - Email/workspace/plan are extracted by manually base64-decoding the JWT's middle segment and reading either the OpenAI-specific `https://api.openai.com/auth` / `.../profile` claims or top-level account_id/plan_type/email fields, with extractCodexAccountInfo as a fallback if that manual decode doesn't yield an email — the same dual-decode strategy the generic route's raw-JWT exchange shortcut also implements independently
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (accessToken is missing or not a string), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (createProviderConnection throws)

### GET /api/oauth/cursor/auto-import — auto-detect and read Cursor IDE's own locally-stored access token from its SQLite state DB

- **id:** `oauth.cursor-auto-import` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** Operator clicks \"Auto-detect from Cursor\" in the dashboard connect flow
- **Input:** none (reads local filesystem only)
- **Output:** { found: true, accessToken, machineId } | { found: false, error } | { found: false, windowsManual: true, dbPath }
- **Rules:**
  - This route makes ZERO network calls to Cursor or any OAuth endpoint — it locates Cursor's own state.vscdb SQLite file (platform-specific candidate paths for darwin/win32/linux) and reads two keys out of its itemTable: cursorAuth/accessToken (or the legacy cursorAuth/token) and one of three machine-id keys — because Cursor has no public OAuth authorize/token endpoint the generic route could call at all
  - Extraction is tried via three strategies in order: better-sqlite3 (bundled native binding) first, then a shell-out to the sqlite3 CLI if the native binding is unavailable, then falls back to `{ found:false, windowsManual:true }` asking the user to paste values manually — the generic route has no equivalent multi-strategy local-file-read fallback chain
  - On Linux specifically, the route additionally verifies Cursor is actually installed (`which cursor` or a .desktop file) before attempting extraction, to avoid treating leftover config from an uninstalled Cursor as a valid source
- **Errors:** `INTERNAL_ERROR` (no candidate state.vscdb path is readable on this machine)

### POST /api/oauth/cursor/import — validate a manually-supplied (or auto-detected) Cursor accessToken+machineId pair and persist it

- **id:** `oauth.cursor-import` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** Submission of the accessToken+machineId pair, whether hand-pasted or pre-filled by oauth.cursor-auto-import
- **Input:** { accessToken, machineId }
- **Output:** { success, connection: { id, provider, email } }
- **Rules:**
  - machineId is a required, separate credential component alongside accessToken — Cursor's API validates the pair together (CursorService.validateImportToken makes the actual upstream API call to confirm the token is live), unlike a normal OAuth exchange where only the token/code matters
  - refreshToken is explicitly stored as null with the comment "Cursor doesn't have public refresh endpoint" — this connection can never be silently refreshed by any of the auth.refresh-* mechanisms; expiresAt is set from the validated token's own expiresIn
  - GET on the same route (no body) returns static instructions + a requiredFields schema for the dashboard's manual-entry form — the generic route has no equivalent self-describing GET for a specific credential-pair form
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (accessToken or machineId missing/not a string), `AUTH_ERROR` (CursorService.validateImportToken rejects the pair)

### The generic /api/oauth/[provider]/[action] route — authorize/device-code/exchange/poll and proxy-session actions shared across most OAuth providers

- **id:** `oauth.generic-provider-action-route` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard \"Connect\" flow for any OAuth-category provider not covered by a specific route
- **Input:** provider + action path params; GET query params (redirect_uri, state, app_port, start_url, region, ...) or POST JSON body (code, redirectUri, codeVerifier, state, deviceCode, extraData, meta)
- **Output:** authorize -> { authUrl, codeVerifier, state, ... }; device-code -> { deviceCode, userCode, verificationUri, codeVerifier }; exchange/poll -> { success, connection } on success, a new providerConnections row created
- **Rules:**
  - One handler serves every provider whose OAuth mechanics fit one of: authorization_code+PKCE (exchange), device_code (device-code + poll), or a local-proxy callback (start-proxy/poll-status/stop-proxy/register-session, used by codex/xai/trae/windsurf/zed) — provider-specific quirks are handled by small inline branches (noPkceDeviceProviders, noPkceExchangeProviders lists) rather than per-provider files
  - exchange auto-detects a raw ChatGPT JWT access token pasted as `code` (starts with "eyJ" and contains a ".") and short-circuits straight to creating an access_token-authType connection, decoding the JWT for email/account/plan — this is the same JWT-decode logic codex/import-token also implements independently (see oauth.codex-import-token)
  - poll's noPkceProviders list (github, kimi, kimi-coding, kilocode, codebuddy-cn, codebuddy-intl) and kiro/qoder need special-cased extraData/codeVerifier handling that this single handler absorbs inline rather than delegating
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (action is not one of the recognized values), `INVALID_REQUEST` (poll/exchange is missing deviceCode/code/redirectUri/codeVerifier as required for that provider's flow), `AUTH_ERROR` (poll returns authorization_pending/slow_down (surfaced as pending:true, not a hard error))

### POST /api/oauth/grok-cli/bulk-import — import many pre-obtained Grok CLI (device-code) account JSON objects in one call

- **id:** `oauth.grok-cli-bulk-import` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** Operator pastes an array/single-object/{accounts:[...]} of previously-obtained grok-cli token JSON
- **Input:** Each item accepts BOTH snake_case (access_token, refresh_token, id_token, expires_in) and camelCase (accessToken, refreshToken, idToken, expiresIn) field names, plus email
- **Output:** { total, success, failed, results: [{ index, ok, id?, email?, error? }] }
- **Rules:**
  - Same rationale as oauth.codex-bulk-import: grok-cli tokens are normally obtained through the generic route's device-code + poll actions one at a time; this route exists for migrating already-obtained tokens (e.g. from another local tool's storage) where there is no device code to poll, only the resulting token JSON, and the source JSON's casing convention is unknown up front so both are accepted
  - email is resolved through a three-step fallback: the item's own email field, else decodeXaiIdTokenEmail(idToken), else extractEmailFromAccessToken(accessToken) — unlike codex-bulk-import which relies solely on extractCodexAccountInfo
  - Unlike codex-bulk-import, this loop is not explicitly commented as serial-for-priority-race reasons, but is still a plain sequential for-loop calling createProviderConnection one item at a time
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (body is not valid JSON, or normalizes to an empty account list), `INVALID_REQUEST` (an individual item is not an object or is missing access_token/accessToken)

### GET /api/oauth/kiro/auto-import — auto-detect a Kiro refresh token from the local AWS SSO cache, including IDC client-credential resolution

- **id:** `oauth.kiro-auto-import` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** Operator clicks \"Auto-detect from Kiro IDE\" in the connect UI
- **Input:** none (reads local filesystem only)
- **Output:** { found, refreshToken, source, clientId, clientSecret, region, authMethod, profileArn }
- **Rules:**
  - This route makes zero network calls — it reads ~/.aws/sso/cache, first checking a known kiro-auth-token.json filename, then scanning every other .json file in that directory for one whose refreshToken starts with the literal prefix "aorAAAAAG" (Kiro's own token format marker) — the generic route has no equivalent local-cache-scan capability
  - For IDC (organization) tokens specifically, the cached token file references a clientIdHash; this route resolves that hash to a second cache file ({hash}.json) to recover the clientId/clientSecret needed to refresh an IDC token via the regional AWS OIDC endpoint — a social/builder-id token has no such linkage and is refreshed differently (see oauth.kiro-import)
  - profileArn is read from a separate Kiro-IDE-specific profile.json (checked at two OS-dependent candidate paths) and its region is force-normalized to us-east-1 in the ARN string regardless of the IDC region, because the comment states the runtime gateway requires us-east-1 in the ARN specifically
- **Errors:** `INTERNAL_ERROR` (~/.aws/sso/cache does not exist (readdir throws))

### POST /api/oauth/kiro/import — persist a manually-supplied (or auto-detected) Kiro refresh token, supporting both social/builder-id and IDC (org) shapes

- **id:** `oauth.kiro-import` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** Submission of a refreshToken (and, for IDC accounts, clientId/clientSecret/region), whether hand-pasted or pre-filled by oauth.kiro-auto-import
- **Input:** { refreshToken, clientId?, clientSecret?, region?, authMethod?, profileArn? }
- **Output:** { success, connection: { id, provider, email } }
- **Rules:**
  - isIdc = !!(clientId && clientSecret) branches the entire flow: IDC (organization) tokens refresh via the regional AWS OIDC endpoint using those client credentials, while social/builder-id tokens use Kiro's own standard social refresh endpoint with no client credentials — the same route handles both shapes rather than splitting into two routes, because both ultimately produce the same kiro-provider connection shape
  - kiroService.refreshToken is called immediately during import (not deferred to the first real chat request) specifically to validate the supplied refreshToken actually works and to obtain a fresh accessToken/expiresIn/profileArn before ever persisting the connection
  - profileArn is resolved with a specific precedence: the client-supplied profileArn body field first, then whatever kiroService.refreshToken's response returned, else null — allowing an auto-imported profileArn (from oauth.kiro-auto-import's separate profile.json read) to be threaded through even though the refresh call itself may not return one
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (refreshToken is missing/not a string), `AUTH_ERROR` (kiroService.refreshToken rejects the supplied token/client credentials)

### POST /api/oauth/kiro/import-cli-proxy — import a CLIProxyAPI auth JSON blob for Kiro Microsoft external_idp accounts

- **id:** `oauth.kiro-import-cli-proxy` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** Operator pastes a CLIProxyAPI-format auth JSON (a third-party tool's exported Kiro credential) for a Microsoft-external-identity Kiro account
- **Input:** { cliProxyAuth } | { auth } | { json } | a bare object — the route accepts several wrapper key names
- **Output:** { success, connection: { id, provider, email } }
- **Rules:**
  - This route exists because Kiro accounts authenticated via Microsoft's external_idp path produce a token JSON shape specific to the CLIProxyAPI tool, not the shape either the generic route's exchange action or oauth.kiro-import's manual refresh-token import expect — normalizeKiroExternalIdpAuth() is the dedicated shape-adapter for this one source format
  - The route accepts the payload under any of four different top-level key names (cliProxyAuth, auth, json, or no wrapper at all) via a single nullish-coalescing chain, tolerating whatever shape the pasting tool happens to wrap its export in
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (normalizeKiroExternalIdpAuth throws on an unrecognized/malformed shape)

### GET /api/oauth/kiro/social-authorize — build a Google/GitHub social-login URL using Kiro's kiro:// custom protocol callback

- **id:** `oauth.kiro-social-authorize` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** Operator picks \"Sign in with Google\" or \"Sign in with GitHub\" for Kiro in the connect UI
- **Input:** ?provider=google|github query param
- **Output:** { authUrl, state, codeVerifier, codeChallenge, provider }
- **Rules:**
  - The generic route's authorize action builds a redirect_uri from a plain HTTP query param intended for a normal browser-redirect OAuth flow; Kiro's social login instead requires a kiro:// custom URL protocol callback (kiro://kiro.kiroAgent/authenticate-success?code=...&state=...) mandated by AWS Cognito's config for this specific identity provider chain, which the generic route's redirect_uri handling has no special case for
  - Only "google" and "github" are accepted as the provider query param — any other value is rejected before any URL is built or PKCE material generated
  - codeVerifier is generated and returned directly in the JSON response (not stored server-side) — the client is responsible for holding onto it and passing it back unchanged to oauth.kiro-social-exchange
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (provider is missing or not google/github)

### POST /api/oauth/kiro/social-exchange — exchange the kiro:// callback code for tokens after Google/GitHub social login

- **id:** `oauth.kiro-social-exchange` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** The dashboard captures the kiro:// custom-protocol redirect and extracts code/state from it, then calls this route
- **Input:** { code, codeVerifier, provider }
- **Output:** { success, connection: { id, provider, email } }
- **Rules:**
  - This is the exchange counterpart to oauth.kiro-social-authorize — it cannot use the generic route's exchange action because that action expects a standard redirectUri to be supplied and re-validated, while this flow's redirect_uri is the fixed kiro:// callback handled internally inside kiroService.exchangeSocialCode rather than passed per-request
  - provider (google|github) is stored verbatim (capitalized) into providerSpecificData.provider and also as providerSpecificData.authMethod — used later purely as a display/diagnostic label distinguishing which social identity produced this Kiro connection, not as a functional branch in the refresh path (auth.refresh-provider-specific's refreshKiro treats every Kiro connection identically regardless of how it was obtained)
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (code or codeVerifier missing), `INVALID_REQUEST` (provider is missing or not google/github), `AUTH_ERROR` (kiroService.exchangeSocialCode rejects the code/verifier pair)

## Provider account management

### clearAccountError — lazy cleanup of expired locks and conditional error-state reset on a successful request

- **id:** `account.clear-error-on-success` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** A request against a connection+model succeeds (called from the handler's onRequestSuccess callback, e.g. src/sse/handlers/chat.js)
- **Input:** connectionId, currentConnection (a credentials object carrying _connection, or a raw connection row), model
- **Output:** An updateProviderConnection() call clearing the succeeded model's lock plus any already-expired locks, and — only if no active lock remains — resetting testStatus/lastError/errorCode/lastErrorAt/backoffLevel
- **Rules:**
  - Early exit: if the connection has no testStatus, no lastError, and zero modelLock_* keys at all, nothing is written — clearAccountError is a no-op on an already-clean connection
  - keysToClear = every modelLock_* key that either (a) is the exact key for the model that just succeeded, (b) is the account-wide modelLock___all key (cleared whenever ANY model succeeds, since an account-wide lock blocks every model), or (c) has already expired (expiry <= now) — this is the 'lazy-cleans any other expired modelLock_* keys' sweep, opportunistic on every success rather than on a timer
  - testStatus/lastError/errorCode/lastErrorAt/backoffLevel are reset to their clean values ONLY if remainingActiveLocks (locks not in keysToClear, still unexpired) is empty — a connection that is locked for model A but just succeeded on model B has its modelLock_A key left untouched and its account-level error/backoff state left untouched too, even though model B now works
  - connectionId === "noauth" is a no-op guard, matching markAccountUnavailable's treatment of the virtual Public connection

### Where modelLock_* (and all other per-connection state) is stored, and whether it survives a restart

- **id:** `account.lock-storage-persistence` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** Any read/write of a providerConnections row (selection filter, markAccountUnavailable, clearAccountError)
- **Input:** connectionId
- **Output:** The connection object with dynamically-named modelLock_${model} keys alongside its fixed columns
- **Rules:**
  - providerConnections has a small set of real SQL columns (id, provider, authType, name, email, priority, isActive, createdAt, updatedAt); every other field — including every modelLock_${model} key, since the model name is caller-supplied and unbounded — is folded into a single JSON `data` TEXT column via connToRow's `{ id, provider, ..., ...rest }` destructure, where `rest` is stringified as JSON
  - rowToConn reverses this by parsing `data` first and spreading it, then overwriting with the fixed columns — so a modelLock_* key set by markAccountUnavailable is written into and read back from that JSON blob, not a dedicated schema column, and a lock key can never collide with a real column name since fixed columns are applied last
  - The SQLite file itself (data.sqlite under DATA_DIR/db) is the persistence boundary for all four driver adapters (bun:sqlite, better-sqlite3, node:sqlite, sql.js) — even the pure-JS sql.js fallback, which has no native file handle, debounces writes back to that same file with fs.writeFileSync — so a modelLock_* lock, once its updateProviderConnection() call resolves, survives a process restart under every adapter, not just the native ones

### Every distinct reason markAccountUnavailable() locks an account+model pair, and that reason's expiry rule

- **id:** `account.mark-unavailable-lock-reasons` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** A provider request for a given connection+model fails; the caller (e.g. src/sse/handlers/chat.js) calls markAccountUnavailable(connectionId, status, errorText, provider, model, resetsAtMs)
- **Input:** connectionId, HTTP status, error text/body, provider id, model, optional resetsAtMs (provider-reported exact reset time in ms epoch)
- **Output:** { shouldFallback, cooldownMs } — and, when shouldFallback, a modelLock_${model} (or modelLock___all) field written on the connection row with an ISO expiry
- **Rules:**
  - Precedence when multiple rules could apply: the GitHub monthly case is checked first (via githubMonthlyResetMs), then a caller-supplied future resetsAtMs, then the generic text/status rule table (checkFallbackError) — the first match wins and the others are not evaluated
  - GitHub monthly usage limit: provider resolves to "github", status is exactly 402, and errorText contains "you've reached your additional usage limit for your plan" (case-insensitive) — locks the ACCOUNT-WIDE modelLock___all key (model is forced to null via `githubResetAtMs ? null : model`) until 00:00 UTC on the 1st of the following month, computed with Date.UTC(year, month+1, 1); backoffLevel is reset to 0
  - Provider-supplied exact reset (non-Antigravity, e.g. codex usage_limit_reached): resetsAtMs is in the future — cooldownMs = resetsAtMs - now, but capped at MAX_RATE_LIMIT_COOLDOWN_MS (30 minutes) even if the provider reports a reset many hours away; backoffLevel resets to 0
  - Provider-supplied exact reset, Antigravity: same resetsAtMs path, but the 30-minute cap is explicitly skipped for provider === "antigravity" — the exact resetAt from Google's quota API is honored uncapped, however far in the future
  - Backoff-rate-limit reasons (checkFallbackError, ERROR_RULES text match on "rate limit"/"too many requests"/"quota exceeded"/"capacity"/"overloaded", or HTTP 429): exponential cooldown = min(2000 * 2^(min(backoffLevel+1,15)-1), 300000) ms — i.e. 2s, 4s, 8s... capped at 5 minutes at level 15; backoffLevel is persisted and incremented on each hit
  - Fixed 2-minute cooldown reasons: text "no credentials" or "improperly formed request", or HTTP status 401/402/403/404 — cooldownMs = 120000 flat, backoffLevel unchanged by this rule (no increment field returned, so the existing level carries over on the connection row)
  - Fixed 5-second cooldown: text "request not allowed" — cooldownMs = 5000
  - Default/unmatched: any error not matched by an ERROR_RULES entry gets TRANSIENT_COOLDOWN_MS (30 seconds)
  - Every one of the above locks a model-scoped key modelLock_${model} — never a whole-account flag — except the GitHub monthly case, which is the one reason that explicitly forces the account-wide modelLock___all key regardless of which model triggered it
- **Errors:** `RATE_LIMIT` (text matches rate limit/too many requests/quota exceeded/capacity/overloaded, or status is 429 — exponential backoff), `AUTH_ERROR` (status is 401 or 403, or text contains "no credentials" — fixed 2 minute cooldown), `QUOTA_EXHAUSTED` (status is 402 (payment required) and NOT the GitHub-monthly text match — fixed 2 minute cooldown), `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` (status is 404 — fixed 2 minute cooldown), `INVALID_REQUEST` (text contains "improperly formed request" — fixed 2 minute cooldown), `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (text contains "request not allowed" — fixed 5 second cooldown), `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (no ERROR_RULES entry matches — default 30 second transient cooldown), `QUOTA_EXHAUSTED` (caller supplies a future resetsAtMs for a non-Antigravity provider (e.g. codex usage_limit_reached) — cooldown = resetsAtMs - now, capped at 30 minutes), `QUOTA_EXHAUSTED` (caller supplies a future resetsAtMs for Antigravity — cooldown = resetsAtMs - now, uncapped exact reset), `QUOTA_EXHAUSTED` (GitHub 402 with the additional-usage-limit-for-your-plan message — locked account-wide until the 1st of next UTC month)

### createProviderConnection — identity-based dedup on re-import, and automatic priority assignment for new connections

- **id:** `connection.create-dedup-and-priority-assignment` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** A new connection is imported/created (OAuth callback, API-key add, access-token add) via createProviderConnection(data)
- **Input:** data.provider, data.authType, data.email, data.name, data.priority, data.providerSpecificData (incl. per-provider identity fields like chatgptAccountId/username/githubLogin)
- **Output:** Either the existing matching connection merged with the incoming data (dedup hit), or a brand-new connection row with an assigned id/name/priority
- **Rules:**
  - Dedup only applies to authType oauth (matched by email, with provider-specific identity tie-breaks) or authType apikey (matched by exact name) — access_token connections are NEVER deduped ('user manages duplicates manually', per the inline comment), so re-adding the same access-token twice always creates a second row
  - OAuth dedup for codex specifically requires BOTH rows to expose the same chatgptAccountId to collapse onto an existing row — this exists because Codex/OpenAI can issue multiple OAuth grants for the same email with single-use refresh tokens, and collapsing a new login onto an existing bare-email row would overwrite the first account's still-valid token pair, silently breaking it
  - Non-Codex workspace providers match on chatgptAccountId when both sides have it; if only one side has it, they're treated as distinct (not deduped). Non-workspace providers fall back to matching on (email + username) requiring both sides to have username, else treated as distinct — the fallback bare-email match only applies when NEITHER side has a username
  - A new connection's priority defaults to max(existing priorities for that provider) + 1 when not explicitly supplied — new accounts are appended to the back of the fill-first queue by default, never inserted ahead of existing ones
  - A dedup hit runs upsert() but skips reorderInTx entirely — priority renumbering only happens for genuinely new connections, not merges

### deleteProviderConnection — row removal followed by a priority renumber for the remaining accounts of that provider

- **id:** `connection.delete-and-reorder` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** DELETE /api/providers/[id] (catalog.connection-detail-crud) or any other caller of deleteProviderConnection(id)
- **Input:** id
- **Output:** true if a row was found and deleted, false if id didn't exist (no error thrown either way)
- **Rules:**
  - The provider id is read from the row being deleted BEFORE the DELETE runs (`SELECT provider FROM ... WHERE id = ?`), so the subsequent reorderInTx(db, row.provider) still knows which provider's remaining connections to renumber even after the row is gone
  - reorderInTx renumbers the survivors to a dense 1..N sequence — deleting priority-2 out of 1/2/3 leaves 1/2 (not 1/3), so priority values are never stable identifiers across deletes, only a live ordering
  - Delete + reorder run inside one db.transaction, same atomicity guarantee as update — no window where the table has a gap in priority numbers visible to a concurrent read
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (id does not correspond to an existing connection)

### The providerConnections row shape — fixed SQL columns vs. an open-ended JSON blob for everything else

- **id:** `connection.storage-shape-json-blob` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** Any read or write of a connection row (rowToConn / connToRow, used by every function in connectionsRepo.js)
- **Input:** A raw SQLite row, or a JS connection object to persist
- **Output:** A JS connection object with all fields flattened to top level, regardless of which storage tier they came from
- **Rules:**
  - Exactly 9 fields are real columns: id, provider, authType, name, email, priority, isActive, createdAt, updatedAt — isActive is stored as SQLite 0/1 and coerced back to boolean on read (row.isActive === 1 || row.isActive === true, the `=== true` arm covering adapters that return native booleans)
  - Everything else a connection carries — accessToken, refreshToken, apiKey, expiresAt, providerSpecificData, testStatus, lastError, backoffLevel, every modelLock_* key, consecutiveUseCount, lastUsedAt, etc. — is opaque JSON in the single `data` column, with no schema enforcement on that blob's shape beyond what application code happens to read/write
  - cleanupProviderConnections() is a maintenance sweep that deletes null/undefined values for a fixed list of known optional fields (and drops an empty providerSpecificData object entirely) from the JSON blob — this is the only place that actively shrinks the blob; nothing else in the repo ever removes a stale key from `data` on its own (matching the modelLock_* accumulation edge case noted in account.lock-storage-persistence)

### updateProviderConnection — atomic read-merge-write per connection, and priority reorder triggered by a priority change

- **id:** `connection.update-atomic-merge-and-reorder` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** Any partial update to a connection — dashboard edit, token refresh write, lock/unlock, round-robin bookkeeping
- **Input:** id, data (any subset of connection fields, including dynamically-named modelLock_* keys)
- **Output:** The merged connection object, or null if id doesn't exist
- **Rules:**
  - The whole operation (SELECT existing row, spread-merge `{ ...existing, ...data }`, UPSERT) runs inside one db.transaction — a concurrent second updateProviderConnection() call for the same id cannot interleave its own read between this call's read and write, because the underlying SQLite driver serializes transactions; this is what makes the modelLock_* read-merge-write safe against corruption even though the JS-level merge logic has no explicit locking of its own
  - reorderInTx (re-numbering every connection's priority for that provider by ascending priority, tie-broken by most-recently-updated first) runs ONLY when data.priority !== undefined — an update that doesn't touch priority never triggers a reorder, so token-refresh/lock writes (which never set priority) are cheaper than a dashboard priority-reorder request
  - A partial update genuinely merges rather than replaces: only keys present in `data` overwrite the existing row's corresponding key, so this is the mechanism that lets markAccountUnavailable set one modelLock_* key without touching any other field, and lets clearAccountError null out only the specific locks it decided to clear
- **Errors:** `INTERNAL_ERROR` (id does not correspond to an existing row — result stays null, no error thrown)

## Provider authentication

### BaseExecutor's own buildHeaders fallback — used by dedicated-executor providers that don't override header construction

- **id:** `auth.base-executor-default-headers` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** A chat request for a provider mapped to a dedicated executor class that inherits BaseExecutor.buildHeaders without overriding it
- **Input:** credentials.apiKey / credentials.accessToken
- **Output:** Authorization: Bearer <token> for most providers; x-api-key (or Bearer if only accessToken present) plus anthropic-version for anthropic-compatible-* provider ids
- **Rules:**
  - BaseExecutor.buildHeaders is a simpler, hardcoded twin of DefaultExecutor's registry-driven buildHeaders — it does not consult transport.auth/AUTH_DESCRIPTORS at all, it only special-cases provider ids starting with "anthropic-compatible-" (x-api-key preferred, Bearer fallback, anthropic-version default) and otherwise always prefers accessToken over apiKey for a plain Bearer header
  - needsRefresh(credentials) delegates to the shared shouldRefreshCredentials(provider, credentials) service for every executor (base and subclasses alike) — refresh-due detection is centralized even though the actual refresh call (refreshCredentials) is overridden per-provider
  - shouldRetry(status, urlIndex) only ever triggers on HTTP 429 and only when another base URL remains in getBaseUrls() — this is the base retry policy every executor inherits unless it overrides shouldRetry itself

### OAUTH_INJECT_FIELDS — clientId/clientSecret/tokenUrl injected from the oauth block, not stored per connection

- **id:** `auth.oauth-client-creds-shared` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** Every provider build pass (catalog.registry-build) and every OAuth token refresh
- **Input:** entry.oauth.clientId / clientSecret / tokenUrl declared once per provider in its registry file
- **Output:** PROVIDERS[id].clientId / .clientSecret / .tokenUrl available on the transport object for executors to read, without duplicating the values in transport
- **Rules:**
  - OAUTH_INJECT_FIELDS = ["clientId", "clientSecret", "tokenUrl"] — buildTransport copies each of these from entry.oauth into the transport object only when the transport object doesn't already define that field itself, so a provider CAN still override one specific field in transport while inheriting the rest from oauth
  - These three fields describe the OAuth application registration (the client_id/client_secret the 9router app itself registered with the upstream, and the token endpoint URL) — they are identical for every connection to that provider, unlike a user's individual accessToken/refreshToken, which is why they live once on the provider's registry entry rather than being duplicated into every providerConnections row
  - Refresh code reads these two ways depending on the path: the generic REFRESH_GRANTS table (open-sse/executors/default.js) reads them off PROVIDER_OAUTH[id] directly (o.clientId, ex.config.clientId for the special-cased gemini id branch); provider-specific refreshers (refreshIflow, refreshKiro, refreshCline, refreshKimi) read PROVIDERS[provider].clientId — i.e. the already-injected transport copy — instead

### Config-driven generic OAuth refresh (REFRESH_GRANTS / refreshFromGrant) for the standard refresh_token grant shape

- **id:** `auth.refresh-generic-grant` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** A chat request whose stored OAuth credential is due for proactive refresh, or fails and needsRefresh signals a retry
- **Input:** credentials.refreshToken; PROVIDER_OAUTH[provider].refresh.{encoding,scope} and .clientId/.tokenUrl
- **Output:** New { accessToken, refreshToken, expiresIn } from the provider's token endpoint, or null on any non-2xx/failure
- **Rules:**
  - REFRESH_GRANTS is built once from Object.entries(PROVIDER_OAUTH).filter(([,o]) => o.refresh) — any provider whose oauth block declares a refresh sub-object gets an entry, independent of whether that provider is ever actually routed through DefaultExecutor
  - The refreshers dispatch map inside refreshCredentials only wires refreshFromGrant for three provider ids explicitly: claude, codex, gemini — every other provider with a REFRESH_GRANTS entry (e.g. gemini-cli, trae, both of which declare oauth.refresh in their own registry files) is never reached through this path because gemini-cli and trae are mapped to their own dedicated executor classes (see auth.transport-auth-custom-executor-override) whose refreshCredentials, if any, is implemented separately
  - gemini itself has no oauth block at all (see auth.oauth-client-creds-shared), so REFRESH_GRANTS.gemini is never actually built despite `gemini` being listed in the refreshers dispatch map and REFRESH_GRANTS.params containing a gemini-specific branch (`id === "gemini" ? {client_id: ex.config.clientId, ...} : ...`) — that branch can only run if PROVIDER_OAUTH.gemini existed with a .refresh block, which it does not in the current registry
  - encoding ("form" vs "json") picks refreshWithForm vs refreshWithJSON — form posts application/x-www-form-urlencoded with grant_type=refresh_token, refresh_token, client_id[, scope]; json posts the same fields as a JSON body
- **Errors:** `AUTH_ERROR` (the refresh endpoint returns a non-ok response (returns null, caller must treat the connection as needing re-auth))
- **Note:** 9router's mechanism here is an accident of its stack. Behavior required, mechanism not.

### Hand-written per-provider refresh methods for providers whose token endpoint doesn't fit the generic grant shape

- **id:** `auth.refresh-provider-specific` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** refreshCredentials() dispatch for iflow, kiro, cline, clinepass, kimi/kimi-coding, or kilocode
- **Input:** credentials.refreshToken, plus provider-specific extras (kimi: providerSpecificData.deviceId)
- **Output:** New { accessToken, refreshToken, expiresIn } shaped per-provider, or null
- **Rules:**
  - refreshIflow sends HTTP Basic auth (base64 clientId:clientSecret) in the Authorization header alongside a form body — the only refresher that authenticates the refresh call itself, rather than just including client_id in the body
  - refreshKiro posts a JSON body ({ refreshToken }) with a hardcoded User-Agent "kiro-cli/1.0.0" to PROVIDERS.kiro.tokenUrl and reads back accessToken/refreshToken/expiresIn in camelCase (not the OAuth-standard access_token/refresh_token/expires_in snake_case every other refresher expects)
  - refreshCline rewrites the returned accessToken to be prefixed "workos:" if it isn't already, and computes expiresIn itself from a returned absolute expiresAt ISO timestamp rather than receiving expires_in directly from the upstream — a response-shape adaptation unique to this provider
  - refreshKimi builds the same buildKimiHeaders(deviceId) fingerprint used on live chat requests (X-Msh-* headers, stable device_id) and sends it on the refresh call too, so refresh looks like it comes from the same device that originally authenticated
  - refreshKilocode always returns null — kilocode's registry comment confirms it uses device-code flow with no refresh-token support at all, so a kilocode credential can never be silently refreshed, only re-imported via a fresh device-code flow
- **Errors:** `AUTH_ERROR` (the provider's refresh endpoint returns a non-ok response)

### transport.auth: { combined: true, header: "Authorization", scheme: "bearer" } — the majority-case header

- **id:** `auth.transport-auth-combined-bearer` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** Any chat request routed through DefaultExecutor for a provider whose transport.auth uses scheme \"bearer\"
- **Input:** credentials.apiKey or credentials.accessToken
- **Output:** Authorization: Bearer <token> header, always set (even when both apiKey and accessToken are absent, producing the literal string "Bearer undefined")
- **Rules:**
  - AUTH_DESCRIPTORS is built once from Object.entries(PROVIDERS).filter(([,t]) => t.auth) — only providers that declare a transport.auth block at all get an entry; providers without one fall through to resolveAuthDescriptor's hardcoded default (also BEARER unless the provider's format is "claude" or its id starts with "anthropic-compatible-")
  - combined:true means a single header always carries whichever of apiKey/accessToken is truthy (apiKey preferred): setAuth always writes the header even if the resulting value is `Bearer undefined` for a misconfigured/noAuth-flagged connection — this is legacy behavior the code comment explicitly calls out as intentional parity with the pre-refactor implementation
  - This is by far the most common shape in the registry — every plain "apikey"-category chat provider that doesn't override format defaults to combined Bearer unless it explicitly declares otherwise

### transport.auth: { combined: true, header: "x-api-key"|other, scheme: "raw" } — token sent unprefixed

- **id:** `auth.transport-auth-combined-raw` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** Any chat request routed through DefaultExecutor for a provider whose transport.auth uses scheme \"raw\"
- **Input:** credentials.apiKey or credentials.accessToken
- **Output:** <header-name>: <token> with no scheme prefix (e.g. x-api-key: sk-... rather than Bearer sk-...)
- **Rules:**
  - setAuth's only branch on scheme is `scheme === "bearer"`; every other scheme value (raw, or a provider-documented custom string like trae's "Cloud-IDE-JWT") is treated identically by the generic path — the header is set to the bare token with no transformation
  - The header name itself varies per provider even within "raw": x-api-key for Anthropic-shaped providers (deepseek's claude-format variant, minimax/minimax-cn/glm/kimi's claude-format variants, kimchi), x-goog-api-key for gemini's split apiKey branch
  - anthropicVersion:true on a descriptor (set alongside scheme:"raw"/header:"x-api-key") makes applyAuth also set anthropic-version if not already present — a second, unconditional side effect of the same descriptor

### transport.auth documented for tooling but bypassed by a provider-specific executor's own buildHeaders

- **id:** `auth.transport-auth-custom-executor-override` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** Any chat request for a provider whose id is mapped to a dedicated executor class in open-sse/executors/index.js
- **Input:** credentials (provider-specific shape)
- **Output:** Headers built entirely by the provider's own buildHeaders override; the registry's transport.auth block is never read for these providers
- **Rules:**
  - getExecutor(provider) returns the mapped dedicated instance (e.g. trae, gemini-cli, kiro, cursor, github, iflow, qoder, ...) when one exists; only providers absent from that map fall through to a cached DefaultExecutor instance — this decides whether AUTH_DESCRIPTORS / applyAuth ever run for a given provider at all
  - trae's registry entry documents scheme: "Cloud-IDE-JWT" purely as a marker for config-driven tooling (its own comment says so) — the real header (`Authorization: Cloud-IDE-JWT <jwt>`) is built by TraeExecutor.buildHeaders, a full override that never calls the shared setAuth/applyAuth helpers
  - zed's registry entry documents scheme: "<user_id> <access_token>" as an explicit placeholder ("real value built in executor") because Zed's Authorization header format is `<user_id> <access_token>` plus a duplicate x-zed-cloud-token header — verified against Zed's own zed_account.rs — which the generic combined/raw setAuth logic cannot express

### transport.auth: { apiKey: {...}, oauth: {...} } — dual-auth providers with a distinct header per credential type

- **id:** `auth.transport-auth-split-branch` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** Any chat request for a provider whose transport.auth declares separate apiKey/oauth sub-descriptors (no top-level combined:true)
- **Input:** credentials.apiKey (preferred) or credentials.accessToken
- **Output:** Only ONE of the two branches' headers is set, chosen by which credential is present — never both
- **Rules:**
  - applyAuth's non-combined branch is a strict either/or: `if (credentials.apiKey) setAuth(headers, desc.apiKey, ...) else if (credentials.accessToken) setAuth(headers, desc.oauth, ...)` — a connection that somehow carries both fields only ever gets the apiKey-shaped header applied
  - claude is the canonical example: apiKey credentials get x-api-key (raw) + anthropic-version, oauth (accessToken) credentials get Authorization Bearer + the same anthropic-version — same upstream API, two different header shapes depending on how the connection was created
  - If neither apiKey nor accessToken is present, this branch sets no auth header at all (unlike the combined branch's always-set-even-if-undefined behavior) — the code comment calls this out explicitly as matching legacy anthropic-compatible skip-when-both-absent behavior

### POST /api/provider-nodes/validate — probe a user-supplied baseUrl+apiKey before a custom provider node is saved

- **id:** `connection.provider-node-validate-partial-ssrf` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard custom-node creation/edit form, on the validate/test step before the node is persisted
- **Input:** { baseUrl, apiKey, type: openai-compatible|anthropic-compatible|custom-embedding, modelId? }
- **Output:** { valid, error?, method?, dimensions? } — 500 with a classified network-error message on a thrown fetch error
- **Rules:**
  - SSRF protection is applied ONLY when isLocalRequest(request) is false — a request from the loopback dashboard UI itself skips the check entirely (deliberate, so a self-hosted target like ollama-local's 127.0.0.1 base URL still validates); a remote caller is checked via ssrfGuard's assertPublicUrl before any fetch happens
  - The SSRF check used here is assertPublicUrl — the synchronous, literal-hostname/IP-only layer described in ssrfGuard.js's own header comment as layer 1 of 3. It does NOT call assertPublicUrlResolved (layer 2: DNS-resolves the hostname and blocks a domain that merely resolves to a private/loopback/metadata address) and the subsequent fetchWithTimeout() is a plain fetch, not fetchPublic (layer 3: re-validates every redirect hop) — a non-local caller supplying a hostname that resolves to an internal address (e.g. a wildcard-DNS domain pointed at 127.0.0.1), or a public URL that 302s to an internal target, passes this route's check and is fetched anyway
  - custom-embedding validates by POSTing a real /embeddings request (requires modelId); anthropic-compatible and the openai-compatible default both try GET /models first, then fall back to a minimal POST /chat/completions (max_tokens:1) if modelId is supplied and /models isn't conclusive (a non-401/403 non-OK status)
  - 401/403 short-circuits straight to a hard fail (API key unauthorized) without attempting the chat fallback — only an ambiguous non-auth failure on /models triggers the secondary chat probe
  - This is NOT an unauthenticated route: src/proxy.js runs dashboardGuard.js's proxy() as Next's middleware on every request, and /api/provider-nodes is one of PROTECTED_API_PATHS — a caller must present a valid dashboard session cookie (auth_token, JWT) or a valid machineId-derived x-9r-cli-token to reach this route at all, UNLESS settings.requireLogin is false. dashboardGuard's own isLocalRequest() (the same function this route calls to decide whether to run ssrfGuard) plays no role in THAT gate — being on the loopback socket does not bypass the session/CLI-token requirement for PROTECTED_API_PATHS, only LOCAL_ONLY_PATHS (a different, smaller list this route is not on)
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (baseUrl or apiKey missing, baseUrl is not a parseable URL, or (non-local caller) the URL is blocked by assertPublicUrl), `AUTH_ERROR` (upstream returns 401/403), `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (network error (ECONNREFUSED/ENOTFOUND/ETIMEDOUT/timeout/cert errors), classified into a specific user-facing message)
- **AIGate required behavior:** A remote (non-local) caller's user-supplied baseUrl is validated with the same DNS-resolution and redirect-safe protection ssrfGuard.js documents as necessary (assertPublicUrlResolved / fetchPublic) — the module comment explicitly says layer 1 alone leaves DNS-rebinding and redirect bypasses open

### POST /api/providers/test-batch — test-connection sweep across a group of connections selected by mode

- **id:** `connection.test-batch-sequential` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard bulk test-all-oauth / test-all-free / test-all-apikey / test-provider / test-all actions
- **Input:** { mode: provider|oauth|free|apikey|compatible|all, providerId? }
- **Output:** { mode, providerId, results:[{provider,connectionId,connectionName,authType,valid,latencyMs,error,diagnosis,statusCode,testedAt}], summary:{total,passed,failed}, testedAt }
- **Rules:**
  - Only isActive connections are ever candidates (getProviderConnections({ isActive: true })) — inactive connections are silently excluded from every mode, not just skipped-and-reported
  - mode:provider requires providerId and filters to that provider only; the other modes (oauth/free/apikey/compatible/all) classify every active connection via getAuthGroup, the same free-vs-oauth-vs-apikey classification connection.test-single-connection's OAUTH_TEST_CONFIG dispatch implicitly relies on
  - Each connection is tested by calling the exact same testSingleConnection(id) used by connection.test-single-connection — this route adds no separate test logic, only grouping/iteration and a richer per-result response shape (connectionName, diagnosis, statusCode)
  - A per-connection test() call that throws (rather than resolving with {valid:false}) is caught individually and still produces a results entry (diagnosis.type: network_error) — one connection's exception never aborts the batch
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (mode is missing, or is not one of provider/oauth/free/apikey/compatible/all (provider mode additionally needs providerId))

### POST /api/providers/[id]/test — probe one connection's credential validity against its provider and persist the result

- **id:** `connection.test-single-connection` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard test-connection action, or internally by connection.test-batch-sequential for each connection in a batch
- **Input:** connectionId path param, no body
- **Output:** { valid, error, refreshed } or 404 Connection-not-found
- **Rules:**
  - apikey/cookie auth types are probed by testApiKeyConnection (one provider-specific request per case, roughly 60 providers switched by id, most treating any non-401/403 status as valid); oauth/other types go through testOAuthConnection driven by OAUTH_TEST_CONFIG
  - testOAuthConnection refreshes proactively (before probing) when shouldRefreshCredentials says the token is expired and the provider is refreshable, rather than waiting for a 401 from the probe itself; providers with checkExpiry:true (claude, kiro, kimi) skip the network probe entirely once expiry is known
  - A soft-success status (e.g. Grok CLI's 402 spending-limit) keeps testStatus:active but writes the soft message into lastError as a warning — this is the same soft-success convention markAccountUnavailable/clearAccountError use for runtime routing (03's account.clear-error-on-success), reused here for a manual test
  - Every call — success or failure — writes testStatus/lastError/lastErrorAt back to the connection row; a passing test also clears a prior error, and an OAuth refresh mid-test persists the new tokens even though the caller only asked to validate
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (connection not found), `AUTH_ERROR` (probe returns 401/403, or refresh fails/is absent for an expired token), `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (provider has no OAUTH_TEST_CONFIG entry and is not apikey/cookie-testable (Provider-test-not-supported))

### Find local desktop API key and optional session identity

- **id:** `connection.xiaomi-mimo-desktop-auto-import` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** GET /api/oauth/xiaomi-mimo/auto-import
- **Input:** none
- **Output:** { found, apiKey?, uid?, baseUrl?, source?, mimoPassToken?, mimoUserId?, mimoCUserId?, error? }
- **Rules:**
  - Searches the first readable MiMoCode auth.json candidate under the user's home directory, with OS-specific paths.
  - Requires xiaomi.key with sk- prefix; extracts metadata UID/base URL and best-effort reads MiMo Desktop's passToken identity from its cookie store.
  - Returns credentials to the caller but does not save a provider connection; the import route performs that write separately.
- **Errors:** `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (no readable auth file or no valid key; found:false), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (unexpected local-file failure; returns 500)

### Import an API key or session credential

- **id:** `connection.xiaomi-mimo-key-import` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** POST /api/oauth/xiaomi-mimo/api-key
- **Input:** { apiKey?, uid?, baseUrl?, mimoPassToken?, mimoUserId?, mimoCUserId?, region? }
- **Output:** { success, validated, modelCount, updated?, connection } or 400/500 error
- **Rules:**
  - An API key must start with sk-. A session-only import is allowed when mimoPassToken exists without an API key.
  - API keys are probed against the chosen base URL's /models endpoint with a 10-second deadline; network/validation failure is soft and the key is stored as untested. Session-only imports skip that probe.
  - Existing Xiaomi connections are matched by uid, exact key, or session user plus optional region and updated; otherwise a new connection is created with per-account session fields.
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (neither API key nor session token is present, or API key lacks sk- prefix), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (connection persistence or unexpected parsing fails)

## Providers

### GET/PUT/DELETE /api/providers/[id] — single-connection read, update, delete

- **id:** `catalog.connection-detail-crud` · **module:** `catalog`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard connection detail view, edit, or delete action
- **Input:** id path param; PUT body: name/priority/globalPriority/defaultModel/isActive/apiKey/testStatus/lastError/lastErrorAt/providerSpecificData/proxy fields
- **Output:** 200 { connection } (secrets stripped) on GET/PUT, 200 { message } on DELETE, 404 if id not found
- **Rules:**
  - PUT only ever overwrites apiKey when the body supplies one AND the existing connection's authType is exactly "apikey" — an oauth or api_key-authType connection's credential cannot be overwritten through this generic body field, it must go through its own import/refresh flow
  - providerSpecificData is merged (existing spread, then incoming spread on top), not replaced — proxy fields (connectionProxyEnabled/Url/NoProxy) and proxyPoolId are folded into that same merged object only when the request body actually touched one of those keys (hasOwnProperty checks), so an unrelated PUT can't accidentally reset proxy settings to their defaults
  - GET/PUT both strip the same four credential fields (apiKey/accessToken/refreshToken/idToken) as the list endpoint before returning the connection
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (id does not correspond to an existing connection (GET/PUT/DELETE)), `INVALID_REQUEST` (PUT body names a proxyPoolId that doesn't exist), `INVALID_REQUEST` (PUT/POST enables connectionProxyEnabled without a connectionProxyUrl)

### GET /api/providers — list stored connections for the dashboard, with secrets stripped

- **id:** `catalog.connection-listing` · **module:** `catalog`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard providers/connections page load
- **Input:** none
- **Output:** 200 { connections: [...] } — every stored connection with apiKey/accessToken/refreshToken/idToken set to undefined
- **Rules:**
  - For OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic-compatible custom nodes, the displayed name is resolved from (in order) the connection's own name, the matching provider node's name looked up via getProviderNodes(), then providerSpecificData.nodeName, then the raw provider id — a plain apikey/oauth provider just uses its stored name
  - The four credential fields are stripped by explicit key deletion on a shallow copy (apiKey/accessToken/refreshToken/idToken: undefined), not by a field allow-list — a new secret field added to the connection shape later would leak through this endpoint unless this deletion list is updated too
- **Errors:** `INTERNAL_ERROR` (getProviderConnections() throws)

### A provider exposing more than one wire format for the same account (transport.transports[])

- **id:** `catalog.multi-format-variants` · **module:** `catalog`
- **Trigger:** A chat request whose detected sourceFormat matches one of a provider's declared alternate transports
- **Input:** sourceFormat (openai/claude/gemini/...) detected from the inbound client request shape
- **Output:** credentials.runtimeTransport set to the matching transports[] entry; buildUrl/buildHeaders in DefaultExecutor prefer it over the provider's default transport
- **Rules:**
  - A provider like deepseek declares a default transport (openai-format chat/completions) plus a transports[] array with one entry per additional native format it also understands (e.g. a claude-format /anthropic/v1/messages endpoint on the same account) — this exists specifically to let a client whose native format already matches skip the lossy double-hop through the OpenAI pivot (see open-sse/AGENTS.md's direct-route guidance)
  - resolveTransport(provider, sourceFormat) in services/provider.js picks the transports[] entry whose format matches; chatCore.js only uses it when the model's modelSupportedFormats also includes that sourceFormat, otherwise it falls back to translation through the default transport
  - Once selected, runtimeTransport's own baseUrl/headers/auth completely replace the provider's default transport fields for that request (DefaultExecutor.buildUrl/buildHeaders check credentials.runtimeTransport first) — the two formats are not merged

### GET /api/providers/[id]/models — fetch the live model catalog for one connection from its upstream provider

- **id:** `catalog.provider-models-live-fetch` · **module:** `catalog`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard refresh-models action on a connection, or an internal caller (e.g. api/providers/[id]/test-models) needing a live model list when no static list exists
- **Input:** connectionId path param
- **Output:** { provider, connectionId, models[], warning? } or a 400/401/404/500 error body
- **Rules:**
  - Dispatch is entirely config-driven via PROVIDER_MODELS_CONFIG: openai-compatible-*/anthropic-compatible-* connections use their own providerSpecificData.baseUrl (+/models), most API-key providers use createOpenAIModelsConfig(url) with a fixed upstream URL, and providers needing OAuth-refresh-on-401 or a non-OpenAI response shape (codex, gemini-cli) get a customResolver via buildOAuthResolver
  - buildOAuthResolver retries exactly once: on a 401/403 with a refreshToken present, it refreshes the token, persists the new credentials via updateProviderCredentials, mutates the in-memory connection object, and retries the same fetch — a second 401 is not retried again
  - Providers with their own dedicated resolver (kimchi, cursor, kiro, qoder, grok-cli) fall back to getStaticProviderModels(providerId) (the static PROVIDER_MODELS table) when the live fetch returns zero models, returning a warning string rather than failing the request
  - ollama-local resolves its base host per-connection via resolveOllamaLocalHost(connection) rather than a fixed URL, so each connection can point at a different local Ollama instance
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (connection not found (404), or an openai-compatible-*/anthropic-compatible-* connection has no providerSpecificData.baseUrl (400)), `AUTH_ERROR` (customResolver's buildOAuthResolver path finds no accessToken at all), `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (the provider has no PROVIDER_MODELS_CONFIG entry and is not OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible (400 does-not-support-models-listing))

### POST /api/providers/[id]/test-models — probe every model configured for one connection through 9router's own internal /v1/* endpoints

- **id:** `catalog.provider-test-models-self-dispatch` · **module:** `catalog`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard test-all-models action for a connection
- **Input:** connectionId path param, no body
- **Output:** { provider, connectionId, results:[{ modelId, name, ok, latencyMs, ... }] } or a 400/404/500 error
- **Rules:**
  - This is a thin per-connection wrapper around the same catalog.model-connectivity-test probe (pingModelByKind) used by /api/models/test — it resolves the connection's model list (static PROVIDER_MODELS, or a live fetch via this route's own /api/providers/[id]/models when the provider is compatible and has no static list) and pings each one
  - The first model is probed alone before the rest run in parallel via Promise.all — a deliberate warm-up to trigger any needed OAuth token refresh once, avoiding a refresh race if all models were dispatched concurrently from a cold/expired token
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (connection not found (404), or the resolved model list is empty (400 No-models-configured))

### Build PROVIDERS / PROVIDER_OAUTH / PROVIDER_MEDIA from the per-provider registry at module load

- **id:** `catalog.registry-build` · **module:** `catalog`
- **Trigger:** First import of open-sse/providers/index.js (or any module re-exporting it) in a process
- **Input:** REGISTRY — the auto-generated static-import array of all registry/{id}.js default exports
- **Output:** Three module-level objects keyed by provider id: PROVIDERS (transport config), PROVIDER_OAUTH (oauth config), PROVIDER_MEDIA (non-chat service config), plus PROVIDER_MODELS
- **Rules:**
  - A single top-level for-loop over REGISTRY populates all four exported objects in one pass; buildTransport(entry.transport, entry.oauth) re-applies the shared default format:"openai" when a provider doesn't declare one, then injects OAUTH_INJECT_FIELDS (clientId, clientSecret, tokenUrl) from entry.oauth into the transport object only for fields the provider's own transport left undefined
  - entry.transports (plural — a per-client-format array of endpoint overrides, e.g. deepseek/glm/minimax/kimi exposing both an openai-shaped and a claude-shaped endpoint for the same account) is copied onto PROVIDERS[id].transports verbatim, untouched by buildTransport
  - PROVIDER_MEDIA[id] is assembled from two overlapping sources for the same entry: any of the flat MEDIA_KEYS (serviceKinds, ttsConfig, sttConfig, embeddingConfig, imageConfig, imageToTextConfig, videoConfig, musicConfig, searchViaChat, searchConfig, fetchConfig, modelsFetcher, mediaPriority, hiddenKinds) declared at the entry's top level, then entry.media (a legacy nested object) is spread over the top of that — so a top-level field and the same key inside entry.media can both exist, and entry.media wins
  - PROVIDER_OAUTH[id] is only ever set when entry.oauth is truthy — a provider with no oauth block (e.g. gemini, which is authModes:["apikey"] only) simply has no key in PROVIDER_OAUTH at all, not an empty object

### Canonical per-provider registry entry contract (REGISTRY_TEMPLATE.js)

- **id:** `catalog.registry-entry-shape` · **module:** `catalog`
- **Trigger:** A developer adding or reading a provider definition (design-time, not a runtime trigger)
- **Input:** none
- **Output:** A documented object shape: identity (id/alias/category), auth hints (authType/hasOAuth/authModes/noAuth), display, transport, oauth, media, models, features/thinkingConfig/passthroughModels
- **Rules:**
  - Only id and category are required; every other block is optional and independently omittable — a media-only provider (tts/stt/embedding) drops transport.baseUrl and models entirely and fills media.*Config instead, per the template's own "Quick recipes" comment
  - transport must declare ONLY fields that differ from PROVIDER_DEFAULTS (format:"openai" etc.) — the template explicitly warns not to duplicate clientId/clientSecret/tokenUrl in transport since those are injected from oauth
  - authType/hasOAuth/authModes are advisory hints read by UI/validation code (e.g. src/app/api/providers/route.js's supportsApiKeyMode check on AI_PROVIDERS[provider]?.authModes) — they are declared independently of, and must be kept consistent with, whether an oauth block or transport.auth is actually present

### Whether PROVIDERS / PROVIDER_OAUTH / PROVIDER_MEDIA are ever mutated after the initial build

- **id:** `catalog.registry-frozen-after-load` · **module:** `catalog`
- **Trigger:** Any runtime read of PROVIDERS[id] / PROVIDER_OAUTH[id] / PROVIDER_MEDIA[id] anywhere in the app
- **Input:** none
