- **Output:** The same object references built once at module load; no code path writes to them afterward
- **Rules:**
  - A repo-wide search for assignment into PROVIDERS[...]/PROVIDER_OAUTH[...]/PROVIDER_MEDIA[...] (the bracket-index `= ` pattern) finds exactly the three assignment sites inside providers/index.js's own build loop — no other file in src/ or open-sse/ ever writes to these objects
  - The objects are plain mutable JS objects, not Object.freeze()'d — nothing technically prevents a future caller from mutating PROVIDERS.foo.baseUrl at runtime, but no current caller does; every other module only reads (PROVIDERS[provider], PROVIDER_OAUTH[provider], PROVIDER_MEDIA[provider])
  - Per-connection data (API keys, OAuth tokens, providerSpecificData) lives entirely in the providerConnections DB table, never on the PROVIDERS registry object — the registry describes the provider (shared across every connection to it), the DB row describes one credential

### GET /api/providers/suggested-models — generic server-side fetch proxy that filters a caller-supplied URL's JSON through one of three named shapers

- **id:** `catalog.suggested-models-open-proxy` · **module:** `catalog`
- **Trigger:** The dashboard's fetchSuggestedModels (providerModelsFetcher.js) calling out during provider connection setup for openrouter-free/opencode-free/mimo-free suggestions
- **Input:** ?url=<any URL>&type=openrouter-free|opencode-free|mimo-free query params
- **Output:** { data:[...] } (shape depends on FILTERS[type]) — or { data: [] } on any upstream failure/non-JSON body
- **Rules:**
  - type must match a key in FILTERS (a fixed set of 3 response-shaping functions); url is NOT validated against any allowlist of known provider endpoints — the route fetches whatever URL string is supplied, server-side, and echoes the filtered result back
  - In normal use, url is always one of a handful of hardcoded fetcher.url values baked into the AI_PROVIDERS registry (the client only ever calls this with those), but nothing in this route itself enforces that — the constraint lives entirely in the caller's discipline, not the server
  - Fetch failures (network error, non-OK status, non-JSON body) are swallowed to { data: [] } rather than surfaced as an error status, so a caller cannot distinguish blocked/unreachable from legitimately empty
  - This is NOT an unauthenticated route: src/proxy.js runs dashboardGuard.js's proxy() as Next's middleware on every request, and /api/providers is one of PROTECTED_API_PATHS — a caller must present a valid dashboard session cookie (auth_token, JWT) or a valid machineId-derived x-9r-cli-token, UNLESS settings.requireLogin is false, in which case dashboardGuard's isAuthenticated() short-circuits to true for anyone who reaches the deny-by-default /api/* branch
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (url or type missing, or type not in FILTERS)
- **AIGate required behavior:** A server-side fetch proxy that accepts an arbitrary URL from the query string validates that URL the same way provider-nodes/validate does (SSRF guard) before fetching it, regardless of which UI feature happens to be the only current caller

### features.usage / features.usageApikey — which providers get a quota/usage card and live usage fetch

- **id:** `catalog.usage-feature-flag` · **module:** `catalog`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard usage page render, or GET /api/usage/[connectionId]
- **Input:** connection.provider, connection.authType
- **Output:** USAGE_SUPPORTED_PROVIDERS / USAGE_APIKEY_PROVIDERS arrays (derived from the registry) gate both UI display and the usage-fetch endpoint's eligibility check
- **Rules:**
  - USAGE_SUPPORTED_PROVIDERS and USAGE_APIKEY_PROVIDERS are computed once by filtering REGISTRY on r.features?.usage / r.features?.usageApikey respectively — a plain array derived from the same static registry as PROVIDERS, not stored anywhere else
  - isUsageEligible / the GET /api/usage/[connectionId] gate requires BOTH: the provider is in USAGE_SUPPORTED_PROVIDERS, AND (the connection's authType is oauth OR the provider is additionally in USAGE_APIKEY_PROVIDERS) — features.usage alone only ever enables usage for OAuth connections; usageApikey is the separate opt-in that extends the same eligibility to apikey/api_key-authenticated connections of that provider
  - Providers with features.usage but no usageApikey (e.g. claude, codex, antigravity, github, grok-cli, gemini-cli, zed) show/fetch usage only for their oauth connections; providers with both (deepseek, glm, groq, kimi, kiro, minimax, ollama, qoder, vercel-ai-gateway, codebuddy-cn/-intl) show/fetch it for apikey connections too

### GET /api/providers/client — paginated, field-allowlisted connection listing for browser-side consumers

- **id:** `connection.client-listing-sanitized` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard pages needing a lightweight, paginated connection list (e.g. usage/quota views per 08's quota.dashboard-refresh-and-visibility) rather than the full connection-management listing
- **Input:** ?provider=&accountStatus=&sort=provider|priority&page=&pageSize= query params
- **Output:** { connections:[sanitized], providerOptions, pagination:{page,pageSize,total,totalPages}, totals:{...} }
- **Rules:**
  - Only connections passing isUsageEligible (provider in USAGE_SUPPORTED_PROVIDERS, and either oauth authType or provider in USAGE_APIKEY_PROVIDERS) are ever returned — this is a usage-tracking-scoped view, not the full connection set catalog.connection-listing exposes to the dashboard's connection-management page
  - Each connection is passed through sanitize(): only SAFE_FIELDS and SAFE_PSD_FIELDS keys survive — apiKey, accessToken, refreshToken, idToken and any other credential field are never included, by allowlist rather than by blocklist
  - maskName partially masks a long (over 16 char) name that also matches a 32+ char alnum/underscore/hyphen token pattern (e.g. an email-like or token-like display name) down to its first 8 characters — a defense against a raw credential accidentally landing in the display name field
  - pageSize is clamped to MAX_PAGE_SIZE (500); an out-of-range page number is clamped down to the last valid page rather than returning an empty page

### GET/POST /api/provider-nodes — list and create custom compatible provider nodes, and how /v1 reaches them by prefix

- **id:** `connection.provider-node-create-list` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard Add custom provider form (POST); the provider page listing custom nodes (GET); a /v1 request naming <prefix>/<model>
- **Input:** POST { name, prefix, type?: openai-compatible|anthropic-compatible|custom-embedding, apiType?: chat|responses, baseUrl? }
- **Output:** GET { nodes: Node[] }. POST 201 { node } where node = { id, type, name, prefix, apiType?, baseUrl, createdAt, updatedAt }
- **Rules:**
  - name and prefix are required after trim (400 Name is required / Prefix is required); type defaults to openai-compatible; an openai-compatible node needs apiType chat or responses
  - The node id is the type prefix plus a generated id (openai-compatible-<apiType>-<id>); connections under the node store that id as their provider
  - An omitted baseUrl defaults to https://api.openai.com/v1 for openai-compatible and custom-embedding nodes
  - openai-compatible create keeps a pasted /chat/completions suffix, while anthropic-compatible and custom-embedding create strip their pasted /messages and /embeddings suffixes
  - Nothing checks that a prefix is unique among nodes, or that it is a usable provider token (a prefix containing / can never match, since <prefix>/<model> splits on the first /)
  - At /v1, <prefix>/<model> reaches the node whose prefix matches, with the model passed as given; built-in provider ids and aliases are reserved and always win, so a node whose prefix equals one is silently unreachable
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (name or prefix missing, apiType invalid for openai-compatible, or an unknown type), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (storage fails (500 Failed to create provider node))
- **AIGate required behavior:** A custom provider without a base URL is refused, a pasted /chat/completions suffix is normalized like the sibling node types, and a prefix that is reserved, duplicated, or unusable is refused when the node is saved

### nodesRepo (src/lib/db/repos/nodesRepo.js) — storage shape and CRUD primitives backing custom/compatible provider nodes

- **id:** `connection.provider-node-repo-storage` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** Called by the /api/provider-nodes* routes (list/create/update/delete) — never called directly by the request/routing path
- **Input:** Node objects: { id, type, name, prefix, apiType?, baseUrl, createdAt, updatedAt }
- **Output:** Plain JS node objects (rowToNode flattens the JSON data blob back onto the row)
- **Rules:**
  - Storage is a hybrid row/blob shape: id/type/name/createdAt/updatedAt are real SQLite columns on providerNodes, while every other field (prefix, apiType, baseUrl, and anything else callers add) is serialized into a single data JSON text column and rehydrated by rowToNode — the same pattern 03's connection.storage-shape-json-blob documents for providerConnections, applied one layer up to nodes
  - updateProviderNode does a read-merge-write inside a db.transaction: it reads the current row, spreads existing fields under the partial update, and re-upserts the whole merged object — a caller can pass only the changed fields and everything else survives untouched
  - upsert always writes via INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE, so createProviderNode and the merge-write inside updateProviderNode share one code path — there is no separate UPDATE statement
  - A node's own id string carries its type-specific prefix (openai-compatible-, anthropic-compatible-, custom-embedding- from src/shared/constants/providers.js), assigned once at creation by the /api/provider-nodes POST route — nodesRepo itself is prefix-agnostic and stores whatever id it's given

### PUT/DELETE /api/provider-nodes/[id] — rename/reconfigure or remove a custom OpenAI/Anthropic/embedding-compatible provider node

- **id:** `connection.provider-node-update-delete` · **module:** `connections`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard edit or delete action on a custom provider node (a user-defined OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic-compatible, or custom-embedding endpoint)
- **Input:** PUT: { name, prefix, apiType?, baseUrl }. DELETE: none (id in path)
- **Output:** PUT: { node: updated }. DELETE: { success: true }. Both 404 if the node id does not exist
- **Rules:**
  - PUT re-derives apiType validation and baseUrl sanitization from node.type read back from storage, not from a type field in the request body — a caller cannot change a node's type through this route, only its name/prefix/baseUrl(/apiType if openai-compatible)
  - baseUrl sanitization mirrors the create route's per-type rules: anthropic-compatible strips a trailing /messages, custom-embedding strips a trailing /embeddings — both exist to prevent double-appending that suffix again at request-build time
  - PUT fans the rename out to every existing connection under this node's provider id (getProviderConnections({ provider: id })), rewriting providerSpecificData.prefix/apiType/baseUrl/nodeName on each — so an in-flight connection immediately reflects the node's new baseUrl/prefix without needing to be recreated
  - DELETE cascades: deleteProviderConnectionsByProvider(id) removes every connection under this node before deleteProviderNode(id) removes the node itself — deleting a node silently deletes all its connections too, with no confirmation or count returned
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (node not found (404), or PUT is missing name/prefix/baseUrl, or apiType is invalid for an openai-compatible node)

## Proxy Pools

### A real (non-noAuth) connection is bound to a proxy pool via its own create/update body

- **id:** `proxypool.assign-to-connection` · **module:** `transport`
- **Trigger:** POST /api/providers (create connection) or PUT /api/providers/[id] (update connection) with a proxyPoolId field in the request body
- **Input:** body.proxyPoolId — a proxy pool id string, or '__none__'/empty/omitted to leave/clear it
- **Output:** connection.providerSpecificData.proxyPoolId set to the validated id, or rejected with 400 if the id does not resolve to an existing pool
- **Rules:**
  - proxyPoolId is validated against the proxyPools table before being accepted — normalizeProxyPoolId() calls getProxyPoolById() and returns an error ('Proxy pool not found') if it doesn't resolve, so a connection can never be bound to a dangling/nonexistent pool id at write time
  - '__none__' (and empty string / null / undefined) explicitly clears the pool assignment rather than being treated as 'leave unchanged' on create; on update, only an explicitly-present 'proxyPoolId' key in the body triggers any change at all (undefined means untouched)
  - The pool assignment is a static 1:1 binding stored on the connection row — there is no rotation for real connections (rotation only exists for noAuth/free providers, see proxypool.rotate-for-noauth); each request re-resolves the SAME assigned pool via resolveConnectionProxyConfig()
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (proxyPoolId given does not resolve via getProxyPoolById)

### POST /api/proxy-pools/cloudflare-deploy — uploads a Worker relay script and resolves its workers.dev URL

- **id:** `proxypool.cloudflare-relay-deploy` · **module:** `transport`
- **Trigger:** POST /api/proxy-pools/cloudflare-deploy with { accountId, apiToken, projectName? }
- **Input:** Cloudflare account id + API token; optional project/script name
- **Output:** 201 { proxyPool, deployUrl }, or an error at any failed step
- **Rules:**
  - Same relay contract as the Vercel function: the Worker reads x-relay-target/x-relay-path, deletes those two plus host before forwarding, and additionally wraps the forward in its own try/catch returning a 502 JSON error on fetch failure (the Vercel/Deno relay functions don't have this extra guard — an unhandled forward failure there propagates as a platform-level 5xx instead of a relay-authored 502 body)
  - Deployment is synchronous (a single multipart PUT of the Worker script, no polling/readiness wait like Vercel or Deno) — the script is live as soon as the upload call returns ok
  - Enabling the workers.dev subdomain (step 2, a POST to .../subdomain) is explicitly best-effort: its response is checked but a non-ok result only logs a warning and the code comment says 'We don't fail completely here, just continue' — deployment proceeds even if the subdomain couldn't be enabled
  - The final deployUrl is only resolvable by a THIRD call (GET account subdomain info) — if that call fails or the account has no workers.dev subdomain configured at all, the route returns a 400 even though the Worker script IS already uploaded and live (partial-deployment: script exists on Cloudflare, but no proxyPools row is created and no cleanup/delete of the uploaded script is attempted)
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (accountId or apiToken missing), `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (Worker script upload (PUT) fails), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (subdomain lookup fails or returns no subdomain — script already uploaded, no local record created, no rollback)

### GET/PUT/DELETE /api/proxy-pools/[id]

- **id:** `proxypool.crud-get-update-delete` · **module:** `transport`
- **Trigger:** GET/PUT/DELETE /api/proxy-pools/{id}
- **Input:** PUT body: partial { name, proxyUrl, noProxy, isActive, strictProxy, type } — only present keys are applied
- **Output:** GET/PUT: { proxyPool }. DELETE: { success: true }, or 409 with boundConnectionCount if the pool is still bound to any connection
- **Rules:**
  - PUT only touches fields present in the body (hasOwnProperty checks per field) — omitted fields are left untouched, matching the partial-PATCH pattern used elsewhere in the codebase (cf. settings.patch-protected-keys)
  - DELETE is guarded: it recomputes bound-connection count the same way as buildUsageMap (real connections only, via providerSpecificData.proxyPoolId) and refuses with 409 if any exist — but, same gap as proxypool.crud-list-and-create, this guard is blind to noAuth providers pinned/rotating onto the pool via settings.providerStrategies, so a pool actively serving a free-provider's traffic can be deleted out from under it with no warning
  - SUSPECTED_BUG: the PUT handler's inline type allow-list (validTypes) is `["http", "vercel", "cloudflare"]` — it omits 'deno', even though VALID_PROXY_TYPES in the sibling create route (proxy-pools/route.js line 10) and the deno-deploy route both treat 'deno' as a first-class type. Any PUT that includes a `type` field on an existing deno-relay pool (even re-submitting its own current value 'deno' from an edit form) silently coerces it to 'http'. Since resolveConnectionProxyConfig() branches on `proxyPool.type === 'vercel' || 'cloudflare' || 'deno'` to decide between the header-relay path (vercelRelayUrl) and the ProxyAgent path (connectionProxyUrl), a pool downgraded to 'http' this way is misrouted: proxyAwareFetch would try to use the Deno relay's URL as a literal HTTP_PROXY endpoint via undici's ProxyAgent instead of sending it the x-relay-target/x-relay-path headers the deployed Deno relay function expects, breaking every request through that pool
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (PUT sets name/proxyUrl to empty, or id not found (404 branch, not modeled as one of the eight enum codes — treated as INVALID_REQUEST here for the not-found case)), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (DB read/write throws)
- **AIGate required behavior:** PUT /api/proxy-pools/[id] should accept the same four proxy types the create route and the deploy routes produce (http, vercel, cloudflare, deno), so editing/resaving an existing Deno-relay pool preserves its type

### GET/POST /api/proxy-pools — list (with optional usage enrichment) and create

- **id:** `proxypool.crud-list-and-create` · **module:** `transport`
- **Trigger:** GET /api/proxy-pools[?isActive=true|false&includeUsage=true]; POST /api/proxy-pools
- **Input:** GET: isActive/includeUsage query params. POST body: { name, proxyUrl, noProxy?, isActive?, strictProxy?, type? }
- **Output:** GET: { proxyPools: [...] }, each optionally carrying boundConnectionCount. POST: { proxyPool } 201, or { error } 400/500
- **Rules:**
  - VALID_PROXY_TYPES = http, vercel, cloudflare, deno — any other/missing type on create silently coerces to 'http' rather than rejecting the request
  - name and proxyUrl are required (trimmed, non-empty) on create; isActive defaults to true when omitted; strictProxy defaults to false (only true if the body literal is `true`)
  - includeUsage=true triggers a second full table scan (getProviderConnections() with no filter) to build a Map of proxyPoolId -> count of connections whose providerSpecificData.proxyPoolId matches, then merges boundConnectionCount onto each pool in the response — this count only reflects real (non-noAuth) connections bound via proxypool.assign-to-connection, not noAuth providers using the pool through rotation/pin in settings.providerStrategies
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (POST body missing name or proxyUrl), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (DB read/write throws)

### POST /api/proxy-pools/deno-deploy — creates a Deno Deploy app, deploys the relay, polls status, and rolls back on 2 of its 3 failure paths

- **id:** `proxypool.deno-relay-deploy` · **module:** `transport`
- **Trigger:** POST /api/proxy-pools/deno-deploy with { denoToken, orgDomain, projectName? }
- **Input:** Deno Deploy API token; org domain (used to build the final *.deno.net URL); optional project/app slug
- **Output:** 201 { proxyPool, deployUrl }, or an error at any failed step
- **Rules:**
  - Same relay header contract as the other two (reads x-relay-target/x-relay-path, deletes those plus host, wraps the forward fetch in try/catch returning a 502 JSON on failure, matching the Cloudflare Worker's guard — unlike the Vercel Edge Function, which has no such try/catch around its forward)
  - Deployment is two calls (create app, then deploy revision) followed by a bounded poll loop: up to 30 attempts at 2000ms apart (60s max) while status is 'queued'/'building'
  - This route has three distinct failure paths, and only two of them roll back. (1) The deploy-revision call itself failing (non-ok) DOES roll back: it hits an explicit DELETE /apps/{id} before returning the error. (2) The poll loop ending with a non-'succeeded' status (reached either by observing a genuine terminal bad status, e.g. 'failed'/'canceled', or by the statusRes fetch itself failing mid-poll and breaking the loop early with whatever status was last seen) also DOES roll back, via the same `if (status !== "succeeded")` DELETE block. (3) The poll loop exhausting all 30 attempts (60s) throws `new Error("Deploy timed out after 60 seconds")` INSIDE the while loop — this throw unwinds immediately past the `if (status !== "succeeded")` rollback block entirely (it's never reached) and lands directly in the function's single outer catch, which only logs and returns a 500 with no DELETE call. So the 60s-timeout path does NOT roll back — see suspicion below
  - The two rollback DELETE calls that do fire are fire-and-forget (.catch(() => {})) — if the DELETE itself also fails, that failure is swallowed silently and the app can still be left behind even on the two paths that do attempt cleanup
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (orgDomain or denoToken missing), `INVALID_REQUEST` (app creation returns 409 (name already exists)), `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (app creation (non-409) or deploy-revision call fails), `TIMEOUT` (poll loop exhausts 30 attempts (60s) without reaching a terminal status — this path orphans the Deno app (no rollback)), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (revision status resolves to anything other than 'succeeded' via a genuine terminal status or an early loop break — this path DOES roll back)
- **AIGate required behavior:** Given that this route already rolls back on 2 of its 3 failure paths (deploy-call failure, bad-final-status), the timeout path should follow the same pattern — either DELETE before throwing, or set a sentinel status and let it fall through to the existing `if (status !== "succeeded")` rollback block, instead of throwing straight past it

### pickProxyPoolId() rotation for free/noAuth providers, keyed by settings.providerStrategies

- **id:** `proxypool.rotate-for-noauth` · **module:** `transport`
- **Trigger:** getProviderCredentials() for a noAuth provider, per request
- **Input:** settings.providerStrategies[providerId].rotateStrategy ('none'/'round-robin'/'random') and .proxyPoolId (fixed pin, used when strategy is 'none'); the list of active pools with a non-empty proxyUrl
- **Output:** One proxyPoolId, fed into resolveConnectionProxyConfig({ proxyPoolId }) to build the synthetic noAuth connection's proxy config
- **Rules:**
  - strategy 'none' (the default when unset) skips pickProxyPoolId entirely and uses providerStrategies[providerId].proxyPoolId as a fixed pin — no pool list is even fetched in that case
  - strategy 'round-robin' or 'random' fetches all isActive pools with a non-empty proxyUrl, then pickProxyPoolId() selects one: round-robin advances a per-providerId index stored in an in-memory Map (rotateState) modulo the pool count; random picks uniformly via Math.random()
  - round-robin state is in-memory only and keyed per providerId (not per pool-list — if the active pool list changes shape between requests, the stored index can point at a different pool than intended, since it's a raw array index, not a cursor tied to pool identity)
  - A single-pool list always short-circuits to that one pool regardless of strategy (pickProxyPoolId's poolIds.length === 1 check), so round-robin/random only matter with 2+ active pools

### proxyPoolsRepo.js — proxyPools table storage shape

- **id:** `proxypool.storage-json-blob` · **module:** `transport`
- **Trigger:** Any proxy-pool CRUD call (createProxyPool/updateProxyPool/deleteProxyPool/getProxyPools/getProxyPoolById)
- **Input:** Pool fields: id, name, proxyUrl, noProxy, type, isActive, strictProxy, testStatus, lastTestedAt, lastError, createdAt, updatedAt
- **Output:** Row objects reconstructed by merging id/isActive/testStatus/createdAt/updatedAt (real columns) with a parsed JSON blob (everything else: name, proxyUrl, noProxy, type, strictProxy)
- **Rules:**
  - Same JSON-blob-over-relational-columns shape as connection.storage-shape-json-blob: only id, isActive, testStatus, createdAt, updatedAt are real SQL columns with types; name/proxyUrl/noProxy/type/strictProxy all live inside a single `data` TEXT column, parsed/stringified via parseJson/stringifyJson on every read/write
  - isActive is stored as SQLite 0/1 (poolToRow: `isActive === false ? 0 : 1`, so anything not literally `false` — including undefined — persists as 1/active) and read back via `row.isActive === 1 || row.isActive === true` (rowToPool) to tolerate either representation depending on the underlying adapter (bun:sqlite/better-sqlite3/node:sqlite/sql.js all normalize booleans differently)
  - createProxyPool/updateProxyPool/deleteProxyPool all use a single INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE (upsert) or a db.transaction() wrapper — id collisions on create silently become an update rather than erroring, since the same `upsert()` helper backs create and update
  - getProxyPools() sorts results by updatedAt descending in application code after the SQL SELECT (no ORDER BY in the query itself) — every list call does a full-table scan-and-sort regardless of the isActive/testStatus filter size
- **Note:** 9router's mechanism here is an accident of its stack. Behavior required, mechanism not.

### POST /api/proxy-pools/[id]/test — live connectivity check, updates testStatus/isActive as a side effect

- **id:** `proxypool.test-connectivity` · **module:** `transport`
- **Trigger:** POST /api/proxy-pools/{id}/test
- **Input:** proxy pool id (path param)
- **Output:** { ok, status, statusText, error, elapsedMs, testedAt }
- **Rules:**
  - Dispatch differs by pool type: vercel/cloudflare/deno pools are tested via testVercelRelay() — a direct GET to the relay URL with x-relay-target: https://httpbin.org and x-relay-path: /get headers, 10s timeout; plain 'http' pools are tested via testProxyUrl() — a HEAD to https://google.com/ dispatched through a fresh, one-off undici ProxyAgent built from the pool's proxyUrl, default 8s timeout (caller-overridable, capped at 30s)
  - The test result is NOT purely read-only: the pool row is unconditionally updated afterward with testStatus ('active'/'error'), lastTestedAt, lastError, and — notably — isActive is overwritten to exactly the test's ok boolean. A previously-active pool that fails one connectivity check is automatically deactivated (isActive: false), and a previously-inactive pool that passes is automatically reactivated, with no separate 'do not auto-toggle' option
  - testProxyUrl()'s one-off ProxyAgent is explicitly closed in a finally block after the test (dispatcher?.close?.()), unlike the long-lived cached ProxyAgents in transport.proxy-dispatcher-cache which are never explicitly closed on eviction
- **Errors:** `TIMEOUT` (probe exceeds its timeout — AbortController fires, surfaced as 'Relay test timed out' or 'Proxy test timed out'), `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (probe request errors for any other reason (connection refused, invalid proxy URL, etc.))

### POST /api/proxy-pools/vercel-deploy — deploys a header-relay Edge Function and polls it to readiness

- **id:** `proxypool.vercel-relay-deploy` · **module:** `transport`
- **Trigger:** POST /api/proxy-pools/vercel-deploy with { vercelToken, projectName? }
- **Input:** Vercel API token; optional project name (defaults to relay-<timestamp36>)
- **Output:** 201 { proxyPool, deployUrl } once the deployment is READY and a proxy pool row has been created for it; or an error response at any failed step
- **Rules:**
  - The deployed RELAY_FUNCTION_CODE is a Vercel Edge Function that reads x-relay-target (the scheme+host to forward to) and x-relay-path (path+query) off the incoming request, rejects with 400 if x-relay-target is missing, then deletes x-relay-target, x-relay-path, AND host from the forwarded headers before calling fetch(targetUrl, ...) — x-relay-target/x-relay-path are internal routing instructions never meant for the real upstream (leaving them would leak 9router's internal relay protocol to the provider and could collide with real headers); host must be deleted because it still holds the RELAY function's own domain (or whatever the original inbound Host was) and is invalid/misleading for a request now going to targetUrl's actual host — fetch() sets the correct Host itself once the stale one is removed
  - After a successful deploy, the code issues a PATCH to disable Vercel's own deployment protection (ssoProtection: null) so the relay is reachable without a Vercel auth challenge — this PATCH's response is not checked (no error handling if it fails), so a deploy can succeed with SSO protection still silently enabled, in which case every subsequent relay request would get intercepted by Vercel's auth page instead of reaching the relay function
  - pollDeployment(deploymentId, token, maxMs=120000) polls GET /v13/deployments/{id} every 3000ms; returns once readyState is READY; throws immediately (no further retry) on ERROR/CANCELED; throws 'Deployment timed out' after 120000ms of polling with no READY/ERROR/CANCELED resolution
  - SUSPECTED_BUG / partial-deployment risk: createProxyPool() — the only step that records the deployment locally — runs AFTER pollDeployment() resolves. If pollDeployment throws (timeout, or Vercel reports ERROR/CANCELED), the outer catch returns a 500 with no cleanup at all: this file contains no DELETE/cleanup call anywhere, for any failure mode. The Vercel deployment (and, if it got that far, the disabled SSO protection) already exists on Vercel's account, consuming a real deployment slot/build minutes, but no proxyPools row is ever created — the operator has no record in 9router of the orphaned Vercel deployment and must find/delete it manually via the Vercel dashboard
  - Newly-created pools from this route always get strictProxy: false and isActive: true hardcoded — strictProxy must be turned on manually afterward via PUT if desired
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (vercelToken missing from the request body), `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (Vercel deployment creation call itself returns non-ok), `TIMEOUT` (pollDeployment exceeds 120000ms without reaching READY/ERROR/CANCELED), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (deployment reaches ERROR/CANCELED state, or any other unhandled exception)
- **AIGate required behavior:** A failed or timed-out Vercel relay deployment should be cleaned up (deleted from Vercel) or otherwise reconciled so no orphaned billable resource is left with zero trace in 9router — the deno-deploy route (proxypool.deno-relay-deploy) shows this codebase already knows how to do that: it issues a DELETE rollback on 2 of its 3 failure paths

### resolveConnectionProxyConfig() — pool vs legacy vs none priority

- **id:** `transport.connection-proxy-config-priority` · **module:** `transport`
- **Trigger:** Called with a connection's (or a synthetic noAuth connection's) providerSpecificData, once per credential resolution (getProviderCredentials in auth.js) or per background quota/usage/reset-credits call
- **Input:** providerSpecificData: { proxyPoolId, connectionProxyEnabled, connectionProxyUrl, connectionNoProxy } (legacy fields kept for pre-proxy-pool connections)
- **Output:** A normalized { source, proxyPoolId, proxyPool, connectionProxyEnabled, connectionProxyUrl, connectionNoProxy, strictProxy, vercelRelayUrl? } object
- **Rules:**
  - Priority, in order: (1) proxyPoolId — if set (and not the sentinel '__none__'), the pool is looked up by id; only used if the pool exists, isActive === true, and has a non-empty proxyUrl (an inactive or URL-less pool is treated as if proxyPoolId were absent, falling through to legacy); (2) legacy connectionProxyEnabled+connectionProxyUrl on the connection itself; (3) no proxy at all
  - A valid pool of type vercel/cloudflare/deno returns connectionProxyEnabled: false and instead sets vercelRelayUrl to the pool's proxyUrl — these three types are header-relay proxies, not HTTP_PROXY-style proxies, so they must NOT go through the undici ProxyAgent dispatch path; a plain 'http' pool type returns connectionProxyEnabled: true / connectionProxyUrl set, for the ProxyAgent path
  - Any error during resolution (e.g. a DB read failure fetching the pool) is caught and degrades to source: 'error' with everything disabled (connectionProxyEnabled: false, strictProxy: false) rather than propagating — the caller always gets a valid object shape, never a rejected promise
- **Errors:** `INTERNAL_ERROR` (DB read for the pool throws)

### MITM_BYPASS_HOSTS — manual DNS resolution + raw-socket TLS to dodge local DNS/hosts poisoning

- **id:** `transport.mitm-dns-bypass` · **module:** `transport`
- **Trigger:** proxyAwareFetch() called with a target URL whose hostname matches (via substring `includes`) one of MITM_BYPASS_HOSTS
- **Input:** target hostname
- **Output:** A Response obtained either through the configured proxy (dispatcher) or, if no proxy, through a manually-constructed HTTPS request to the real (Google-DNS-resolved) IP
- **Rules:**
  - MITM_BYPASS_HOSTS = cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com, daily-cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com, api.individual.githubcopilot.com, q.us-east-1.amazonaws.com, codewhisperer.us-east-1.amazonaws.com, api2.cursor.sh — exactly the upstream API hosts used by 9router's own antigravity/cloudcode, GitHub Copilot, kiro/codewhisperer, and cursor executors
  - These are the same hostnames src/mitm/ rewrites in the OS hosts file / local DNS (per src/shared/constants/mitmToolHosts.js) to intercept IDE traffic for its own capture feature. When 9router's own outbound executor calls hit the SAME hostnames on a machine where the MITM feature is active, the OS-level resolution would route them into the local MITM interceptor instead of the real provider — this bypass exists so the router's own provider traffic is unaffected by whatever DNS/hosts state the MITM capture feature has put the machine in
  - DNS resolution uses a dedicated Node dns.Resolver pinned to Google's public servers (8.8.8.8, 8.8.4.4), not the system resolver, specifically to avoid the poisoned /etc/hosts or local resolver
  - TLS is still fully established and validated: the resolved real IP is used only for the raw TCP connect; the TLS `servername` (SNI) and the Host header are set to the ORIGINAL hostname, not the IP — confirmed empirically (see file header) that https.request() wraps the raw net.Socket in a genuine TLS session keyed to `servername`, and a mismatched servername causes a handshake failure. So certificate-hostname validation is preserved against the real target host; this bypass only sidesteps the DNS/hosts layer, not TLS trust
- **Errors:** `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (DNS resolve fails, or the raw-socket HTTPS request errors)

### Cached undici ProxyAgent dispatchers, keyed by normalized proxy URL

- **id:** `transport.proxy-dispatcher-cache` · **module:** `transport`
- **Trigger:** getDispatcher(proxyUrl) called from either branch of proxyAwareFetch that needs to dispatch through a proxy
- **Input:** normalized proxy URL string
- **Output:** A cached (or newly-created) undici ProxyAgent instance
- **Rules:**
  - Bounded by count only (MEMORY_CONFIG.proxyDispatchersMaxSize = 20), never by time — there is no TTL/expiry for an entry once created; an entry only leaves the Map when the cache is full AND a brand-new proxy URL needs to be inserted
  - Eviction is FIFO by insertion order, not true LRU: `proxyDispatchers.keys().next().value` always deletes the oldest-INSERTED entry (Map iteration order), and a cache HIT on an existing key does not re-insert/move it — so a frequently-reused proxy that happens to be old still gets evicted ahead of a rarely-used one that was added more recently
  - An evicted ProxyAgent is only dropped from the Map reference — nothing calls .close()/.destroy() on it, unlike the one-off tester dispatcher in proxyTest.js which explicitly closes its ProxyAgent in a finally block. Sockets/connections held by an evicted-but-still-open agent are left to be reclaimed by GC/keep-alive timeout rather than an explicit close

### proxyAwareFetch() dispatch priority chain

- **id:** `transport.proxy-priority-chain` · **module:** `transport`
- **Trigger:** Every outbound provider/executor HTTP call routed through proxyAwareFetch(url, options, proxyOptions) instead of raw fetch
- **Input:** target url; fetch options; proxyOptions ({ connectionProxyEnabled, connectionProxyUrl, connectionNoProxy, vercelRelayUrl, strictProxy } or null)
- **Output:** A Response — either relayed through a deployed Vercel/Cloudflare/Deno function, dispatched through an undici ProxyAgent, sent via a manual DNS-bypass socket, or sent as a direct fetch
- **Rules:**
  - Priority order, evaluated in this sequence: (1) proxyOptions.vercelRelayUrl, if non-empty, short-circuits everything else — the request is forwarded to the relay URL with x-relay-target/x-relay-path headers added, unconditionally, before any proxy/MITM logic runs; (2) connectionProxyUrl = resolveConnectionProxyUrl(targetUrl, proxyOptions) — only non-null when proxyOptions.enabled or proxyOptions.connectionProxyEnabled is exactly true AND a URL is present AND the target host is not matched by proxyOptions.noProxy/connectionNoProxy; (3) envProxyUrl is computed ONLY when connectionProxyUrl is null (a per-connection pool proxy always wins over HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/ALL_PROXY env vars, and env lookup itself honors NO_PROXY/no_proxy); (4) proxyUrl = connectionProxyUrl || envProxyUrl
  - If the target host is in MITM_BYPASS_HOSTS: with a proxyUrl present, it tries the proxy first (return on success); on proxy failure it falls through (not returns) to the manual-DNS-bypass branch, which resolves the real IP via Google DNS and opens a direct raw-socket HTTPS request to that IP with the original hostname as TLS servername/Host
  - If that manual-bypass branch also fails (DNS resolve fails, or realIP is falsy, or createBypassRequest throws), execution falls out of the MITM block entirely and re-enters the generic `if (proxyUrl)` branch below — meaning a MITM host with a working proxyUrl and a failing bypass gets a SECOND proxy dispatch attempt through the same dispatcher before finally falling back to a plain direct fetch
  - For non-MITM hosts (the common case): if proxyUrl is set, dispatch through the cached undici ProxyAgent; if proxyUrl is unset, call the original (unpatched) global fetch directly — got-scraping/TLS-fingerprinting is present in the file but fully commented out (dead code), so no JA3 spoofing occurs at all despite the file header describing it
- **Errors:** `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (proxy dispatch throws and strictProxy is not exactly true — caught, logged, silently falls back to a direct fetch (see transport.strict-proxy-fallback))

### strictProxy — hard-fail vs silent direct fallback on proxy dispatch failure

- **id:** `transport.strict-proxy-fallback` · **module:** `transport`
- **Trigger:** proxyUrl is set and the undici ProxyAgent dispatch throws (proxy unreachable, auth failure, connection refused, etc.)
- **Input:** proxyOptions.strictProxy (boolean, sourced from a proxy pool's strictProxy field)
- **Output:** Either a thrown Error (request fails visibly) or a silent retry of the same URL with a plain direct fetch (no proxy, no error to the caller)
- **Rules:**
  - strictProxy only gates the two explicit `if (proxyOptions?.strictProxy === true) throw` sites in proxyFetch.js, both immediately after a caught proxy-dispatch error — it does not affect any other branch (vercel relay, MITM manual-bypass failure, or the 'no proxy configured at all' path)
  - With strictProxy anything other than exactly true (false, undefined, missing), a dead/unreachable proxy is caught, a console.warn is emitted, and the SAME request is silently retried via the unpatched direct fetch — the caller receives a normal response with no indication the proxy was bypassed
  - SUSPECTED_BUG: the primary chat-completion request path (open-sse/handlers/chatCore.js, the code every /v1 chat request goes through) builds its proxyOptions object WITHOUT a strictProxy field at all, so `proxyOptions?.strictProxy === true` is always false on that path regardless of what a proxy pool's strictProxy toggle is set to. Three sibling call sites that also build a proxyOptions object DO set the field explicitly: antigravityQuota.js propagates the resolved value faithfully (strictProxy: proxyCfg.strictProxy === true); usage/[connectionId]/route.js and codex-reset-credits/route.js force it to false with an explicit code comment explaining the choice ('force strictProxy=false so quota/refresh fall back to direct on failure'). chatCore.js has no such comment and no such field — it reads as an omission, not a deliberate choice, and it means the strictProxy toggle can never actually enforce anything for real model traffic, only for the three secondary (quota/refresh) paths that already deliberately ignore it
- **Errors:** `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (strictProxy === true and proxy dispatch fails)
- **AIGate required behavior:** A proxy pool with strictProxy enabled should cause real model-traffic requests through that pool to fail (not silently go direct) when the proxy is unreachable, matching what the dashboard toggle promises and what the other three call sites (antigravityQuota, usage, codex-reset-credits) already do with the same field

## Quota Tracker

### Antigravity's locally-counted/inferred quota — RAM cache plus a strike-based trust override

- **id:** `quota.antigravity-local-cache-strike-breaker` · **module:** `usage`
- **Trigger:** auth.js's account pre-filter reading the cache, or a 409/429 from an Antigravity generation call
- **Input:** connectionId, accessToken, providerSpecificData, model, HTTP status (409/429)
- **Output:** quotaCache.get(connectionId)[model] = {remainingPercentage, resetAt} — either the vendor's own reading or a synthesized 0%-blocked entry
- **Rules:**
  - refreshAntigravityQuota is throttled to once per 30000ms (MIN_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS) per connectionId, with in-flight-promise dedup so concurrent 409/429 bursts share one upstream call; every attempt (success or failure) still updates lastRefreshAt so a failing quota endpoint cannot itself trigger a request-amplification loop
  - A fresh vendor read replaces the cache entry, but applyActiveStrikeBlocks() re-asserts any still-active synthesized block on top of it immediately — so an optimistic vendor reading cannot resurrect a pair 9router has already decided to distrust
  - handleAntigravityQuotaError: on a 409/429 where the vendor's own quota reading is either optimistic (remainingPercentage > 0) or unavailable, it counts a 'strike' in a 60000ms (STRIKE_WINDOW_MS) fixed window anchored at the FIRST qualifying strike (not a rolling window); 3 strikes (STRIKE_THRESHOLD) within that window synthesizes a local 0%-remaining, 15-minute-blocked (STRIKE_BLOCK_MS) cache entry regardless of what the vendor API claims — this is the 'locally-counted / inferred' quota reading, overriding the vendor's own number because the generation endpoint and the quota endpoint disagreed 3 times in a row
  - When the vendor reading is instead a genuine exhausted (remainingPercentage <= 0, resetAt present and in the future), strikes are cleared and the vendor's own resetAt is used directly — this branch is measured, not inferred

### quotaAutoPing scheduler — opt-in pings that start a new quota window right after reset

- **id:** `quota.auto-ping-window-warming` · **module:** `usage`
- **Trigger:** A 60000ms (tickIntervalMs) scheduler interval, started/stopped based on whether any connection has auto-ping enabled
- **Input:** settings.claudeAutoPing/codexAutoPing.connections[id] === true, per-connection vendor usage reading
- **Output:** A tiny (1-token 'hi', or a minimal Codex Responses call) request sent to the provider to open a fresh quota window early
- **Rules:**
  - Only connections explicitly opted in via settings (claudeAutoPing/codexAutoPing.connections[connectionId] = true) and active + oauth are targeted
  - Claude waits for the wall-clock resetAt to actually pass (within pingLeadMs = 5000ms tolerance) before pinging — a time-based window
  - Codex instead pings whenever its resetAt 'slides' by resetAtDriftMs (30000ms) or more between reads (pingWhenResetAtSlides) — an inactive session's window doesn't start counting down until first use, so Codex polls every tick rather than waiting for a fixed time, gated by minPingIntervalMs (600000ms) and skipWhenBlockingQuotaExhausted
  - A ping is skipped entirely if a blocking (non-session) quota is already exhausted, if the same resetAt was already pinged (lastPingedResetKey dedup, normalized to whole minutes), or if a ping/refresh failed recently (failureCooldownMs = 900000ms)
  - On success, the connection is updated with lastPingedResetAt/lastPingedResetKey/lastPingAt so the same reset window is never pinged twice
  - The scheduler's interval handle lives on global.__quotaAutoPing (same 'survive Next.js hot reload / one instance per process' pattern as usage.global-state-next-reeval) rather than module-scope state
- **Errors:** `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (the ping request itself fails (non-ok response))

### Codex reset credits — a redeemable pool that manually ends the current 5h window early

- **id:** `quota.codex-reset-credits` · **module:** `usage`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard 'use reset credit' button on a Codex connection
- **Input:** none (GET to list) / a server-generated redeemRequestId (POST to consume)
- **Output:** GET: {availableCount, credits: [{status, grantedAt, expiresAt}]}; POST: {code, reset, windows_reset, credit} or a 409/error
- **Rules:**
  - POST generates redeemRequestId server-side via crypto.randomUUID() specifically to prevent a client-controlled replay of the same redeem id
  - A 409 no_credit response is returned distinctly from other 4xx/5xx failures when the vendor reports zero credits available
  - The dashboard confirms via a modal showing the remaining credit count, then re-fetches the connection's quota (fetchQuota) after a successful reset so the UI reflects the freshly-reset window immediately
- **Errors:** `QUOTA_EXHAUSTED` (vendor responds with noCredit (no reset credits available)), `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (the consume call returns an unexpected non-4xx-non-2xx response)

### The /dashboard/quota page — auto-refresh cadence, per-provider throttling, client cache, visibility settings

- **id:** `quota.dashboard-refresh-and-visibility` · **module:** `usage`
- **Trigger:** User opens /dashboard/quota
- **Input:** none
- **Output:** ProviderLimits renders one card per connection with its parsed quota rows
- **Rules:**
  - quota/page.js is a thin wrapper (Suspense + CardSkeleton) around the ProviderLimits client component, which does all the fetching
  - Auto-refresh polls every REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS = 60000ms; Claude connections are additionally throttled to once every CLAUDE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS / REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS = 10 ticks (i.e. ~600000ms) unless force=true (manual refresh or 'refresh all')
  - The auto-refresh interval and its 1s countdown are both cleared and stop firing when the browser tab is hidden (Page Visibility API), and re-armed on visibilitychange when it becomes visible again
  - Each connection's last successful quota read is cached client-side in localStorage under QUOTA_CACHE_KEY ('quotaCacheData'); this is purely a client-side display cache, not consulted for freshness decisions
  - Per-quota-row visibility (hide/show individual quota lines like a specific model's weekly window) and per-connection auto-ping toggles are both persisted server-side via PATCH /api/settings (quotaVisibility, claudeAutoPing/codexAutoPing.connections), not client-only state
  - DEPLETED_QUOTA_THRESHOLD = 5 (percent) drives the 'Turn off Empty' / 'Turn on Available' bulk actions: a connection counts as depleted if any of its quota rows has remaining% <= 5
- **Errors:** `AUTH_ERROR` (a connection's quota fetch 401s — shown inline as a message instead of throwing)

### The four categories behavioral.md §21 asks about — which exist in 9router and how

- **id:** `quota.sources-taxonomy` · **module:** `usage`
- **Trigger:** N/A — cross-cutting taxonomy over the quota subsystem
- **Input:** None — this is a classification over the whole quota subsystem, not a single call's input
- **Output:** A classification of every quota reading 9router produces as vendor-reported, subscription, locally-counted, or absent (budget)
- **Rules:**
  - vendor-reported (measured): the majority of quota data. USAGE_HANDLERS dispatches by provider to a handler in open-sse/services/usage/*.js that calls the provider's own usage/rate-limit API directly (Claude OAuth usage endpoint, GitHub copilot_internal/user, Codex rate_limit endpoint, Kiro, GLM, MiniMax, etc.). Refresh cadence is on-demand (dashboard poll or auto-refresh timer), not push-based; reset time and 'remaining' are computed however the vendor's own payload expresses them (percent-utilization for Claude/Codex, used/total counts for GitHub) — 9router does not compute 'remaining' itself for these, it relays the vendor's number.
  - subscription (measured, embedded): not a separately-fetched source — every vendor usage handler also returns a `plan` field (Claude Code plan tier, GitHub copilot_plan, Codex plan_type) alongside the quota numbers, describing which tier's limits are in effect
  - locally-counted (inferred): Antigravity is the one provider where 9router does not simply relay the vendor's number. A local in-memory cache (antigravityQuota.js) stores the last vendor reading per connection+model, refreshed at most once per 30s, AND a strike-based circuit breaker can override that cache with a synthesized 0%-remaining entry after 3 429/409s within 60s on the same pair — even when the vendor API itself still claims quota remains. See quota.antigravity-local-cache-strike-breaker.
  - budget: absent. No spend-cap, budget-limit, or cost-ceiling enforcement mechanism exists anywhere in src/ or open-sse/ — grepping for budget/spending-limit/cost-cap across both trees turns up only Claude/Kiro 'thinking budget' (an unrelated token-count parameter) and the Grok CLI 402 'spending-limit' vendor status code, which 9router treats as a soft-success (credentials are fine, the vendor's own account is out of credits) rather than something it enforces or tracks locally. Cost itself is tracked per-request (pricing.cost-calculation-cache-inclusive) but is never compared against any ceiling.

### Vendor-reported quota fetch mechanics — per-provider windows, caching, cooldowns

- **id:** `quota.vendor-fetch-caching-claude-github-codex` · **module:** `usage`
- **Trigger:** GET /api/usage/[connectionId] for an OAuth/apikey-eligible connection
- **Input:** connection.accessToken, force flag
- **Output:** Provider-specific {plan, quotas: {name: {used, total, remaining, resetAt, unlimited}}}
- **Rules:**
  - Claude: primary source is the OAuth usage endpoint, returning rolling 5h (five_hour) and 7d (seven_day) windows plus per-model 7d windows (seven_day_sonnet, seven_day_opus, seven_day_fable...); utilization is %-used, remaining = 100 - used; a 429 from this endpoint triggers a 180000ms (OAUTH_429_COOLDOWN_MS) per-token cooldown that routes subsequent calls to a legacy settings+org-usage endpoint instead; successful reads are cached 300000ms (USAGE_CACHE_TTL_MS) per access token, with in-flight-promise dedup so concurrent callers share one fetch, and force=true bypasses both the cache and the dedup
  - GitHub: two response shapes depending on plan — paid plans return quota_snapshots (chat/completions/premium_interactions, each with entitlement/remaining, resetAt from quota_reset_date, a MONTHLY cadence); free/limited plans return monthly_quotas + limited_user_quotas with a separate limited_user_reset_date
  - Codex: rate_limit primary/secondary windows map to session/weekly quotas (percent-used, resetAt), plus separate review and spark sub-limit windows found via several possible response key shapes (code_review_rate_limit, rate_limits_by_limit_id, additional_rate_limits array); also returns resetCredits.availableCount, a distinct redeemable pool (see quota.codex-reset-credits)
- **Errors:** `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (the vendor usage/rate-limit endpoint returns non-200 and there is no fallback for that provider)

## Remote functionality

### Hosts-file DNS entries — atomic write+rollback on Windows vs direct overwrite on macOS/Linux, and unconditional cleanup on stop

- **id:** `mitm.hosts-file-atomic-write-and-rollback` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** enableToolDNS/addDNSEntry (per-tool) during MITM setup, and stopServer's unconditional full-hosts cleanup on every stop
- **Input:** tool name (key into TOOL_HOSTS), sudoPassword
- **Output:** 127.0.0.1 <host> lines added to or removed from the OS hosts file for the given tool's hostnames
- **Rules:**
  - Windows hosts-file writes use a genuine atomic-write-with-rollback pattern (atomicWriteHostsWin): write the new content to a '.9router.new' sibling file, rename the current hosts file to '.9router.bak', then rename '.new' onto the real path — same-volume renames are atomic on NTFS. If the second rename fails, it explicitly rolls back by renaming '.bak' back onto the target, falling back to a raw fs.writeFileSync(target, originalContent) as a last resort if even that rename fails
  - macOS/Linux hosts-file writes have no equivalent rollback: addDNSEntry/removeDNSEntry pipe the full new content through `printf ... | tee ${HOSTS_FILE}` under sudo — a direct overwrite of the live file with no temp-file-then-rename step and no backup copy. The code's own comment calls this 'atomic', which is true only in the narrow sense that a single small write() to a regular file is unlikely to produce a torn/partial line — it provides no rollback if the operation fails outright (wrong password, process killed before the write), unlike the Windows path. This is the same non-atomic-write class already flagged for CLI-tool config writes in clitools.write-not-atomic, here applied to a shared OS system file instead of one app's own config
  - stopServer() removes ALL tool DNS entries unconditionally on every stop, regardless of which tools were actually enabled, matching clitools.antigravity-mitm-control's already-documented DELETE-handler behavior; on Windows, stopServer bypasses PowerShell entirely and writes the hosts file directly when the process is already admin, falling back to a separate PowerShell regex-filter script when not admin — a second, independent hosts-file-write code path from atomicWriteHostsWin, with no atomic rename step in either stopServer branch
  - checkDNSEntry/checkAllDNSStatus are pure substring checks against the raw hosts-file text, read directly on every call rather than cached — a hosts file that is mid-write (or corrupted) simply causes a false 'not active' rather than an error, since the read is wrapped in a try/catch that returns false
- **Errors:** `AUTH_ERROR` (execWithPassword's sudo call rejects with an incorrect-password-shaped stderr — surfaced as 'Wrong sudo password'), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (any other addDNSEntry/removeDNSEntry failure — surfaced as 'Failed to add/remove DNS entry: <message>')

### Root CA generation + OS trust-store installation during MITM server start, and the missing rollback when startup fails after install

- **id:** `mitm.root-ca-generation-and-trust-install` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** startServer() (invoked from POST /api/cli-tools/antigravity-mitm, per clitools.antigravity-mitm-control) when no valid, unexpired Root CA + trust-store entry exists yet
- **Input:** sudoPassword (mac/linux), apiKey, forceKillPort443
- **Output:** A self-signed 10-year Root CA (src/mitm/cert/rootCA.js) generated to disk and installed into the OS trust store (Windows Root store via certutil, macOS System keychain via security, Linux distro trust dir + NSS DBs) before the MITM server process is even spawned
- **Rules:**
  - startServer()'s Step 1 (generateRootCA) only regenerates the CA if it's missing or isCertExpired (within 30 days of the 10-year expiry) — the old cert is best-effort uninstalled from the trust store first, wrapped in try/catch so a failed uninstall doesn't block regeneration
  - Step 1.5 auto-installs the (possibly freshly generated) Root CA into the OS trust store if checkCertInstalled() reports it isn't already trusted — the Windows/macOS checks compare the exact certificate fingerprint (not just the CommonName), so a stale cert with the same CN but a different key correctly reports 'not installed' and triggers a real re-install rather than a false-positive skip
  - On Linux specifically, if no sudo is available at all, the system trust-store install is skipped entirely (only user-level NSS databases for Firefox/Chromium profiles are updated) and the log tells the user to manually trust the cert file on client machines — a degraded but non-fatal path
  - Windows processes that already have admin rights install with zero password prompt (runElevatedPowerShell runs directly with no UAC popup when isAdmin() is already true); non-admin Windows processes get exactly one UAC popup per elevated call (winElevated.js's own comment documents batching multiple admin tasks into one script to avoid popup spam)
  - There is no rollback of the trust-store install if a later startup step fails: if Step 1.5 successfully installs the Root CA but the subsequent server spawn or its 8s health poll (pollMitmHealth) then fails, startServer only kills the spawned process and cleans up its lock/PID files — it never calls uninstallCert to undo the trust-store change it just made. uninstallCert is only ever invoked from the expiry-regeneration branch of Step 1, never on a failed startup and never from stopServer() (see mitm.hosts-file-atomic-write-and-rollback)
- **Errors:** `AUTH_ERROR` (a sudo password is required (mac/linux, isSudoPasswordRequired) to install the cert but none was supplied or cached — startServer throws 'Sudo password required to install Root CA certificate'), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (installCert itself throws (e.g. wrong sudo password, certutil failure) — wrapped and re-thrown as 'Failed to trust certificate: ...')

### 9Remote button + promo modal — zero backend, zero routes, zero persistence

- **id:** `remote.nineremote-promo-no-backend` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** User clicks the Remote button in the dashboard's top toolbar (NineRemoteButton)
- **Input:** none
- **Output:** A promo modal opens client-side; its only action button does window.open('https://9remote.cc', '_blank') — an external, separate SaaS product's marketing site
- **Rules:**
  - NineRemoteButton.js and NineRemotePromoModal.js are pure client components ('use client') with no fetch/API call anywhere in either file — confirmed by reading both files in full: no import of any /api/* path, no server action, no use of localDb/settings
  - There is no backend route under /api/remote, /api/nine-remote, or any similar path anywhere in src/app/api/ — the only 'remote'-adjacent routes in the app are the unrelated /api/tunnel/* (Cloudflare/Tailscale) routes traced elsewhere in this file
  - Nothing about this feature is persisted anywhere (no settings key, no DB row, no localStorage/cookie) — every render starts from the same static FEATURES/BULLETS arrays and the hardcoded NINE_REMOTE_URL constant
  - This is a pure marketing/promo surface for a separate paid product (9remote.cc), not a capability 9router itself implements. The spec excludes 9Remote from AIGate entirely — a later worker auditing 'missing routes for the Remote button' should treat that as expected, not as a gap to fill in
- **Note:** 9router's mechanism here is an accident of its stack. Behavior required, mechanism not.

### POST /api/tunnel/enable and /api/tunnel/disable — Cloudflare quick-tunnel lifecycle

- **id:** `tunnel.cloudflare-quick-tunnel-enable-disable` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard Endpoint page Enable/disable action for the Cloudflare tunnel row (client-side gated, see tunnel.enable-lacks-server-side-security-gate)
- **Input:** none (both POST with empty body)
- **Output:** enable: {success, tunnelUrl, shortId, publicUrl, alreadyRunning?}; disable: {success:true}
- **Rules:**
  - enableTunnel() first checks if cloudflared is already running AND both the direct trycloudflare.com URL and the public https://r{shortId}.abc-tunnel.us URL probe alive — only then does it reuse the existing tunnel instead of respawning, to avoid a stale socket surviving a network change
  - On a fresh spawn, the tunnel is registered with 9router's own worker (POST {WORKER_URL}/api/tunnel/register) to bind shortId -> tunnelUrl, before the public *.abc-tunnel.us URL is health-checked — the public URL depends on this external worker being reachable
  - POST /api/tunnel/enable waits a hardcoded DNS_WARMUP_DELAY_MS=8000ms after the tunnel registers, purely to let Cloudflare edge DNS propagate, before returning to the caller — a fixed sleep, not a poll-until-ready
  - disableTunnel() sets svc.cancelToken.cancelled=true first, specifically so that an enable already in flight (e.g. a slow spawn racing a user's disable click) cannot resurrect tunnelEnabled/tunnelUrl in settings after disable has cleared them (throwIfCancelled checks are sprinkled through enableTunnel)
- **Errors:** `INTERNAL_ERROR` (enableTunnel()/disableTunnel() throws (cloudflared spawn/exit error, health check failure) — caught and returned as {error: message} with status 500)

### The dashboard's 'do not expose without an API key / with weak dashboard auth' rule is enforced only in the React UI, not inside the tunnel-enable routes themselves

- **id:** `tunnel.enable-lacks-server-side-security-gate` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** A direct POST to /api/tunnel/enable or /api/tunnel/tailscale-enable (curl, a modified/compromised frontend build, or any script holding dashboard/CLI-token auth) instead of clicking the dashboard's Enable button
- **Input:** none
- **Output:** The tunnel or Tailscale Funnel is enabled and the gateway becomes reachable from the public internet, regardless of settings.requireApiKey, settings.requireLogin, or whether the dashboard still has the default password
- **Rules:**
  - EndpointPageClient.js's Cloudflare-row Enable handler refuses to open the enable modal when isLoginUnsafe (requireLogin off, or the dashboard still has the default password) or !requireApiKey is true, showing 'Security required: ...' instead — proving the product's own intended invariant is 'never let a user turn on public exposure while the endpoint has no key or the dashboard has weak auth'
  - That client-side guard is itself inconsistently applied: the Cloudflare row's onClick checks both isLoginUnsafe and !requireApiKey, but the Tailscale row's primary onClick (the not-yet-enabled state) checks only isLoginUnsafe — it never checks requireApiKey at all, so even the UI does not stop a user from enabling Tailscale Funnel while 'Require API key' is off. The Tailscale row's error-retry state (tsStatus?.type === 'error') is guarded even less: its Enable button calls handleOpenTsModal() directly with no check at all, not even isLoginUnsafe — so once a Tailscale enable attempt has failed once, retrying from that state skips every client-side guard entirely
  - None of this is enforced server-side: src/app/api/tunnel/enable/route.js and src/app/api/tunnel/tailscale-enable/route.js call enableTunnel()/enableTailscale() unconditionally on POST — neither route, nor src/lib/tunnel/**, nor src/mitm/manager.js (which both share code with) ever reads settings.requireApiKey, settings.requireLogin, or a 'dashboard has default password' flag
  - dashboardGuard.js does gate who may call these routes at all (LOCAL_ONLY_PATHS requires a loopback+authenticated caller or a valid machineId-derived CLI token; PROTECTED_API_PATHS additionally requires isAuthenticated for the /api/tunnel prefix generally) — but that answers 'is the caller allowed to manage the tunnel', not 'is it safe to expose the endpoint publicly given its current API-key/login posture'; those are two independent questions and only the first is enforced server-side
  - Once exposed, dashboardGuard.js's canAccessPublicLlmApi() (the /v1 gate) does not read settings.requireApiKey either — it grants access on isLocalRequest() OR a valid CLI token OR a real row in the apiKeys table (hasValidApiKey), independent of the 'Require API key' toggle. requireApiKey only gates the request inside each src/sse/handlers/*.js (e.g. chat.js, per endpoint.enforce-require-api-key) — reachable only for callers isLocalRequest() already let through
- **AIGate required behavior:** Given the dashboard UI already encodes 'do not let a tunnel/Funnel go live while requireApiKey is off or dashboard auth is weak', that same rule should be enforced inside POST /api/tunnel/enable and POST /api/tunnel/tailscale-enable themselves (or in enableTunnel()/enableTailscale()), so server-side state can never diverge from a client-only UI guard — and the guard should apply identically to both the Cloudflare and Tailscale rows.

### Full state machine across the 7 /api/tunnel/* routes for both the Cloudflare quick-tunnel and Tailscale Funnel lanes

- **id:** `tunnel.remote-access-state-machine` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard Endpoint page tunnel/Tailscale controls
- **Input:** POST with no body (enable/disable/tailscale-enable/tailscale-disable), POST { sudoPassword? } (tailscale-install), GET (status, tailscale-check)
- **Output:** Transitions through not-installed -> installed -> logged-in -> funnel-enabled -> running for Tailscale, or an implicit not-running -> running for Cloudflare (binary auto-downloaded on first enable, no separate install step)
- **Rules:**
  - Cloudflare lane collapses 'not installed' and 'installed' into one step: GET /api/tunnel/status never reports whether the cloudflared binary is present — enableTunnel() calls spawnQuickTunnel(), which calls ensureCloudflared() internally, auto-downloading the ~30MB binary from GitHub releases on the very first POST /api/tunnel/enable if missing. There is no separate 'install cloudflared' route or button.
  - Tailscale lane exposes every step as dashboard-visible state: GET /api/tunnel/tailscale-check reports {installed, loggedIn, daemonRunning}; POST /api/tunnel/tailscale-install (SSE) installs the binary and starts the daemon; POST /api/tunnel/tailscale-enable then must (a) start the daemon with a cached/supplied sudo password, (b) check login via isTailscaleLoggedInStrict — if not logged in, returns {needsLogin:true, authUrl} instead of erroring, expecting the caller to open authUrl and retry, (c) call startFunnel — if Tailscale's own Funnel feature isn't turned on for the tailnet, returns {funnelNotEnabled:true, enableUrl} rather than an error, again expecting a manual out-of-band step, then (d) re-verifies via the *Strict probes before persisting tailscaleEnabled=true
  - Both lanes persist their 'enabled' bit and public URL into 9router's own settings row (tunnelEnabled/tunnelUrl or tailscaleEnabled/tailscaleUrl), separate from the Cloudflare-lane-only shortId/tunnelUrl file at DATA_DIR/tunnel/state.json which only the Cloudflare code path reads/writes
  - 'Running' is re-derived on every status poll rather than trusted from the persisted flag: getTunnelStatus() only probes isCloudflaredRunning() (a PID-liveness check) when settings.tunnelEnabled is true (lazy skip), and getTailscaleStatus() only checks isTailscaleRunning() when isTailscaleLoggedIn() is true — so a persisted 'enabled=true' with a dead process reports enabled:false in status without ever clearing the stored settings flag itself
- **Errors:** `INTERNAL_ERROR` (any of the 7 routes' try/catch bodies catch a thrown error and return {error: error.message} with status 500)

### GET /api/tunnel/status — coalesced polling across both lanes plus download progress

- **id:** `tunnel.status-polling-and-caching` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard Endpoint page polling both tunnel lanes' live state
- **Input:** none
- **Output:** { tunnel: {enabled, settingsEnabled, tunnelUrl, shortId, publicUrl, running}, tailscale: {enabled, settingsEnabled, tunnelUrl, running, loggedIn}, download: {downloading, progress} }
- **Rules:**
  - A process-global 3s cache (global.__tunnelStatusCache — the same 'survive Next.js hot reload' pattern as consoleLogBuffer's global._*) coalesces rapid dashboard polls into one pair of underlying probes; the inline comment notes the underlying probes already self-cache for 10s, so this is a second, shorter coalescing layer on top
  - Download progress (cloudflared binary fetch) is deliberately excluded from the 3s cache and read live on every call via getDownloadStatus(), so the UI's download progress bar updates smoothly even while the rest of the payload is served from cache
  - enabled is derived as settingsEnabled && running for both lanes — a persisted 'enabled' setting alone never reports as enabled if the live process probe disagrees, but nothing here clears the stale settings flag (see tunnel.remote-access-state-machine)
- **Errors:** `INTERNAL_ERROR` (either probe throws — caught and returned as {error: message} with status 500)

### POST /api/tunnel/tailscale-enable and /api/tunnel/tailscale-disable — daemon start, login, Funnel activation

- **id:** `tunnel.tailscale-funnel-enable-disable` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** User clicks Enable on the Tailscale row once tailscale-check reports installed:true
- **Input:** none (POST, empty body)
- **Output:** enable: {success:true, tunnelUrl} on full success, or {success:false, needsLogin:true, authUrl} / {success:false, funnelNotEnabled:true, enableUrl} / {success:false, error} on partial outcomes; disable: {success:true}
- **Rules:**
  - enableTailscale() is a 4-stage sequential flow, each stage able to short-circuit the response before the next: (1) startDaemonWithPassword, (2) isTailscaleLoggedInStrict -> startLogin if false, (3) stopFunnel() then startFunnel() -> retries via startLogin if the funnel error looks like a not-logged-in condition, (4) a final isTailscaleLoggedInStrict + isTailscaleRunningStrict double-check after funnel start succeeds, tearing the funnel back down (stopFunnel) if that strict check fails (e.g. the device was removed from the tailnet mid-flow)
  - stopFunnel() is called unconditionally at the start of stage 3, before startFunnel() — every enable call tears down and rebuilds the funnel rather than checking if one is already correctly running, unlike the Cloudflare lane's explicit alive-probe-then-reuse path
  - TLS cert provisioning (provisionCert(hostname)) after a successful funnel start is explicitly non-fatal: provisionCert itself wraps its own tailscale-CLI call in a try/catch and only warns on failure, so enableTailscale can report success:true with a tunnelUrl that may not yet serve valid HTTPS
  - The post-funnel health check (waitForHealth) treats its own timeout as non-fatal (only re-throws non-timeout errors), returning success:true with reachableNow:false logged, relying on a background watchdog for eventual reachability rather than failing the enable call
  - disableTailscale() never stops the tailscaled daemon itself — only stopFunnel() — so the daemon (and any sudo password cached to start it in stage 1) keeps running after disable; only the public Funnel exposure is torn down
- **Errors:** `INTERNAL_ERROR` (any stage throws an error that isn't the recognized not-logged-in/funnel-not-enabled shape — caught by the route and returned as {error: message} with status 500)

### POST /api/tunnel/tailscale-install (SSE) and GET /api/tunnel/tailscale-check

- **id:** `tunnel.tailscale-install-sse-flow` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** User clicks Enable on the Tailscale row when tailscale-check reports installed:false, or explicitly retries install
- **Input:** POST { sudoPassword? } (falls back to cached/encrypted password shared with the MITM subsystem); GET (check) takes nothing
- **Output:** check: {installed, loggedIn, platform, brewAvailable, daemonRunning, customDaemonRunning, systemDaemonRunning, hasCachedPassword}; install: SSE stream of {event: progress|done|error}
- **Rules:**
  - tailscale-install reuses the exact same cached/encrypted sudo password store as the MITM subsystem (getCachedPassword/loadEncryptedPassword imported from @/mitm/manager) — entering a sudo password once for MITM makes it available to Tailscale install and vice versa, an intentional cross-feature convenience, not a coincidence of shared code
  - A password is only required (needsPassword) on non-Windows, non-Homebrew-macOS platforms; Windows and Homebrew-installed-macOS paths install without any sudo password prompt at all
  - tailscale-check runs three daemon probes in parallel (a custom daemon via its own socket, the system daemon, and Homebrew availability) rather than a single check, because Tailscale can be running via 9router's own bundled daemon binary, the OS's system-installed tailscaled, or not at all — the UI needs to distinguish all three to decide what Enable should even do next
  - installTailscale's progress callback streams free-text messages as SSE 'progress' events with no structured stage/step field — the dashboard can only display them as a scrolling log, not drive a stepper UI off them
- **Streaming:** yes
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (a sudo password is required (non-Windows, non-brew) but none was supplied or cached — returns 400 'Sudo password is required'), `AUTH_ERROR` (installTailscale rejects with a message containing 'incorrect password' or 'Sorry' — surfaced over SSE as {event:'error', error:'Wrong sudo password'})

## Request routing

### Upstream URL construction (compatible-prefix rule, runtime transport, gemini path, accountId template)

- **id:** `routing.build-url` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** Every attempt inside executor.execute (called per baseUrl index, including retries)
- **Input:** model, stream, urlIndex, credentials (providerSpecificData.baseUrl / apiType, runtimeTransport)
- **Output:** The absolute upstream URL
- **Rules:**
  - Q6 exact rule: for openai-compatible-* the base is providerSpecificData.baseUrl (default https://api.openai.com/v1), ONE trailing slash is removed with replace(/\/$/, ""), then "/responses" (apiType responses) or "/chat/completions" is appended. No /v1 detection of any kind: "https://x/v1" -> "https://x/v1/chat/completions", "https://x" -> "https://x/chat/completions" (no /v1 added), "https://x/v1/chat/completions" -> "https://x/v1/chat/completions/chat/completions"
  - anthropic-compatible-*: same single trailing-slash strip, then "/messages" (default base https://api.anthropic.com/v1). Node creation strips a pasted trailing /messages, but the openai-compatible create path does not strip a pasted /chat/completions
  - DefaultExecutor order: runtimeTransport baseUrl(+urlSuffix) first, then the compatible prefixes, then gemini-format `${baseUrl}/${model}:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse | :generateContent`, then registry urlSuffix, then {accountId} template substitution (throws if accountId missing), else config.baseUrl
  - BaseExecutor (specialized executors that do not override buildUrl) returns baseUrls[urlIndex] || baseUrls[0] || config.baseUrl
  - apiType resolution: stored providerSpecificData.apiType chat|responses wins; otherwise a provider id containing "responses" means responses
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (baseUrl contains {accountId} but providerSpecificData.accountId is empty — buildUrl throws, surfacing as a 502 from chatCore's catch)

### Claude-CLI warmup / title / count requests answered locally without any provider call

- **id:** `routing.bypass-canned-responses` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** user-agent contains claude-cli and the message list matches one of the bypass patterns
- **Input:** body.messages, model string, user-agent, settings.ccFilterNaming
- **Output:** A canned assistant response in the client's format (stream or JSON), never touching an account
- **Rules:**
  - Bypass is checked BEFORE combo expansion so that warmup traffic does not consume a combo round-robin slot
  - Patterns: last assistant message text is exactly "{" (title extraction), first message text is "Warmup", single user message "count", any SKIP_PATTERNS text, and (with ccFilterNaming) the naming prompt — which gets a synthetic {isNewTopic, title} built from the first 3 words of the user message
  - Only user-agents containing claude-cli are ever bypassed; every other client goes to a real provider
  - The same check runs a second time inside handleChatCore with the provider-stripped model name (belt and braces for callers that enter chatCore directly)
- **Streaming:** yes

### Single-model request silently widened into an adapter combo when the model lacks a hard capability

- **id:** `routing.capacity-adapter-solo` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** A non-combo request whose body needs a hard capability (e.g. an image) that the requested model does not satisfy
- **Input:** modelStr, required capabilities, settings (capacity adapter models)
- **Output:** Either the plain single-model path, or a handleComboChat run over [requested model, adapter models...]
- **Rules:**
  - augmentModelsWithCapacityAdapter returns the list unchanged when there are no hard capabilities required or any listed model already satisfies them
  - Otherwise adapter models that satisfy the capability are appended; if the result has more than one model the request is run as a combo named after the requested model, using the adapter's active strategy
  - withCapacityAdapterStripping wraps the per-model executor so adapter-added models get the adapter-specific body treatment
- **Streaming:** yes

### Cancelling the upstream request when the client goes away

- **id:** `routing.client-disconnect-propagation` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** The client closes the connection at any point in the request
- **Input:** Next's cancellation of the returned response body; request.signal (never read)
- **Output:** Upstream fetch aborted — only in the streaming phase
- **Rules:**
  - The only link from client to upstream is streamController: its AbortController signal is merged into every fetch, and it is aborted by handleDisconnect, which is called from the ReadableStream cancel() of the returned SSE body
  - handleDisconnect delays the abort by 500 ms to allow cleanup, then aborts; cancel() also cancels the reader chain, which cancels the upstream body
  - request.signal is never read on the chat lane (the video lane is the only one that passes it), and handleChat never passes onDisconnect to handleChatCore
  - Q4: before the streaming Response is returned (translation, image prefetch, headroom/pxpipe, up to 249 s of connect timeouts and retries per URL, token refresh, trying further accounts and combo members) a client disconnect is NOT propagated — work continues and further accounts may be tried and locked for nobody. Non-streaming requests are never cancelled
- **Streaming:** yes
