- **AIGate required behavior:** A client disconnect cancels the upstream call and stops retry/fallback at any stage

### Combo detection and hand-off to the combo/fusion engine

- **id:** `routing.combo-dispatch` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** body.model has no "/" and names a combo row with at least one model
- **Input:** Combo name, body, settings.comboStrategies[name], settings.comboStrategy, settings.comboStickyRoundRobinLimit
- **Output:** The Response of the first combo member that succeeds (or the fusion result, or an all-failed error)
- **Rules:**
  - Required capabilities (vision/audio/etc.) are detected from the body once, before combo lookup
  - Strategy precedence: combo-specific comboStrategies[name].fallbackStrategy, then global settings.comboStrategy, then "fallback"
  - "fusion" goes to handleFusionChat with the ORIGINAL combo list (no capacity-adapter augmentation); panel calls get a clientRawRequest with tools/tool_choice stripped
  - Every other strategy goes to handleComboChat with the capacity-adapter-augmented list; each member is executed through handleSingleModelChat, i.e. the full per-account loop below runs once per combo member
  - The same combo branch is duplicated inside handleSingleModelChat for the case where getModelInfo returns provider null for a combo name reached through an alias
  - Combo ordering, rotation, fusion and per-model fallback rules are traced by Task 11; this entry records only the hand-off point
- **Streaming:** yes

### POST /v1/messages/count_tokens — local character-based estimate

- **id:** `routing.count-tokens-estimate` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** POST /v1/messages/count_tokens (Claude Code preflight)
- **Input:** Anthropic Messages body (system, tools, messages)
- **Output:** { input_tokens: ceil(chars / 4) }
- **Rules:**
  - Never routed to a provider and never touches accounts, API-key enforcement or usage
  - Characters counted: system + tools (keys and values) + each message's content; text blocks count text, tool_use counts name + input, tool_result counts content, thinking counts thinking; total / 4 rounded up
  - Invalid JSON -> 400 {error: 'Invalid JSON body'}
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (body is not JSON — 400)

### Proactive token refresh and project-id cold miss before dispatch

- **id:** `routing.credential-preparation` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** After an account is selected, before handleChatCore
- **Input:** provider, the selected credentials
- **Output:** refreshedCredentials passed to handleChatCore; onCredentialsRefreshed / onRequestSuccess callbacks bound to this connection
- **Rules:**
  - checkAndRefreshToken runs unconditionally after every selection (mechanics in auth.refresh-generic-grant / auth.refresh-provider-specific)
  - antigravity and gemini-cli need a real projectId: if missing it is fetched synchronously on the request path, then persisted in the background (fire-and-forget, errors swallowed)
  - onCredentialsRefreshed persists reactive refresh results with testStatus active; onRequestSuccess clears the account's error/lock for this model and the Antigravity strike counter
  - Per-request toggles read from settings here: providerThinking[provider], rtk/headroom/caveman/ponytail/pxpipe flags, ccFilterNaming

### Unregistered provider id silently inherits the OpenAI transport config

- **id:** `routing.default-executor-openai-fallback` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** A chat request whose resolved provider id has no PROVIDERS entry and is not openai-compatible-* / anthropic-compatible-*, while an active connection exists for it — reachable today via a custom-embedding node prefix on /v1/chat/completions
- **Input:** model "<embeddingNodePrefix>/<model>"
- **Output:** A POST to https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions carrying that node's API key as Bearer
- **Rules:**
  - getModelInfo maps custom-embedding node prefixes to the node id (custom-embedding-...) on every lane, including chat
  - getProviderCredentials finds the node's connection, so the account loop proceeds
  - getExecutor has no entry -> DefaultExecutor(provider) with config PROVIDERS.openai because the id is not in the registry
  - DefaultExecutor.buildUrl only reads providerSpecificData.baseUrl for openai-compatible-* and anthropic-compatible-* prefixes; for custom-embedding-* it falls through to this.config.baseUrl, i.e. OpenAI's chat URL
- **Errors:** `AUTH_ERROR` (OpenAI rejects the foreign key with 401 — then the node's account is locked 2 minutes)
- **AIGate required behavior:** A provider id with no transport config is rejected (or an embedding-only node is refused on the chat lane) before any upstream call

### getExecutor — specialized map, aliases, DefaultExecutor fallback

- **id:** `routing.executor-selection` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** handleChatCore just before dispatch
- **Input:** resolved provider id
- **Output:** An executor instance
- **Rules:**
  - A fixed map holds one singleton instance per specialized provider (antigravity, azure, gemini-cli, github, iflow, qoder, kiro, kimchi, codex, cursor, vertex, vertex-partner, opencode, opencode-go, grok-web, grok-cli, perplexity-web, ollama-local, commandcode, xiaomi-tokenplan, mimo-free, codebuddy-cn, codebuddy-intl, trae, zed, windsurf, devin-cli)
  - Alias keys cu, gcli, gb and mmf map to SEPARATE new instances of the cursor, grok-cli and mimo-free executors
  - Any provider id not in the map falls back to new DefaultExecutor(provider), cached per id in defaultCache for the process lifetime
  - DefaultExecutor's config is PROVIDERS[provider], or PROVIDERS.openai when the id has no registry entry
  - Q7: the fallback is correct for registry providers (their transport config drives URL/auth) and for openai-compatible-* / anthropic-compatible-* nodes (URL comes from providerSpecificData.baseUrl). It is wrong for an id with no PROVIDERS entry that is not a compatible node — see routing.default-executor-openai-fallback

### Chat-lane route handlers that hand the request to handleChat

- **id:** `routing.lane-entry-routes` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** POST /v1/chat/completions, /v1/messages or /v1/responses (after the next.config.mjs rewrite to /api/v1/*)
- **Input:** The raw Next Request (headers + JSON body)
- **Output:** Whatever handleChat returns — a JSON or SSE Response
- **Rules:**
  - All three chat-shaped routes are identical: they call initTranslators() once per module instance, then return handleChat(request) unchanged — the route itself does no parsing, auth or format detection
  - The three endpoints are NOT distinguished by the route: the endpoint path is re-read later by detectFormatByEndpoint (see routing.source-format-detection) to pick the client wire format
  - OPTIONS preflight on each route returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * with GET, POST, OPTIONS and any header
- **Streaming:** yes

### Drop media the model cannot read; inline remote images for targets that cannot fetch URLs

- **id:** `routing.modality-strip-prefetch` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** Every non-passthrough request, before translation
- **Input:** body, sourceFormat, targetFormat, capabilities of provider/model
- **Output:** body mutated in place — unsupported vision/audio/pdf blocks removed, remote image URLs replaced by base64
- **Rules:**
  - Capabilities come from getCapabilitiesForModel on the already-resolved provider/model (catalog.capability-tier-fallback)
  - Stripping is silent: no error is returned to the client when media is removed
  - Image prefetch failure is caught and logged; the request continues with the URL untouched (fail-open)

### Model string to {provider, model}

- **id:** `routing.model-resolution` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** handleSingleModelChat entry, once per model tried
- **Input:** "provider/model", "alias/model", "nodePrefix/model", or a bare alias/combo name
- **Output:** { provider, model } — provider null means combo, or unresolvable
- **Rules:**
  - "x/y": x is resolved through ALIAS_TO_PROVIDER_ID (registry id, alias, aliases[]); unknown x is kept as-is as the provider id
  - If x is not a reserved built-in prefix, openai-compatible, then anthropic-compatible, then custom-embedding provider nodes are matched by their user-defined prefix and the node id becomes the provider
  - A bare name is checked as a combo first, then as a model alias (alias semantics in catalog.alias-resolve-before-capability)
  - provider null and not a combo -> 400 "Invalid model format"
  - An unknown provider prefix is not rejected here; it fails later at account selection with 404 "No active credentials"
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (bare name that is neither a combo nor an alias — 400 Invalid model format)

### Same-ecosystem CLI to provider — skip translation

- **id:** `routing.native-passthrough` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** The detected client tool and the provider belong to the same ecosystem (isNativePassthrough)
- **Input:** clientRawRequest headers + body, provider
- **Output:** translatedBody = client body with only the model swapped (and codex reasoning effort / Claude passthrough normalization)
- **Rules:**
  - Passthrough skips modality stripping, image prefetch and translateRequest entirely — only the model id (with any thinking suffix removed) changes, and the Bearer is swapped by the executor
  - codex passthrough: a thinking suffix on the model becomes body.reasoning.effort and top-level reasoning_effort is deleted
  - claude passthrough: normalizeClaudePassthrough rewrites newer Cowork/Claude Code beta shapes the API rejects; after all token savers run, anchorClaudeCache re-pins cache breakpoints on the final body

### Non-streaming response parse, translation and return

- **id:** `routing.non-streaming-response` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** stream is false and upstream is ok
- **Input:** providerResponse (JSON, or SSE text when the upstream streamed anyway)
- **Output:** { success: true, response: JSON } in the client's format
- **Rules:**
  - An SSE content-type is parsed into one OpenAI response; parse failure -> 502 'Invalid SSE response for non-streaming request'. JSON parse failure -> 502 'Invalid JSON response from <provider>'
  - Tool names are decloaked on the raw body before translation; translateNonStreamingResponse runs when target != source
  - Post-fixes: finish_reason forced to tool_calls when tool_calls exist; object/created filled; Azure prompt_filter_results/content_filter_results removed; usage buffered and filtered to the client format; reasoning_content dropped when content is non-empty
- **Errors:** `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (2xx body is not parseable JSON/SSE — 502, which then locks the account 30 s and tries the next (fallback.error-classification))
- **AIGate required behavior:** The usage a client receives is the usage the vendor reported

### POST /v1/api/chat — Ollama-native clients

- **id:** `routing.ollama-lane-transform` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** POST /v1/api/chat (Ollama API path)
- **Input:** Ollama chat body (model defaults to llama3.2 for the transform label)
- **Output:** NDJSON lines {model, message, done} built from the OpenAI-format SSE that handleChat returns
- **Rules:**
  - The body is cloned to read the model name, then the request goes through handleChat unchanged; source format is body-sniffed (no endpoint override for this path)
  - transformToOllama only understands `data:` SSE lines: content deltas become done:false lines, tool_call deltas are accumulated and emitted on finish_reason, and done:true is emitted on [DONE], on finish, and again in flush
  - The outgoing Response defaults to status 200 and Content-Type application/x-ndjson whenever handleChat returned a body — the handleChat status is not copied in that case. Only when handleChat's response has NO body at all does the original status get copied through instead
- **Streaming:** yes
- **Errors:** `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (handleChat returns an error JSON (which has a body) — it has no data: lines, so the client receives only {done:true} with HTTP 200)
- **AIGate required behavior:** Upstream errors surface to Ollama clients with an error status, and non-streaming requests return the answer

### Body parse, 1M-context marker strip, API-key gate, missing-model check

- **id:** `routing.request-preflight` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** First thing handleChat does for every chat-lane request
- **Input:** Request JSON body (body.model), Authorization / x-api-key headers, settings.requireApiKey
- **Output:** Either an early error Response or a parsed body with body.model stripped of a trailing [1m] marker
- **Rules:**
  - Order is fixed: (1) request.json() — failure returns 400 "Invalid JSON body"; (2) build clientRawRequest {endpoint, body, headers} for logging; (3) strip a Claude Code `<model>[1m]` context marker from body.model; (4) API-key enforcement; (5) missing model -> 400 "Missing model"
  - The [1m] marker is removed before any combo/alias/provider lookup because it matches none of them; the capability itself still travels in the anthropic-beta header, which is forwarded unchanged
  - API key enforcement only runs when settings.requireApiKey is true — missing key and invalid key both return 401 (details in endpoint.enforce-require-api-key)
  - The model check runs AFTER the API-key check, so an unauthenticated request with no model gets 401, not 400
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (body is not valid JSON — 400 Invalid JSON body), `AUTH_ERROR` (requireApiKey is true and the key is missing or invalid — 401), `INVALID_REQUEST` (body.model is empty after marker strip — 400 Missing model)

### translateRequest — direct source:target route or OpenAI pivot

- **id:** `routing.request-translation` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** Non-passthrough request, sourceFormat and targetFormat known
- **Input:** sourceFormat, targetFormat, upstream model, body, stream, credentials, provider, strip list
- **Output:** translatedBody (target-shaped), with _toolNameMap / _customToolNames side channels lifted off by chatCore
- **Rules:**
  - Translators self-register by register(from, to, reqFn, resFn) as an import side effect; the static import list at the bottom of translator/index.js is the registry
  - Pre-steps for every translation: strip opt-in content types, normalizeThinkingConfig, ensureToolCallIds, fixMissingToolResponses (skipped for kiro), capture thinking intent and session id from the untranslated body
  - Same format -> no translator runs. Different format -> if requestRegistry has the exact `${source}:${target}` key it runs as a direct route (e.g. claude:kiro); otherwise source->openai then openai->target
  - Post-steps: applyThinking to the target format (skipped when kiro translators map it themselves), filterToOpenAIFormat for openai targets, prepareClaudeRequest for claude targets, tool-name cloaking for providers flagged cloakToolsOnOAuth when the token is an sk-ant-oat OAuth token
  - chatCore then forces translatedBody.model to the thinking-suffix-free upstream id and strips encrypted_content continuity fields so they never reach upstream
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (translateRequest returns a falsy body — createErrorResult 400, which the account loop then treats as an account failure (fallback.error-classification)), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (a translator throws — not caught in handleChatCore; propagates out of handleSingleModelChat (single model: unhandled, route returns 500; combo: caught and next member tried))

### Choosing forced SSE-to-JSON, plain JSON, or streaming handling for a 2xx response

- **id:** `routing.response-mode-dispatch` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** Upstream response is ok
- **Input:** clientRequestedStreaming, providerRequiresStreaming, stream
- **Output:** The result object from one of the three handlers
- **Rules:**
  - Provider forces streaming and the client did not ask for it -> handleForcedSSEToJson collapses the SSE into one JSON body
  - stream false -> handleNonStreamingResponse
  - Otherwise -> buildOnStreamComplete + handleStreamingResponse
  - Pending-request counters (dashboard live view) are incremented before dispatch and decremented on each terminal path; the decrement clamps at 0 so double decrements are harmless
- **Streaming:** yes

### POST /v1/responses/compact — compaction via the same pipeline with body._compact

- **id:** `routing.responses-compact-lane` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** POST /v1/responses/compact
- **Input:** Responses-API body
- **Output:** handleChat result; for codex the upstream URL should gain /compact
- **Rules:**
  - The route parses the body, sets body._compact = true, rebuilds a Request with the original headers and hands it to handleChat — full routing/fallback applies
  - Only CodexExecutor consumes the flag: transformRequest stores this._isCompact and deletes body._compact; buildUrl appends /compact when this._isCompact is true
  - BaseExecutor.execute calls buildUrl BEFORE transformRequest, so the URL of a request is computed from the _isCompact value left by the PREVIOUS codex request on this singleton executor
- **Streaming:** yes
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (body is not JSON — request.json() throws in the route (unhandled, 500), unlike the 400 of the other lanes)
- **AIGate required behavior:** A compact request goes to .../responses/compact and a normal request to .../responses

### Deciding the client's wire format

- **id:** `routing.source-format-detection` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** handleChatCore entry
- **Input:** Request pathname and body
- **Output:** sourceFormat — openai, openai-responses, claude, gemini, antigravity
- **Rules:**
  - Endpoint wins first: a path containing /v1/responses is openai-responses; /v1/messages is claude; /v1/chat/completions with an input[] array is openai (Cursor CLI sends a Responses body to the chat endpoint)
  - Otherwise body sniffing, in order: input (array or string) without messages -> openai-responses; request.contents + userAgent antigravity -> antigravity; contents[] -> gemini; any OpenAI-only field (stream_options, response_format, logprobs, n, penalties, logit_bias, user) -> openai; Claude-shaped content blocks or system/anthropic_version -> claude; default openai

### Whether the upstream call streams, and whether the client gets SSE

- **id:** `routing.stream-mode-decision` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** handleChatCore, before translation
- **Input:** body.stream, sourceFormat, PROVIDERS[provider].forceStream, model type, detected client tool, Accept header
- **Output:** stream (upstream mode) and clientRequestedStreaming (drives the SSE->JSON collapse)
- **Rules:**
  - clientRequestedStreaming is true only when body.stream === true or the source format is antigravity/gemini/gemini-cli (always-streaming protocols)
  - stream = true when the provider forces streaming; otherwise body.stream !== false — an OMITTED stream flag means streaming
  - Image-generation models on antigravity/gemini-cli are forced non-streaming
  - deepseek-tui without an explicit stream:true is forced non-streaming
  - Accept: application/json without text/event-stream, and no explicit stream:true, and no forceStream -> non-streaming (AI SDK compatibility)
  - forceStream provider + client did not request streaming -> upstream streams, response is collapsed to JSON (routing.response-mode-dispatch)
- **Streaming:** yes
- **AIGate required behavior:** An omitted stream flag means non-streaming, as in the OpenAI and Anthropic APIs this endpoint emulates

### Upstream SSE -> transform -> disconnect-aware stream -> client (first byte)

- **id:** `routing.streaming-pipeline` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** Streaming response branch
- **Input:** providerResponse, sourceFormat, targetFormat (or the executor's responseFormat), provider
- **Output:** { success: true, response: new Response(transformedBody, SSE headers) } — returned as soon as headers are ok, before any token is read
- **Rules:**
  - Non-SSE guard: if the 2xx content-type is neither text/event-stream nor application/json (e.g. a Cloudflare HTML page), the body is read, the <title> is extracted and sanitized (tags removed, 160 chars) and a success:false JSON error is returned instead of piping HTML
  - Response translation choice: Responses-format providers (codex) translate Responses SSE into the client's format via CODEX_SOURCE_TO_TARGET (droid/codex-cli user agents excluded); otherwise translate when targetFormat != sourceFormat; else passthrough with usage/[DONE] fix-ups
  - Response translation mirrors the request side: direct `${target}:${source}` translator if registered, else target->openai->source pivot; same format only decloaks tool names
  - Stall watchdog: any upstream byte re-arms a timer of PROVIDERS[provider].stallTimeoutMs or STREAM_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS (env, default 360 s); on expiry the stream is errored and the upstream fetch aborted. The timer starts when piping starts, so it is also the only time-to-first-token bound on the generic lane (STREAM_FIRST_CHUNK_TIMEOUT_MS is used only by kiro)
  - A placeholder request-detail row ('[Streaming in progress...]') is saved immediately; buildOnStreamComplete later overwrites it by id
- **Streaming:** yes
- **Errors:** `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (2xx with an HTML/text content type — success:false with the 2xx status, which the account loop then treats as an account failure), `TIMEOUT` (no upstream bytes for the stall timeout — stream aborted)

### When an account is marked healthy (onRequestSuccess)

- **id:** `routing.success-callback-timing` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** A 2xx response reaches a response handler
- **Input:** onRequestSuccess from chat.js (clearAccountError + clearAntigravityStrikes)
- **Output:** Account error/lock state for this model cleared
- **Rules:**
  - Streaming: fired as a microtask at the top of handleStreamingResponse — before the non-SSE guard and before any token is read
  - Non-streaming: fired (not awaited) after the body has been parsed successfully
  - Forced SSE->JSON: awaited after the SSE has been collapsed
- **Streaming:** yes

### POST /v1/systemone forwards a decision payload through account fallback

- **id:** `routing.systemone-decision-lane` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** POST /v1/systemone (OPTIONS handles CORS preflight)
- **Input:** JSON with model, state, and questions object
- **Output:** Upstream JSON decision body or classified error response
- **Rules:**
  - The route delegates to handleSystemone, which validates JSON, API key when requireApiKey is enabled, required state/questions, and model alias resolution.
  - It selects one provider account, refreshes credentials, dispatches a native decision payload through systemoneCore, and tries the next account only when markAccountUnavailable allows fallback.
  - Core uses the provider's systemoneConfig URL/headers and forwards the body with resolved model, without chat translation; successful upstream usage is recorded when supplied.
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (JSON, model, state, or questions is missing/invalid), `AUTH_ERROR` (requireApiKey is enabled and key is absent/invalid), `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (provider lacks systemoneConfig or all accounts fail)

### Choosing the upstream format and endpoint (runtime transport)

- **id:** `routing.target-format-transport` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** handleChatCore, after source-format detection
- **Input:** provider, model, sourceFormat, credentials
- **Output:** targetFormat, upstreamModel id, strip list, and (multi-endpoint providers) credentials.runtimeTransport
- **Rules:**
  - Multi-endpoint providers declare transports[]; the one whose format equals sourceFormat is chosen so the request needs zero translation
  - Per-model guard: when the model declares supportedFormats, the source-matched transport is only used if sourceFormat is in that list (opencode-go kimi/glm only do /chat/completions)
  - Precedence: matched transport format > model-level targetFormat > provider format (openai-compatible -> openai or openai-responses by apiType; anthropic-compatible -> claude; else PROVIDERS[provider].format, else openai)
  - The chosen transport is attached to credentials.runtimeTransport and later overrides URL, headers and auth in DefaultExecutor
  - getModelUpstreamId maps the catalog model id to the vendor's wire id; provider-level thinking mode (on/off/effort) is injected here only if the client did not set its own

### Final-body mutations before dispatch (tool dedupe, RTK, headroom, caveman, ponytail, pxpipe)

- **id:** `routing.token-saver-pipeline` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** After translation/passthrough, every request
- **Input:** translatedBody, finalFormat, settings token-saver flags, x-9router-token-saver header
- **Output:** translatedBody mutated in place (or replaced by pxpipe)
- **Rules:**
  - Fixed order: Claude-client tool dedupe, TTS tool stripping, default Claude tool type, RTK, headroom, caveman, ponytail, pxpipe (pxpipe is last so it sees the final body)
  - Header x-9router-token-saver: off disables RTK, headroom, caveman and ponytail for this request; pxpipe is gated only by its own setting
  - All savers are fail-open — headroom absence is logged as skipped, pxpipe event reporting errors are swallowed

### When token usage is persisted relative to the response being flushed

- **id:** `routing.usage-recording-timing` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** Successful non-streaming, forced-JSON, or streaming completion
- **Input:** Usage extracted from the upstream response or accumulated from the stream (estimated when absent)
- **Output:** A usageHistory row via saveUsageStats -> saveRequestUsage (fire-and-forget), plus a requestDetails row
- **Rules:**
  - Q8 non-streaming: usage is extracted and saveUsageStats is called BEFORE the response is translated and returned — i.e. before the flush; the write itself is not awaited (it runs concurrently with the return)
  - Q8 forced SSE->JSON: onRequestSuccess is awaited, then usage saved, then the JSON Response is returned — before the flush
  - Q8 streaming: finalizeStream runs AFTER the terminal bytes are enqueued — in flush() for normal ends, or inside transform() on the Responses terminal event (because Responses clients close right after it and flush never runs). The save runs concurrently with the final flush to the client
  - When the upstream sends no usage, it is estimated from the request body and emitted content length
  - Rows with zero input and zero output tokens are not written at all
- **Streaming:** yes
- **Errors:** `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (stream errors or is cancelled before its terminal event — flush never runs, usage is never recorded)
- **AIGate required behavior:** Tokens the provider billed are recorded even when the stream ends abnormally or the client leaves

### GET /v1 re-exports the model listing

- **id:** `routing.v1-root-alias` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** GET or OPTIONS /v1
- **Input:** None
- **Output:** Same response as GET /v1/models
- **Rules:**
  - The /v1 root route is a one-line re-export of the models route's GET and OPTIONS; it is not part of the chat routing chain

## Settings

### GET /api/auth/status — unauthenticated auth-configuration probe

- **id:** `identity.auth-status-disclosure` · **module:** `identity`
- **Trigger:** Login page loads (before any credential is submitted), or any caller of GET /api/auth/status
- **Input:** none
- **Output:** 200 JSON describing the current auth configuration and, if a valid session exists, that session's display identity — never the password hash or OIDC/SAML secret values
- **Rules:**
  - The route is unauthenticated by design ('/api/auth/status' is in dashboardGuard.js's PUBLIC_API_PATHS) so the login page can render the right form (password vs SSO button, custom login labels) before the caller has any credential
  - Fields returned to an unauthenticated caller include requireLogin, authMode, ssoType, oidcConfigured/samlConfigured (booleans only), the operator-customized login-button labels, and hasPassword (whether any password hash has ever been set) — none are secret values, but hasPassword does tell an unauthenticated network caller whether the install is still in its unset/first-run password state
  - authenticated defaults to false and displayName/loginMethod fall back to generic strings ('Password user'/'Password') when getDashboardAuthSession(cookie) returns null, so an unauthenticated caller learns nothing about who (if anyone) is logged in via another session
  - A thrown error (e.g. malformed settings JSON) is swallowed and answered with a hardcoded safe-default body (requireLogin: true, everything else false/null) instead of a 500 — the route never fails closed into an error response

### OIDC authorization-code + PKCE login (start → IdP → callback)

- **id:** `identity.oidc-login-flow` · **module:** `identity`
- **Trigger:** GET /api/auth/oidc/start (user clicks the OIDC login button), then the IdP redirects back to GET /api/auth/oidc/callback
- **Input:** start: none; callback: ?code=...&state=... query params from the IdP redirect
- **Output:** start: 302 redirect to the IdP authorization endpoint; callback: 302 redirect to /dashboard on success (session cookie set) or to /login?error=... on any failure
- **Rules:**
  - Settings keys that drive OIDC: settings.authMode must be 'oidc' or 'both' AND settings.oidcIssuerUrl + oidcClientId + oidcClientSecret must all be non-empty (getOidcRuntimeConfig / isOidcConfigured) — missing any one disables /start entirely (redirects straight to /login?error=oidc_not_configured)
  - CSRF protection: a random 16-byte state value is generated per /start call, stored in an httpOnly oidc_state cookie (10 min maxAge), and the callback rejects the exchange outright ('oidc_invalid_state') if the returned ?state= does not exactly match the cookie, or if any of the three OIDC cookies is missing
  - Replay protection: a random 16-byte nonce is generated per /start call, stored in oidc_nonce, and passed through to verifyOidcIdToken, which requires the id_token's nonce claim to match via jose's jwtVerify options (a library-enforced claim check, not a manual string compare after the fact) — a mismatched nonce fails verification and throws
  - PKCE (S256) is used unconditionally: a code_verifier/code_challenge pair is generated at /start, the challenge sent in the authorize URL, and the verifier sent to the token endpoint at exchange time — on top of, not instead of, the state/nonce checks
  - The returned identity maps to a session by embedding oidc: true, oidcSub, oidcEmail, oidcName as extra JWT claims on the same auth_token cookie used by password login — there is no separate OIDC session type
  - The id_token is verified against the IdP's live JWKS (createRemoteJWKSet), with issuer and audience (=clientId) both enforced — a token signed by a different issuer or intended for a different client is rejected
- **Errors:** `AUTH_ERROR` (state cookie missing or mismatched, or any of the three OIDC cookies absent), `AUTH_ERROR` (id_token missing, signature invalid, or issuer/audience/nonce mismatch/expired), `INVALID_REQUEST` (code or state query param missing from the callback URL)

### POST /api/auth/oidc/test — validate an OIDC configuration before saving it

- **id:** `identity.oidc-test-probe` · **module:** `identity`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard admin clicks "Test connection" on the OIDC settings form, before or after saving
- **Input:** { issuerUrl?, clientId?, clientSecret?, scopes? } — any field omitted falls back to the currently-saved setting
- **Output:** 200 { ok, discoveryOk, clientSecretTested, clientSecretValid, authorizationEndpoint, tokenEndpoint, jwksUri, ... } — never echoes the client secret back
- **Rules:**
  - Access requires the same gate as a protected dashboard action: settings.requireLogin === false lets anyone through, otherwise the auth_token cookie must verify — implemented locally in the route (canAccessTestRoute) rather than via dashboardGuard's PROTECTED_API_PATHS, because '/api/auth/oidc' is otherwise entirely in PUBLIC_API_PATHS (needed for /start and /callback)
  - The route accepts issuerUrl/clientId/clientSecret in the request body as overrides of the stored settings, so an admin can test a new IdP configuration before saving it — this means an authenticated caller can direct the server to fetch discovery from an arbitrary attacker-chosen issuerUrl
  - Secret validation is a live probe, not a local check: probeOidcClientSecret POSTs a deliberately-invalid authorization code to the IdP's real token endpoint with the given client_secret; an invalid_client/unauthorized_client response means the secret is wrong, while invalid_grant/invalid_code means the secret was accepted and only the intentionally-bogus code failed
- **Errors:** `AUTH_ERROR` (requireLogin is true and the caller has no valid auth_token), `INVALID_REQUEST` (issuerUrl or clientId missing after merging body and stored settings)

### POST /api/auth/reset-password — reset the dashboard password to the install default

- **id:** `identity.reset-password-local-only` · **module:** `identity`
- **Trigger:** A local-machine caller (browser on loopback + already authenticated, or a valid machineId-derived CLI token) POSTs with no body
- **Input:** none
- **Output:** 200 { success: true }; settings.password is cleared (set to null)
- **Rules:**
  - The route performs no current-password check at all — it unconditionally sets settings.password to null via updateSettings, so the next login falls back to the process.env.INITIAL_PASSWORD-or-'123456' comparison in the login route; this IS the 'forgot password' recovery path, not a self-service password rotation
  - Who may call it is enforced entirely outside the route body, in dashboardGuard.js: '/api/auth/reset-password' is in LOCAL_ONLY_PATHS, so canAccessLocalOnlyRoute requires either a valid x-9r-cli-token header (machineId-derived) or (isLocalRequest(request) AND isAuthenticated(request)) — an already-logged-in browser session on loopback, or the CLI, not a bare unauthenticated caller
  - Because the browser branch of canAccessLocalOnlyRoute requires isAuthenticated() (valid JWT OR requireLogin===false) in addition to isLocalRequest(), a fully logged-out local browser with requireLogin still true cannot call this route either — matching the route's own comment 'Local-only (enforced by dashboardGuard)'
- **Errors:** `INTERNAL_ERROR` (updateSettings throws)

### SAML 2.0 SP-initiated login (start → IdP → ACS)

- **id:** `identity.saml-login-flow` · **module:** `identity`
- **Trigger:** GET /api/auth/saml/start (user clicks the SAML login button), then the IdP POSTs the assertion to /api/auth/saml/acs
- **Input:** start: none; acs: multipart form body with a SAMLResponse field (base64-encoded XML)
- **Output:** start: 302 redirect to the IdP's SSO endpoint; acs: 302 redirect to /dashboard with the session cookie set, or to /login?error=... on any failure
- **Rules:**
  - Settings keys that drive SAML: settings.samlEntryPoint (IdP SSO URL) and settings.samlCert (IdP X.509 cert) must both be present (isSamlConfigured) for /start to proceed; samlIssuer/samlAttributeEmail/samlAttributeName are optional overrides
  - @node-saml/node-saml is configured with wantAssertionsSigned: true, so an unsigned or tampered assertion fails validatePostResponseAsync's signature check against the configured idpCert regardless of any other check
  - Login attempts are rate-limited per source IP via the same checkLock/recordFail/recordSuccess mechanism as password login (loginLimiter), applied before the SAMLResponse is even parsed
  - The returned identity maps to a session the same way as OIDC: setDashboardAuthCookie is called with { saml: true, samlEmail, samlName } as extra JWT claims on the one shared auth_token cookie
  - Attribute extraction (pickSamlEmail/pickSamlDisplayName) tries a configured custom attribute name first, then a fixed list of common SAML/WS-Fed claim URIs, then falls back nameID → email → a hardcoded 'SAML user' string — an IdP that puts identity under an attribute not in that list needs the custom samlAttributeEmail/samlAttributeName setting
- **Errors:** `RATE_LIMIT` (source IP has exceeded the login-attempt lockout threshold), `AUTH_ERROR` (SAMLResponse missing, SAML not configured, or validatePostResponseAsync rejects the assertion (bad signature, expired, wrong audience/recipient))

### GET /api/auth/saml/metadata — public SP metadata document

- **id:** `identity.saml-metadata-public` · **module:** `identity`
- **Trigger:** An administrator (or the IdP's own configuration tooling) fetches the SP's metadata XML to configure the IdP side of the trust
- **Input:** none
- **Output:** 200 application/xml — SAML SP metadata (entity ID/issuer, ACS endpoint URL, NameID format) generated from current settings
- **Rules:**
  - The route is deliberately unauthenticated (dashboardGuard's PUBLIC_API_PATHS matches the '/api/auth/saml' prefix) — SP metadata is not secret; it only describes where the IdP should send assertions, not any credential
  - generateSamlMetadata builds the document from the same createSamlInstance config used at login/ACS time, so the ACS URL and issuer it advertises always match what /acs and /start actually enforce, with no separate hand-maintained metadata file
  - If settings.samlCert is unset, the metadata is generated against the DUMMY_FALLBACK_CERT rather than failing — an operator who fetches metadata before configuring the IdP cert gets a syntactically valid but non-functional document instead of an error
- **Errors:** `INTERNAL_ERROR` (generateSamlMetadata throws (returns a 500 with an XML error body, not JSON))

### SAML assertion replay protection is skippable whenever no saml_state cookie is presented

- **id:** `identity.saml-replay-inresponseto-gap` · **module:** `identity`
- **Trigger:** POST /api/auth/saml/acs with a SAMLResponse but no (or an already-expired/already-consumed) saml_state cookie
- **Input:** A previously-valid, correctly-signed SAMLResponse, replayed without the original saml_state cookie
- **Output:** The assertion is accepted and a session cookie is issued exactly as if it were a fresh, expected response — the InResponseTo value inside the assertion is never checked in this case
- **Rules:**
  - createSamlInstance configures node-saml with validateInResponseTo: 'never' — the library's own built-in InResponseTo/replay tracking is explicitly disabled for every request, by explicit choice, not omission
  - validateSamlResponse's own manual replay check only runs when expectedRequestId is truthy; expectedRequestId is cookieStore.get('saml_state')?.value || '', so any ACS POST that arrives without a live saml_state cookie (cookie already expired past its 10-minute maxAge, already deleted by an earlier ACS attempt — the route deletes it unconditionally before validation even starts — or simply omitted by a replaying client) skips the InResponseTo comparison entirely
  - With both the library-level and the fallback manual check bypassable, validatePostResponseAsync's signature/expiry checks are the only remaining defense — a correctly-signed assertion remains fully valid to replay for its entire IdP-set validity window (NotOnOrAfter), from any client, with no per-assertion one-time-use enforcement anywhere in this code path
- **AIGate required behavior:** A signed SAML assertion should be usable to establish a session at most once: either node-saml's own validateInResponseTo tracking should be enabled ('always' or 'ifPresent'), or the code's manual InResponseTo/expectedRequestId comparison should be mandatory (reject when expectedRequestId is missing) rather than only applied when a saml_state cookie happens to still be present.

### POST /api/auth/saml/test — validate a SAML configuration's shape before saving it

- **id:** `identity.saml-test-probe` · **module:** `identity`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard admin clicks "Test connection" on the SAML settings form
- **Input:** { samlEntryPoint?, samlIssuer?, samlCert? } — any field omitted falls back to the currently-saved setting
- **Output:** 200 { ok: true, samlEntryPoint, samlIssuer, certValid: true, acsUrl, metadataUrl } or 400 on a shape-validation failure
- **Rules:**
  - Access requires the same local canAccessTestRoute gate as the OIDC test route (requireLogin===false OR a valid auth_token), duplicated here rather than shared, since '/api/auth/saml' is otherwise fully public
  - Unlike the OIDC test route, this is a pure local validation: it checks that samlEntryPoint parses as a URL and that samlCert reformats successfully via formatX509Certificate — it never makes an outbound network call to the IdP, so a syntactically valid but wrong/unreachable entry point or an expired cert both report ok: true
- **Errors:** `AUTH_ERROR` (requireLogin is true and the caller has no valid auth_token), `INVALID_REQUEST` (samlEntryPoint missing/not a URL, samlIssuer missing, samlCert missing, or samlCert fails to reformat as a certificate)

### Dashboard session cookie issuance, verification, and destruction (login/dashboardGuard/logout)

- **id:** `identity.session-cookie-lifecycle` · **module:** `identity`
- **Trigger:** POST /api/auth/login with a valid password issues the cookie; every subsequent /api/* request through middleware verifies it; POST /api/auth/logout destroys it
- **Input:** login: { password }; logout: none (relies on the existing auth_token cookie)
- **Output:** login: httpOnly auth_token JWT cookie (24h expiry) set on success; logout: auth_token and any pending oidc_state/oidc_nonce/oidc_code_verifier cookies deleted
- **Rules:**
  - auth_token is a jose-signed HS256 JWT (createDashboardAuthToken) with a 24h expiration; its secret is loaded once from the JWT_SECRET env var or a persisted DATA_DIR/jwt-secret file (generated on first run, mode 0o600) — the same pattern as identity.machine-id-derivation's persisted secret
  - The cookie is httpOnly and sameSite=lax always, but secure only when AUTH_COOKIE_SECURE=true or the request carries x-forwarded-proto: https (shouldUseSecureCookie) — a plain HTTP request behind a non-TLS-terminating proxy gets a non-secure cookie
  - dashboardGuard.js's isAuthenticated() treats the caller as authenticated if EITHER the auth_token cookie verifies (hasValidToken → verifyDashboardAuthToken) OR settings.requireLogin === false — the JWT check and the requireLogin bypass are two independent ways to pass the same gate
  - logout is unconditional and itself unauthenticated (no session check gates calling it) — it always clears auth_token plus the three OIDC PKCE/state cookies regardless of whether an OIDC flow was ever started, but does not clear saml_state

### Combo rotation state invalidated when combo strategy settings change

- **id:** `settings.combo-rotation-reset` · **module:** `settings`
- **Trigger:** PATCH /api/settings whose body includes comboStrategy, comboStickyRoundRobinLimit, or comboStrategies
- **Input:** Updated settings object (post-persist)
- **Output:** In-memory combo rotation state cleared; next combo request re-derives its starting point under the new strategy
- **Rules:**
  - resetComboRotation() with no argument clears the entire in-memory Map, not just the affected combo — any change to any of the three keys invalidates rotation state for every combo, not only the ones using the changed strategy

### GET/POST /api/settings/database — full database backup export and restore

- **id:** `settings.database-export-import` · **module:** `settings`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard admin uses the "Export database" / "Import database" action
- **Input:** GET: x-9r-password header (or x-9r-cli-token) for re-auth; POST: { password, ...fullDbPayload } body
- **Output:** GET: 200 with the full exported DB as JSON; POST: 200 { success: true } after wiping and replacing every table's contents
- **Rules:**
  - Both GET and POST require a fresh password re-verification (verifyDashboardPassword — bcrypt.compare against the live settings.password, or INITIAL_PASSWORD/'123456' if unset) UNLESS the caller presents a valid x-9r-cli-token header, on top of dashboardGuard's own middleware gate: '/api/settings/database' is in ALWAYS_PROTECTED, so a valid dashboard JWT or CLI token is already required just to reach the route body
  - exportDb() returns the settings table completely unstripped (exportSettings() is a bare readRaw(), unlike GET /api/settings which strips password/oidcClientSecret per settings.get-secret-stripping) plus every apiKeys row with its plaintext key column, plus each providerConnections/providerNodes/proxyPools row's full JSON data blob — which for OAuth-based connections includes access/refresh tokens. This is a deliberate full-fidelity backup (the point is restoring exact state), not an oversight, but the exported file is itself a complete credential bundle for the install
  - importDb wipes settings, providerConnections, providerNodes, proxyPools, apiKeys, combos, and the modelAliases/customModels/mitmAlias/pricing kv scopes inside a single transaction before repopulating them from the payload — a partial payload still fully wipes tables it doesn't repopulate (e.g. omitting proxyPools from the payload empties proxyPools even if the caller never intended to touch it)
  - After a successful import, applyOutboundProxyEnv is re-run against the freshly-imported settings so an imported outbound-proxy configuration takes effect immediately, matching settings.outbound-proxy-live-apply's normal PATCH-time behavior
- **Errors:** `AUTH_ERROR` (GET/POST without a CLI token and with a wrong/missing password), `INVALID_REQUEST` (POST payload is missing, not an object, or an array), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (the export query or import transaction throws)

### DEFAULT_SETTINGS shape and migration-free merge with persisted data

- **id:** `settings.defaults-and-merge` · **module:** `settings`
- **Trigger:** Every getSettings()/updateSettings() call (i.e. every settings read or write anywhere in the app)
- **Input:** Raw JSON blob previously stored in the settings table (may be missing keys added after it was last written)
- **Output:** A settings object with every DEFAULT_SETTINGS key present, persisted values taking precedence
- **Rules:**
  - mergeWithDefaults is a flat `{ ...DEFAULT_SETTINGS, ...raw }` object spread plus one pass filling in any key still `undefined` after that spread — it has no per-key migration/rename table
  - The one hand-written exception: if outboundProxyEnabled is undefined but outboundProxyUrl is a non-empty string, outboundProxyEnabled is inferred true instead of falling back to the DEFAULT_SETTINGS false — a bespoke backward-compat rule for one specific key, not a general mechanism
  - Unknown keys present in raw (e.g. a key that has since been renamed or removed from DEFAULT_SETTINGS) pass through untouched in the merged object — nothing prunes them

### GET /api/settings response shaping — secret stripping and env-only fields

- **id:** `settings.get-secret-stripping` · **module:** `settings`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard settings page load
- **Input:** none
- **Output:** 200 with the full settings object minus password/oidcClientSecret, plus derived oidcConfigured/hasPassword booleans and env-sourced enableRequestLogs/enableTranslator
- **Rules:**
  - password and oidcClientSecret are destructured out of the response object and never sent to the client; hasPassword (boolean) and oidcConfigured (boolean, requires issuer+clientId+secret all present) are sent instead
  - enableRequestLogs and enableTranslator are read directly from process.env on every GET and are not stored in, or ever read from, the settings DB row — they are appended to the response object after the settings spread, so even if a client PATCHed same-named keys into the DB blob, the env-derived values would still win on the next GET
- **Errors:** `INTERNAL_ERROR` (getSettings() throws (e.g. malformed stored JSON))

### Settings read on the request hot path

- **id:** `settings.hot-path-read-no-cache` · **module:** `settings`
- **Trigger:** Every /v1 chat request (via handleChat's requireApiKey check) and any other call site that reads settings mid-request
- **Input:** none
- **Output:** Full merged settings object
- **Rules:**
  - getSettings() always does a fresh `SELECT data FROM settings WHERE id = 1` — there is no in-process cache, TTL, or invalidation-on-write layer; every caller re-reads and re-parses the JSON blob
  - Of the full settings object, handleChat's enforcement gate only actually reads the single boolean requireApiKey

### Outbound proxy env vars applied immediately on PATCH, without restart

- **id:** `settings.outbound-proxy-live-apply` · **module:** `settings`
- **Trigger:** PATCH /api/settings whose body includes outboundProxyEnabled, outboundProxyUrl, or outboundNoProxy
- **Input:** Updated settings object (post-persist) containing the three outbound-proxy fields
- **Output:** process.env.HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/ALL_PROXY/NO_PROXY mutated in the current process
- **Rules:**
  - applyOutboundProxyEnv only runs when the PATCH body itself contained one of the three keys (checked via hasOwnProperty on the request body, not on whether the merged value differs from before)
  - It only ever writes env vars it validated (scheme allow-list http/https/socks4/socks4a/socks5/socks5h, rejects control chars/backticks/$ in the URL) and tracks a NINE_ROUTER_PROXY_MANAGED marker so it only clears vars it previously set, never externally-provided proxy env vars it didn't write
  - Disabling the proxy (outboundProxyEnabled: false) only clears the env vars if they were previously marked as managed by this code — an externally-set HTTP_PROXY survives untouched

### Password change flow inside PATCH /api/settings

- **id:** `settings.patch-password-change` · **module:** `settings`
- **Trigger:** PATCH /api/settings with a newPassword field
- **Input:** { newPassword, currentPassword? }
- **Output:** password field replaced with a fresh bcrypt hash; 400/401 on validation failure
- **Rules:**
  - If a password hash already exists (settings.password is set), currentPassword is required and must bcrypt.compare true against it, else 401 'Invalid current password'
  - If no password hash exists yet (first-time setup), currentPassword is optional; but if supplied, it must equal the literal string '123456' or the request is rejected with 401
  - On success, newPassword is bcrypt-hashed (genSalt(10)) into body.password, and both newPassword and currentPassword are deleted from body before it reaches updateSettings
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (a password hash already exists but currentPassword was not supplied), `AUTH_ERROR` (currentPassword does not match the stored hash (or, first-time, does not equal '123456'))
- **AIGate required behavior:** The first-time password-change gate in PATCH /api/settings checks currentPassword against the operator's actual configured initial password, i.e. `process.env.INITIAL_PASSWORD || "123456"`, mirroring the check already implemented in src/app/api/auth/login/route.js line 58 for the same purpose

### PATCH /api/settings mass-assignment protection

- **id:** `settings.patch-protected-keys` · **module:** `settings`
- **Trigger:** Any PATCH /api/settings request
- **Input:** Arbitrary JSON body of settings keys to update
- **Output:** Body is mutated in place to delete PROTECTED_SETTING_KEYS before any other handling runs
- **Rules:**
  - PROTECTED_SETTING_KEYS = ['password', 'mitmSudoEncrypted'] — both are deleted from the incoming body before the password-change block, oidcClientSecret handling, or updateSettings(body) ever see them
  - This is a mass-assignment guard (the code comment cites CWE-915): without it, a client could set body.password directly to an attacker-chosen bcrypt hash (or arbitrary string) and bypass the bcrypt.compare(currentPassword) check entirely, since that check only runs inside the body.newPassword branch — a raw password field would flow straight into updateSettings unauthenticated by any current-password check
  - mitmSudoEncrypted (the encrypted sudo password used for MITM proxy host-file elevation) is protected the same way — direct overwrite would let a client plant attacker-controlled ciphertext that the MITM subsystem later decrypts and uses for privileged local operations

### POST /api/settings/proxy-test — verify an outbound proxy URL works before saving it

- **id:** `settings.proxy-test-outbound-probe` · **module:** `settings`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard admin clicks "Test" next to the outbound proxy URL field
- **Input:** { proxyUrl, testUrl?, timeoutMs? } — testUrl defaults to https://google.com/ if omitted
- **Output:** 200 { ok, status, statusText, url, elapsedMs } on success, or { ok: false, error } with a 400/500/timeout status on failure
- **Rules:**
  - The route has no auth check of its own — it relies entirely on dashboardGuard's generic /api/* fallback, where '/api/settings/proxy-test' matches PROTECTED_API_PATHS's '/api/settings' prefix: a valid dashboard session/CLI token is required unless settings.requireLogin is false
  - The server issues a real outbound HEAD request to testUrl through a client-supplied proxyUrl (undici ProxyAgent) — both fields are attacker/client-controlled within the caller's existing trust level, so an authenticated caller can direct the server to probe arbitrary hosts (including internal network addresses) through an arbitrary proxy
  - timeoutMs is clamped to a maximum of 30000ms regardless of what the caller requests, with an 8000ms default when omitted or invalid
  - The setting itself is never persisted by this route — it is a stateless connectivity probe; saving the tested value into settings.outboundProxyUrl happens via the normal PATCH /api/settings path (settings.outbound-proxy-live-apply)
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (proxyUrl missing or fails ProxyAgent's own URL parsing), `TIMEOUT` (the HEAD request does not complete within timeoutMs)

### GET /api/settings/require-login — public pre-auth login-page context

- **id:** `settings.require-login-public-status` · **module:** `settings`
- **Trigger:** Login page loads, before any credential is available, to decide whether to show a login form at all and whether tunnel-based dashboard access is restricted
- **Input:** none
- **Output:** 200 { requireLogin, tunnelDashboardAccess, tunnelUrl, tailscaleUrl } — always 200, even on internal error (falls back to { requireLogin: true })
- **Rules:**
  - The route is deliberately unauthenticated: dashboardGuard's PUBLIC_API_PATHS lists '/api/settings/require-login' explicitly (a carve-out from the otherwise-protected '/api/settings' prefix) specifically so the login page can read it before any session exists
  - requireLogin is the exact toggle read by dashboardGuard.js's isAuthenticated() to decide whether ANY caller (not just this route) is treated as pre-authenticated across every PROTECTED_API_PATHS route — this GET only reports the current value; it cannot change it
  - Turning requireLogin OFF is not reachable from this route (GET-only): it happens through the generic PATCH /api/settings, which is itself in PROTECTED_API_PATHS — so, unlike the tunnel-enable gap recorded in tunnel.enable-lacks-server-side-security-gate (13-console-remote.yaml), disabling requireLogin requires the caller to already hold a valid session or CLI token (or requireLogin to already be false); an unauthenticated remote caller cannot flip it themselves
  - Once requireLogin is false, dashboardGuard.js's isAuthenticated() (the settings.requireLogin===false branch) is consulted by the generic /api/* fallback with no additional locality check — the bypass is not scoped to loopback callers the way LOCAL_ONLY_PATHS's equivalent bypass is, so a deliberately-disabled requireLogin removes the login requirement for every PROTECTED_API_PATHS route (settings, keys, providers, combos, models, usage, oauth, media-providers, pricing, tags, cli-tools, mcp, translator, tunnel) from any network location that can reach the server, not just the local machine — this matches the setting's literal name/intent but is a materially broader blast radius than a 'local-only testing convenience' if the server is ever reachable remotely while it is set

### GET /api/health and GET /api/init — liveness/init-ping endpoints

- **id:** `tooling.health-init-probes` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** An external process manager or the CLI launcher polls /api/health to confirm the server is up; something outside this file calls /api/init once at startup
- **Input:** none
- **Output:** /api/health: 200 { ok: true } with wildcard CORS headers; /api/init: 200 plain-text 'Initialized'
- **Rules:**
  - Both routes are unauthenticated (dashboardGuard's PUBLIC_API_PATHS lists both '/api/health' and '/api/init' explicitly) so a health-checker or launcher never needs credentials to confirm the server responds
  - /api/health also answers CORS preflight (OPTIONS → 204 with the same wildcard headers), the only route in this task's scope that sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin: '*' — deliberate, since a liveness check may come from a browser on a different origin (e.g. a tunnel URL) or a monitoring tool
  - /api/init performs no actual initialization logic in its own handler body — the file's comment ('called automatically to initialize app') describes why something calls it, not what it does; any real 'initialization' side effect is whatever module-level code already ran as a side effect of Next.js loading this route's module tree for the first request, not code inside this GET handler

### POST /api/shutdown — development-only remote process termination

- **id:** `tooling.shutdown-dev-secret-gate` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** A caller with a valid dashboard session/CLI token (dashboardGuard) additionally presenting the correct SHUTDOWN_SECRET bearer token, on a non-production server
- **Input:** Authorization: Bearer <SHUTDOWN_SECRET> header
- **Output:** 403 in production regardless of any credential; 401 if SHUTDOWN_SECRET is unset or the header doesn't match; 200 { success: true } then process.exit(0) after a 500ms delay
- **Rules:**
  - Three independent gates stack: (1) dashboardGuard.js's ALWAYS_PROTECTED lists '/api/shutdown', so the request never reaches the route handler at all without a valid dashboard JWT or CLI token; (2) inside the handler, NODE_ENV === 'production' short-circuits to 403 before the secret is even checked; (3) only in non-production does it compare Authorization against Bearer + SHUTDOWN_SECRET, and SHUTDOWN_SECRET is not set in .env.example — if the operator never sets it, every request 401s unconditionally
  - process.exit(0) is scheduled 500ms after the response is built (not awaited before responding), so the caller reliably receives the 200 body before the process actually terminates
- **Errors:** `AUTH_ERROR` (NODE_ENV is production (always 403), or SHUTDOWN_SECRET is unset/doesn't match the bearer token)

### GET /api/version — current vs. latest npm version check

- **id:** `tooling.version-check-public` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard loads the version/update-check widget, or any caller of GET /api/version
- **Input:** none
- **Output:** 200 { currentVersion, latestVersion, hasUpdate } — currentVersion from the bundled package.json, latestVersion from the npm registry (or null if unreachable)
- **Rules:**
  - The route is unauthenticated (dashboardGuard's PUBLIC_API_PATHS lists '/api/version') — knowing the running version and whether an update exists is not treated as sensitive
  - The npm registry lookup (GET https://registry.npmjs.org/9router/latest) is cached process-wide for 1 hour in a global (global.__npmVersionCache), surviving Next.js hot-reload/module re-evaluation the same way other global._* caches in this codebase do (per usage.global-state-next-reeval's pattern)
  - A failed or timed-out (4s) registry fetch resolves to null rather than throwing, so hasUpdate is reported false and latestVersion null — the route never 500s due to registry unavailability
  - compareVersions only compares the first three numeric dot-separated components — a pre-release/build-metadata suffix is not distinguished from the bare version by this comparison

### POST /api/version/shutdown — authenticated restart to release file locks before a manual update

- **id:** `tooling.version-shutdown-for-update` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard admin (or CLI) triggers a controlled restart, e.g. before manually replacing the install
- **Input:** none
- **Output:** 200 { success: true, message: 'Shutting down for manual update...' } then process.exit(0) after 500ms
- **Rules:**
  - Gated purely by dashboardGuard.js's ALWAYS_PROTECTED ('/api/version/shutdown' is listed explicitly) — a valid dashboard JWT or CLI token is required, with no additional in-route secret unlike /api/shutdown, and no NODE_ENV restriction: this is the production-facing equivalent of the dev-only /api/shutdown route
  - killAppProcesses() best-effort kills sibling processes that could hold file locks: the MITM proxy (via its PID file, escalating to sudo/PowerShell Stop-Process if needed), any other node.exe/next-server processes matching this install's path or cli.js, and cloudflared/tray binaries — via platform-specific shell commands (taskkill/PowerShell on Windows, kill/ps on POSIX)
  - All kill attempts are wrapped in try/catch and proceed regardless of individual failures ('best effort') — the route always returns success and always schedules process.exit(0), even if killAppProcesses killed nothing or partially failed

### POST /api/version/update — production-only self-update via a detached npm install

- **id:** `tooling.version-update-npm-relaunch` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard admin (or CLI) triggers "Update now" from the version-check widget
- **Input:** none
- **Output:** 200 { success: true, message: 'Updater started. This app will exit shortly.' } (production only); 403 outside production
- **Rules:**
  - Gated by dashboardGuard.js's ALWAYS_PROTECTED ('/api/version/update') plus an in-route NODE_ENV !== 'production' → 403 check — the inverse restriction of /api/shutdown (dev-only): this route only runs in production builds (the shipped CLI)
  - killAppProcesses() runs first (same best-effort sibling-process kill as /api/version/shutdown) to release file locks Windows would otherwise hold during an npm overwrite
  - spawnUpdaterAndExit() copies the bundled src/lib/updater/updater.js into DATA_DIR/runtime/updater (so a subsequent `npm install -g` overwriting the app's own installed files can't delete the script out from under the process running it), then spawns it as a fully detached (unref'd) Node child process before the parent exits
  - The detached updater.js runs `npm i -g <packageName>@latest` (packageName defaults to '9router') via child_process.spawn, with retry logic (UPDATER_RETRIES, default 3) and a status file/log written to DATA_DIR/update — this IS the actual download-and-install step, performed entirely by npm's own registry client, not by any custom download code in this route
  - After the npm install completes, the updater relaunches the app via `npx 9router` (npx.cmd on Windows) with --skip-update, preserving --tray mode if TRAY_MODE=1 was set — then the current server process exits via process.exit(0)
- **Errors:** `AUTH_ERROR` (NODE_ENV is not 'production')

## Skills

### Single source-of-truth array mapping each capability to a raw GitHub SKILL.md URL third parties fetch directly

- **id:** `skills.catalogue-raw-github-contract` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** /dashboard/skills page render (reads SKILLS to list cards); any third-party AI agent fetching a copied raw URL at its own setup/tool-load time
- **Input:** a skill id
- **Output:** a raw.githubusercontent.com URL: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/decolua/9router/refs/heads/master/skills/<id>/SKILL.md
- **Rules:**
  - SKILLS is a flat array of 8 entries: one 'entry' hub skill (isEntry:true, endpoint:null, meant to be pasted first) plus 7 capability skills, each carrying the exact /v1/* endpoint path it documents (chat, images/generations, audio/speech, audio/transcriptions, embeddings, search, web/fetch) — this array is the only place these ids/endpoints are declared for the dashboard
  - getSkillRawUrl/getSkillBlobUrl build their URLs purely from three module-level constants (REPO='decolua/9router', BRANCH='master', SKILL_PATH='skills') and the skill's id — there is no indirection, redirect, or version pin beyond the hardcoded branch name
  - Q5 answer — who fetches it: the user copies the raw URL from the dashboard and pastes it into an arbitrary third-party AI agent/tool framework, which fetches SKILL.md over plain HTTP at ITS OWN request/setup time; 9router's own server has no further role once the URL is handed out
  - Q5 answer — what breaks if a SKILL.md moves: because the URL is built from fixed constants with no fallback, a rename/move/deletion of skills/<id>/SKILL.md in the decolua/9router repo (or a branch rename away from 'master') makes every previously-copied raw URL 404 on its next fetch by any third party, silently and with no way for 9router's own runtime to detect or warn about it — the fetch happens entirely outside this codebase
  - Per CLAUDE.md's own note, skills.js (this catalogue) and the actual files under skills/ (tracked separately in skills/README.md's table) are two independently-maintained sources kept in sync only by convention/process, not by any code in this repository

## Token Saver

### Headroom stage: send messages to an external compression proxy, fail open on any failure

- **id:** `tokensaver.headroom-compress` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** Stage 2, only when tokenSaverEnabled && headroomEnabled
- **Input:** translatedBody plus finalFormat/upstreamModel/headroomUrl/headroomCompressUserMessages/headroomTimeoutMs
- **Output:** translatedBody.messages (or .input, or Kiro's projected fields) replaced with the proxy's compressed messages; null on any failure, body left untouched
- **Rules:**
  - The proxy's /v1/compress endpoint only understands OpenAI message shape, so Claude, OpenAI-Responses and Kiro bodies are translated to OpenAI messages first, compressed, then translated back into the original wire shape using 9Router's own translators
  - openai-responses bodies carrying tool/reasoning input items are refused up front (hasUnsafeResponsesInputForCompression) rather than risking a lossy round-trip
  - A hard timeoutMs (default 3000ms) is enforced via AbortSignal.timeout on the fetch to the proxy
  - compressUserMessages is an opt-in flag forwarded as config.compress_user_messages; by default only tool/assistant history is compressed, not the user's own messages

### 6 api/headroom/* routes: process lifecycle for headroom, an external (not library-mode) proxy

- **id:** `tokensaver.headroom-management-routes` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard Token Saver card actions for the Headroom stage
- **Input:** None (GET/POST), except extras which takes {extras: string[]}
- **Output:** JSON status/result payloads; a nested proxy/[...path] route forwards arbitrary requests to the live headroom process
- **Rules:**
  - Unlike PXPIPE, headroom is a real child process 9Router spawns/manages (start/restart/stop against a port derived from settings.headroomUrl, default 8787) — not an in-process module
  - start/restart both refuse (400 EXTERNAL_PROXY) unless the configured headroomUrl is a loopback address — 9Router will not try to manage a proxy it doesn't own
  - extras manages optional Python-based compression extras (findPython310 discovery) independent of the main proxy process
  - proxy/[...path] reverse-proxies to the configured headroomUrl, stripping hop-by-hop headers and additionally stripping cookie/authorization when the target host is not loopback (credential leak guard), and rewrites the vendored dashboard HTML's relative fetch() calls to stay under the /api/headroom/proxy prefix
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (start/restart called with a non-loopback headroomUrl), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (headroom package not installed when start/restart is called)

### Five-stage pipeline run once per chat request, just before dispatch

- **id:** `tokensaver.pipeline-execution-order` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** Every chat request, after translation/passthrough and before getExecutor(provider) is resolved
- **Input:** translatedBody (already translated/passthrough), finalFormat, upstreamModel, the settings token-saver flags, and the x-9router-token-saver request header
- **Output:** translatedBody mutated in place by RTK/headroom/caveman/ponytail; replaced wholesale by pxpipe when it applies
- **Rules:**
  - Fixed order, not configurable: RTK -> Headroom -> Caveman -> Ponytail -> PXPIPE (matches the UI pipeline diagram in the spec, §5#15)
  - Per-request opt-out header x-9router-token-saver: off computes tokenSaverEnabled=false, which gates RTK/headroom/caveman/ponytail — but NOT pxpipe (see tokensaver.pxpipe-master-optout-bug)
  - Each of the four gated stages is additionally gated by its own settings.*Enabled flag: rtkEnabled, headroomEnabled, cavemanEnabled (+ cavemanLevel truthy), ponytailEnabled (+ ponytailLevel truthy)
  - PXPIPE is last so it sees the final body after every other saver has already run

### PXPIPE stage: render bulky Claude-format tool context as dense PNGs via an in-process transform

- **id:** `tokensaver.pxpipe-compress` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** Stage 5, gated only by pxpipeEnabled (see tokensaver.pxpipe-master-optout-bug for why that's a finding)
- **Input:** translatedBody (Claude format only), model, minChars threshold, timeoutMs, and the transform function (pxpipeTransform, looked up once per request in chat.js)
- **Output:** { body: <new body with text replaced by image blocks> | null, summary }. body is null (original untouched) whenever pxpipe skips or fails
- **Rules:**
  - Only Claude-format bodies are eligible (format !== FORMATS.CLAUDE -> skipped('unsupported_format'))
  - A minChars threshold (settings.pxpipeMinChars, default 25000) gates the whole call — bodies smaller than the threshold are skipped before the transform even runs
  - The CPU-bound transform can't be aborted mid-flight, so it's raced against a timer (Promise.race) with a default 15000ms budget; losing the race discards the (still-running) result and leaves the original body untouched
  - The transformed body trades bytes for tokens: base64 PNGs make it bigger in bytes, but Anthropic bills images by pixels/750 rather than encoded length, so the after-estimate uses image-token math, not chars/4 of the new body

### 'PXPIPE is running' means the transform module is loaded in-process, not that a port is listening

- **id:** `tokensaver.pxpipe-library-mode-status` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** GET /api/pxpipe/status, or any internal caller of getPxpipeStatus()
- **Input:** none
- **Output:** { installed, installing, version, path, running, loadedAt, uptimeMs, npmAvailable, mode: 'library' }
- **Rules:**
  - PXPIPE has no server process and no port: 'install' is an npm install into DATA_DIR/pxpipe, 'start'/'restart' load the package's dist/core/library.js via a versioned dynamic import(), and 'stop' just drops the cached module reference
  - running is literally `loaded.loaded`, i.e. whether the in-process module cache (`cached` in loader.js) is populated — there is no health probe of a network socket anywhere in this path
  - The module is cache-busted by package version on every load (?v=<version> query on the file:// import URL) so a repair/upgrade takes effect without a full server restart

### 8 api/pxpipe/* routes: install, lifecycle, and observability for the in-process PXPIPE module

- **id:** `tokensaver.pxpipe-management-routes` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard Token Saver card actions and status polling
- **Input:** None (GET) or {extras} style bodies where noted; all are simple POST/GET, no auth beyond the dashboard session
- **Output:** JSON status/result payloads; errors returned as {error, code} with 500 (or 400/409 for expected preconditions), never thrown to the Next.js error boundary
- **Rules:**
  - install: npm-installs pxpipe-proxy@latest into DATA_DIR/pxpipe (serialized — concurrent calls await the same in-flight promise), unloads any cached module, then re-runs the health check
  - start: auto-installs first only if settings.pxpipeAutoInstall is true and the package is missing, otherwise 409 NOT_INSTALLED; then loads the module
  - stop: drops the cached module reference only — requests fail open to uncompressed passthrough (compressWithPxpipe sees transform is not a function) until started again
  - restart: unload then load, for picking up an upgraded install without a full server restart
  - health: installed? -> module loads? -> a synthetic ping request transforms? three-step checklist, each step short-circuiting the next on failure
  - logs / stats: read-only; logs tails install.log plus the events.jsonl audit trail, stats aggregates it into all-time/today/7d/30d windows and a daily timeline
- **Errors:** `INTERNAL_ERROR` (npm not found on PATH during install), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (npm install exits non-zero or times out after 5 minutes), `INVALID_REQUEST` (start called while not installed and pxpipeAutoInstall is off)

### SB-1: the token-saver master opt-out header does not reach the PXPIPE gate

- **id:** `tokensaver.pxpipe-master-optout-bug` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** A client sends x-9router-token-saver: off intending to disable the whole token-saver pipeline, while settings.pxpipeEnabled is true
- **Input:** x-9router-token-saver: off header + a Claude-format body large enough to clear pxpipeMinChars
- **Output:** RTK/headroom/caveman/ponytail are all skipped (tokenSaverEnabled is false), but PXPIPE still runs and can replace the body with image-block content
- **Rules:**
  - Every other stage's enable check is `tokenSaverEnabled && <stage>Enabled` (chatCore.js:254,260,274,280); PXPIPE's check at line 287 is `if (pxpipeEnabled)` alone — tokenSaverEnabled is computed at line 251 but never referenced again after line 280
  - This is confirmed directly from source (not inferred): grepping the whole file for tokenSaverEnabled shows exactly 5 uses — the definition plus 4 gate checks (RTK, headroom, caveman, ponytail) — and none at the PXPIPE gate
- **AIGate required behavior:** x-9router-token-saver: off disables every token-saver stage, including PXPIPE, for that request

### RTK filter selection: autoDetectFilter dispatch order and the caps that bound it

- **id:** `tokensaver.rtk-autodetect-order` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** compressText() calls autoDetectFilter(text) for any candidate string within [MIN_COMPRESS_SIZE, RAW_CAP]
- **Input:** The candidate text (a tool_result / tool-message string)
- **Output:** A filter function to apply, or null (no filter matched -> text passes through unchanged)
- **Rules:**
  - Detection only inspects the first DETECT_WINDOW (1024) chars of the text, not the whole string
  - Fixed priority order: git-log -> git-diff -> git-status -> build-output -> (porcelain heuristic re-checked as git-status) -> grep -> find -> tree -> ls -> search-list -> read-numbered -> dedup-log -> smart-truncate -> null
  - build-output is checked before the porcelain/git-status heuristic specifically to stop cargo's 'Compiling' lines from being misdetected as git status output
  - find requires ALL non-empty lines to be path-like and >=3 lines; grep requires ANY of the first 5 non-empty lines to look like 'file:number:content'

### RTK stage: compress tool_result / tool-message content across four wire shapes plus Kiro

- **id:** `tokensaver.rtk-compress-shapes` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** Stage 1 of the pipeline, only when tokenSaverEnabled && rtkEnabled
- **Input:** translatedBody.messages[] or .input[] (or body.conversationState for Kiro)
- **Output:** Matched text fields rewritten in place with a compressed version; stats object {bytesBefore, bytesAfter, hits[]} or null
- **Rules:**
  - Four non-Kiro shapes handled: (1) OpenAI tool message string content, (1b) OpenAI tool message array content, (2) Claude tool_result string content, (3) Claude tool_result array content; plus a fifth top-level Responses shape (function_call_output, string or array output)
  - Kiro is a fully separate code path (compressKiroFormat) walking conversationState.history[]/currentMessage instead of messages[]/input[]
  - A candidate string is only compressed when MIN_COMPRESS_SIZE <= length <= RAW_CAP; otherwise it passes through unchanged and still counts toward bytesBefore/bytesAfter
  - The chosen filter's output is discarded (original kept) if it is empty or not smaller than the input — RTK never grows or blanks a tool result

### Why RTK refuses to compress an error tool_result

- **id:** `tokensaver.rtk-error-preservation` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** A tool_result block has is_error: true (Claude) or a Kiro toolResult has status: 'error'
- **Input:** The same block that would otherwise be compressed
- **Output:** Block is left byte-for-byte unmodified and does not contribute to stats.bytesBefore/bytesAfter
- **Rules:**
  - RTK's compression filters are heuristic (git-log/diff/status, grep, find, ls, tree, dedup, smart-truncate — see tokensaver.rtk-autodetect-order) and are lossy by design: they drop lines, dedupe, or truncate
  - An error result is the one place the exact original text matters — the model needs to see precisely what failed and why to recover, and a downstream reviewer/trace needs the untouched error for debugging; lossy truncation could hide the failing line or the error message itself
  - Skipping is a full bypass, not a lighter compression: no filter is even selected for these blocks

### RTK's two-layer fail-open: a bad filter panics safely, a bad body returns null

- **id:** `tokensaver.rtk-fail-open` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** Any exception while compressing a message body, or a single filter throwing on its input
- **Input:** The in-flight body / candidate text at the point of failure
- **Output:** compressMessages/compressKiroFormat return null (request continues with the body untouched by RTK); safeApply returns the original text unmodified if the chosen filter itself throws
- **Rules:**
  - Two independent catch layers: the per-filter layer (safeApply) prevents one bad filter from aborting the whole compression pass; the outer layer (compressMessages/compressKiroFormat) prevents any other bug in the loop from throwing out of the token-saver stage
  - Both layers only log (console.warn) — neither raises, retries, nor surfaces an error to the client

### Only PXPIPE's savings are persisted; RTK and headroom stats are console-log only and discarded

- **id:** `tokensaver.savings-recording` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** End of each stage's run, per request
- **Input:** Each stage's own stats object (rtkStats, headroomStats/headroomDiagnostics, pxpipeSummary)
- **Output:** PXPIPE: one JSON line appended to DATA_DIR/pxpipe/events.jsonl (rotated at 5MB) via onPxpipeEvent -> appendPxpipeEvent, later aggregated by getPxpipeStats() for the dashboard. RTK/headroom/caveman/ponytail: formatted into a console.log/log.line string and never written anywhere else
- **Rules:**
