  - chatCore.js never returns rtkStats/headroomStats to its caller (chat.js) and chat.js does not persist them either — grepping the whole tree for rtkStats/headroomStats/rtkLine/headroomLine shows no reference outside chatCore.js's own log lines
  - pxpipeSummary is the one exception: chat.js wires onPxpipeEvent: appendPxpipeEvent, and chatCore.js calls onPxpipeEvent?.({provider, model, ...pxpipeSummary}) after every pxpipe attempt (applied or not), inside its own try/catch so a broken stats write can't fail the request
  - getPxpipeStats() buckets events into all/today/yesterday/last7d/last30d totals plus a daily timeline, classifying non-applied events as either 'errors' (transform_error/timeout) or 'bypassed' (everything else, e.g. below_threshold/unsupported_format)

### Caveman + Ponytail stages: inject a terse-style system prompt via a shared, format-dispatching injector

- **id:** `tokensaver.system-prompt-injection` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** Stage 3 (caveman) when tokenSaverEnabled && cavemanEnabled && cavemanLevel; stage 4 (ponytail) when tokenSaverEnabled && ponytailEnabled && ponytailLevel
- **Input:** translatedBody, finalFormat, and the level-selected prompt string (CAVEMAN_PROMPTS[level] / PONYTAIL_PROMPTS[level])
- **Output:** The prompt text appended into the body's system/instructions field for the detected wire shape; no-op if already present (idempotent) or if the shape is unrecognized
- **Rules:**
  - injectCaveman and injectPonytail are thin wrappers over the same injectSystemPrompt(body, format, prompt) — they differ only in which prompt table they pull from
  - Dispatch is by wire shape, checked in order: Kiro (systemPrompt+conversationState) -> Claude (system field) -> Gemini/Gemini-CLI/Vertex/Antigravity (systemInstruction) -> OpenAI instructions string -> OpenAI messages[] -> OpenAI Responses input[]; a plain string body.input is left untouched
  - Idempotency is exact: the prompt must appear as its own SEP-delimited segment (or the whole string), not merely as a substring, before it is considered already-injected
  - Kiro injection additionally mirrors/repairs the prompt into the first user turn's content (not just systemPrompt), with a rollback if the write doesn't converge

## Translation / language functionality

### Supported-locale catalog and the DEFAULT_LOCALE fallback

- **id:** `i18n.locale-normalization-fallback` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** Every read of LOCALES/normalizeLocale/isSupportedLocale — client cookie parsing, /api/locale validation, LanguageSwitcher menu rendering
- **Input:** any locale string (from a cookie, a request body, or an unrecognized value)
- **Output:** one of 34 supported locale codes, or DEFAULT_LOCALE ('en') for anything unrecognized
- **Rules:**
  - LOCALES lists exactly 34 codes (en, vi, zh-CN, zh-TW, ja, pt-BR, pt-PT, ko, es, de, fr, he, ar, ru, pl, cs, nl, tr, uk, tl, id, km, th, hi, bn, ur, ro, sv, it, el, hu, fi, da, no, fa); LOCALE_NAMES supplies a human-readable display name for each
  - normalizeLocale('zh') and normalizeLocale('zh-CN') both resolve to 'zh-CN' — the only alias in the chain; every other supported code maps to itself, and anything not in the chain falls through to DEFAULT_LOCALE
  - A cookie value that is missing, malformed, or for a locale removed from LOCALES silently becomes 'en' everywhere this fallback is used (getLocaleFromCookie in runtime.js, LanguageSwitcher, the profile page) — there is no user-visible error for a corrupted/unsupported cookie value, it just silently reverts to English

### POST /api/locale — validate, normalize, persist the chosen locale as a 1-year cookie

- **id:** `i18n.locale-selection-persistence` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** User picks a language in LanguageSwitcher (dashboard UI)
- **Input:** { locale } JSON body
- **Output:** { success, locale } and a `locale` cookie set; or 400 for an unsupported locale
- **Rules:**
  - isSupportedLocale rejects (400) before any normalization runs — an unrecognized locale string never reaches normalizeLocale or the cookie write
  - normalizeLocale is a 35-if if/else chain (1 zh/zh-CN alias branch + 34 identity branches, one per entry in LOCALES, each returning the exact value it matched) plus a DEFAULT_LOCALE fallback — functionally equivalent to `isSupportedLocale(x) ? x : DEFAULT_LOCALE`, but written as an explicit long-form chain rather than a lookup
  - The cookie (LOCALE_COOKIE = 'locale') is set with path: '/' and maxAge: 60*60*24*365 (1 year) — no httpOnly/secure/sameSite flags are set, so it is readable and writable from client-side JavaScript, which is required by design since runtime.js reads it directly via document.cookie
  - PUBLIC_API_PATHS in dashboardGuard.js includes /api/locale, so this route is reachable without an authenticated dashboard session
  - LanguageSwitcher's handleSetLocale POSTs the cookie, then calls reloadTranslations() to apply the change immediately client-side, without a full page reload; the profile page separately reads the cookie into its own local state on mount via a duplicated getLocaleFromCookie() implementation (not imported from runtime.js)
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (locale missing or not in the LOCALES whitelist (400)), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (cookie write throws (500 Failed to set locale))

### Literal-keyed runtime DOM text substitution (not a conventional key-based i18n library)

- **id:** `i18n.runtime-dom-translation` · **module:** `tooling`
- **Trigger:** initRuntimeI18n on client mount (RuntimeI18nProvider useEffect) and reloadTranslations on every route change / locale switch
- **Input:** public/i18n/literals/{locale}.json — a flat English-source-string -> translated-string dictionary
- **Output:** Matching text nodes in the live DOM have their nodeValue replaced with the translated string
- **Rules:**
  - There is no translation-key system: literal English source strings ARE the dictionary keys (e.g. public/i18n/literals/vi.json has 195 entries like {"Cancel": "Hủy", "Delete": "Xóa"}) — any component text that does not exactly match a stored key (including trailing/leading whitespace, which is handled via .trim(), but not case or punctuation variants) is left untranslated
  - loadTranslations treats locale === 'en' as a no-op (empty translationMap, translate() short-circuits to the original text) rather than loading an en.json — English is the fallback identity, not a translated catalog
  - The mechanism is a DOM TreeWalker (SHOW_TEXT) over document.body plus a MutationObserver watching childList/subtree — every text node gets translate() applied to its ORIGINAL text (cached on node._originalText on first visit) so re-running the walker after a locale switch always re-translates from the untranslated source, never double-translates an already-translated node
  - Nodes are skipped when their parent tag is script/style/code/pre/table-structural/select-related, or when any ancestor carries a data-i18n-skip attribute — an explicit opt-out mechanism for text that must not be swapped
  - Locale detection is entirely client-side: initRuntimeI18n reads the cookie via document.cookie (getLocaleFromCookie) — there is no server-side Accept-Language negotiation, no SSR-rendered translated markup, and no cookie read during Next.js server rendering; the page always first paints in whatever the server rendered (English source text) and then gets DOM-patched client-side after mount
  - reloadTranslations (triggered on every pathname change via RuntimeI18nProvider, with a double requestAnimationFrame to wait for React's DOM commit) re-reads the cookie, re-fetches the locale's JSON, and re-walks the entire document.body — there is no scoping to only the newly-rendered route content
- **Errors:** `INTERNAL_ERROR` (the locale JSON fetch fails or fails to parse — caught, translationMap reset to {} so translate() falls back to returning the original (English) text for every string)

### How Kiro EventStream, Cursor protobuf, and CommandCode NDJSON avoid the translator's pivot dispatch

- **id:** `translator.binary-protocol-bypass` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** A response arrives from kiro, cursor, or commandcode in its native binary/line-delimited wire format
- **Input:** AWS EventStream binary frames (kiro) / ConnectRPC protobuf frames (cursor) / NDJSON lines (commandcode)
- **Output:** An OpenAI-shaped Response object (SSE text or JSON) returned by the executor itself, before chatCore's generic translateResponse dispatch ever runs on the raw upstream bytes
- **Rules:**
  - KiroExecutor.transformEventStreamToSSE parses AWS EventStream framing (CRC32 checksums, header/payload bounds, KIRO_EVENT_TYPES) directly inside the executor and emits OpenAI chat.completion.chunk-shaped SSE text; the registered kiro:openai and kiro:claude response translators both open with an explicit 'already in OpenAI format, return as-is' check, confirming their real job is a passthrough for these executor-built chunks, not EventStream decoding
  - CursorExecutor.transformProtobufToSSE/transformProtobufToJSON parse the ConnectRPC frame + gzip/deflate decompression + protobuf field extraction directly inside the executor (readCursorFrame, extractTextFromResponse) and build the final OpenAI-shaped Response themselves; cursorToOpenAIResponse's docblock states 'CursorExecutor already emits OpenAI format - this is a passthrough'
  - CommandCodeExecutor is the odd one out: inspectAndWrapCommandCodeResponse wraps the raw upstream NDJSON body in a TransformStream (wrapNdjsonAsOpenAISse) that calls commandCodeToOpenAIResponse — the translator FILE's own parsing function — directly and synchronously per line, before the Response object is ever returned from executor.execute(). So the NDJSON-to-OpenAI-chunk mapping logic does live in translator/response/commandcode-to-openai.js, but it is invoked by the executor's own stream pipeline, never through chatCore's translateResponse dispatch or the responseRegistry lookup
  - All three converge on the same effect: by the time chatCore reads `result.response`, the body is already OpenAI-shaped SSE/JSON, so the generic per-chunk translateResponse loop (when it does run, e.g. for a Claude-format client) only needs the trivial X:openai passthrough leg plus the ordinary openai:target leg — the actual protocol decoding never goes through the registry's two-hop pivot machinery
- **Streaming:** yes

### Claude OAuth anti-ban tool cloaking and fingerprint injection

- **id:** `translator.claude-oauth-cloaking` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** translateRequest's final step, only when PROVIDERS[provider].quirks.cloakToolsOnOAuth is set and the credential is a Claude Code OAuth token (apiKey/accessToken contains 'sk-ant-oat')
- **Input:** translated Claude-format body with client tool declarations and tool_use history
- **Output:** body with every client tool/tool_use renamed with a suffix, ~20 decoy Claude-Code-native tool declarations appended, and (via applyCloaking, gated separately) a fabricated billing header + fake user_id metadata
- **Rules:**
  - cloakClaudeTools renames every client-declared tool (and matching tool_use blocks in message history) by appending CLAUDE_TOOL_SUFFIX, skipping only tools that carry their own `type` (Anthropic built-ins like web_search_20250305, which must keep their exact reserved name); it then appends ~20 CC_DECOY_TOOLS (Task, Bash, Glob, Grep, Read, Edit, Write, WebFetch, WebSearch, etc.) each described as 'currently unavailable' — these make the outbound tool list resemble a real Claude Code CLI session
  - A forced tool_choice pointing at a client tool is rewritten to the suffixed name so Claude does not reject it as unknown; decoy/built-in names are never rewritten
  - The toolNameMap produced here is threaded back through translateResponse (decloakStreamChunk) so the client sees its original, unsuffixed tool names in the streamed response — Q1's claude-to-openai loss list does not apply here since this is a same-format (claude->claude) or post-translation cloak, not a pivot step
  - applyCloaking (a separate function, not always called alongside cloakClaudeTools) injects a fabricated x-anthropic-billing-header as system[0] and a fake {device_id, account_uuid, session_id} JSON blob into metadata.user_id, deriving device_id/account_uuid deterministically from the API key (stable per account) so repeated requests from the same account look like the same real device
- **Streaming:** yes

### The one bidirectional direct route — claude:kiro / kiro:claude

- **id:** `translator.direct-route-claude-kiro` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** sourceFormat=claude, targetFormat=kiro (request) or upstream=kiro, client=claude (response)
- **Input:** Claude Messages-API request body / Kiro-executor-emitted OpenAI-shaped chunk
- **Output:** Kiro GenerateAssistantResponse payload / Claude SSE events
- **Rules:**
  - claudeToKiroRequest converts Anthropic Messages requests straight to Kiro/AWS CodeWhisperer payloads instead of claude->openai->kiro, avoiding the double hop that would otherwise silently drop thinking blocks and is_error (openai has no field for either) before Kiro's session-replay canonicalizer ever sees them
  - On the way back, KiroExecutor.transformEventStreamToSSE already decodes the binary AWS EventStream into OpenAI-shaped chat.completion.chunk objects (see translator.binary-protocol-bypass) before any translator runs, so kiroToClaudeResponse's real input is OpenAI chunks, not raw Kiro events
  - kiroToClaudeResponse re-implements the same OpenAI-chunk -> Claude-SSE mapping that openai-to-claude.js (response) performs, duplicated so the direct route is self-contained and does not depend on a second pivot hop for reasoning_content -> thinking blocks, tool_calls -> tool_use blocks, and usage -> message_delta
  - The direct route is reached only when source is exactly claude and target is exactly kiro (or the reverse for response); any other claude<->kiro-adjacent pairing still goes through the openai pivot with the losses in translator.pivot-loss
- **Streaming:** yes

### Base64 data-URI encode/parse shared by every image-capable translator

- **id:** `translator.image-data-uri-concern` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** Any translator converting an image content block between formats
- **Input:** mime type + base64 payload, or a data: URI string
- **Output:** data: URI string, or {mimeType, base64}, or null when the string is not a data URI
- **Rules:**
  - encodeDataUri/parseDataUri are pure string helpers with no validation of the base64 payload itself or the declared mime type — any string matching `^data:([^;]+);base64,([\s\S]+)$` parses successfully regardless of whether the payload actually decodes to that mime
  - This concern only covers already-inline (base64) images; fetching a remote URL into base64 is a separate, security-hardened concern (fetchImageAsBase64 in the same file) used by routing.modality-strip-prefetch's image-prefetch step, not by the per-block translators directly

### What breaks when a translator file is not imported by index.js

- **id:** `translator.missing-import-failure-mode` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** A translator module exists under request/ or response/ but is not among the static imports at the bottom of index.js
- **Input:** None — this is a startup/wiring condition, not a per-request input
- **Output:** No error — the affected leg of the pivot is skipped silently
- **Rules:**
  - register() is only ever invoked as an import side effect (the docblock and lazy var-hoisted requestRegistry/responseRegistry exist specifically to survive circular-import order); a translator file that is never imported never calls register(), so its `${from}:${to}` key is simply absent from the Map — there is no startup check that all expected pairs exist
  - translateRequest's Step 1 (source->openai) and Step 2 (openai->target) each guard with `if (toOpenAI)` / `if (fromOpenAI)` before calling; when the lookup misses, that whole leg is skipped and `result` (the still-untranslated body from the previous step, or the original body if Step 1 missed) is passed straight to the next step or to the upstream provider
  - The failure is invisible to the caller: no exception, no log line, no error code — the request goes out with fields the target provider does not expect (e.g. a Claude tool_result block sent verbatim to an OpenAI-shaped executor), and any resulting 400 from the provider surfaces only as a generic upstream error, not as a translator diagnostic

### What survives a round trip through the OpenAI intermediate format, and what does not

- **id:** `translator.pivot-loss` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** Any request whose source and target format differ and have no direct route registered (the common case — see translator.direct-route-claude-kiro for the one exception)
- **Input:** Source-format request/response, translated through source->openai->target
- **Output:** Target-format body/chunk with the fields below dropped, collapsed, or fabricated
- **Rules:**
  - Thinking/reasoning block CONTENT + signature: claude-to-openai.js's convertClaudeMessage switch handles only text/image/tool_use/tool_result — there is no case for Claude's `thinking` or `redacted_thinking` block type, so a prior-turn thinking block from a Claude-native client is dropped entirely on the claude->openai leg (not even converted to plain text)
  - Even when a thinking block DOES reach the OpenAI-target normalization step, filterToOpenAIFormat strips it explicitly: its own docblock says 'Remove: thinking, redacted_thinking, signature, and other non-OpenAI blocks', and stripBlock unconditionally destructures `signature` out of every content block regardless of source or target provider
  - On the response leg (upstream Claude -> client), reasoning TEXT itself survives: content_block_delta's thinking_delta case calls reasoningDelta(delta.thinking), which builds a separate structured `{ reasoning_content: text }` delta that concerns/chunk.js's buildChunk passes through verbatim as choices[0].delta — the same reasoning_content convention used for GLM/Qwen/DeepSeek/Kimi, not a text merge. What IS lost is the discrete thinking-BLOCK structure: content_block_start/content_block_stop for a THINKING block instead emit bare literal `<think>`/`</think>` boundary markers into the OpenAI `content` field (no text inside them) — so a client sees a `<think>` marker in `content` running in parallel with the actual reasoning text arriving on a separate `reasoning_content` field, an unusual split representation — plus any cryptographic signature on the thinking block, which has no field on either side. redacted_thinking has no case in this response switch at all, so it produces neither markers nor reasoning_content. server_tool_use (built-in web-search) blocks are dropped outright (skip, no representation at all)
  - The reverse direction (a prior turn's reasoning_content -> Claude thinking block) is not reconstructed at all: openai-to-claude.js's getContentBlocksFromMessage only reads msg.content (array or string) and msg.tool_calls for an assistant message — it never reads the sibling msg.reasoning_content field, so that text is silently dropped, not converted into a Claude thinking block, whenever a request is translated toward the claude target format
  - cache_control: Claude content-block cache_control markers are never copied by claude-to-openai.js's block conversion; filterToOpenAIFormat also strips cache_control from every block unless the target provider is flagged quirks.preserveCacheControl, in which case it is kept but only as an opaque pass-through, not reconciled with any OpenAI-side caching concept (OpenAI has none)
  - tool_use id: preserved verbatim when it already matches Anthropic's `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$` pattern; ensureToolCallIds regenerates a brand-new id (from message/tool-call position, not derived from the original string) whenever it does not match, so an original id containing e.g. `:` or `.` never survives the pivot unchanged
  - tool_result is_error: claude-to-openai.js's TOOL_RESULT case builds a plain `{ role: tool, tool_call_id, content }` OpenAI message with no is_error field — OpenAI's tool-message shape has no equivalent, so the flag is lost on the claude->openai leg. It is preserved only in the one place OpenAI-to-Claude conversion re-reads an already-Claude-shaped tool_result block that arrived embedded in an OpenAI-format message (an edge case, not the general claude-native path)
  - Non-base64 (URL-sourced) images: claude-to-openai.js only handles `block.source?.type === 'base64'` — a Claude-native client's `source: {type: 'url', ...}` image block has no matching case and is silently dropped on the claude->openai leg. The reverse leg (openai->claude) DOES preserve an http(s) image_url as `source: {type: 'url', url}`, so the loss is asymmetric
  - System prompt arrays: Claude's `system` is an array of blocks (each with its own optional cache_control); claude-to-openai.js joins them into one newline-separated string on the way into OpenAI, discarding block boundaries and any per-block cache_control
  - Stop reasons: OPENAI_FINISH has 4 values (stop/length/tool_calls/content_filter); CLAUDE_STOP has 4 of its own including stop_sequence. toOpenAIFinish maps end_turn AND stop_sequence to the same generic 'stop' — which sequence string actually matched is not carried into the OpenAI shape at all, since OpenAI's finish_reason has no slot for it
  - Usage: cache_read_input_tokens/cache_creation_input_tokens ARE preserved into OpenAI's non-standard prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens/cache_creation_tokens, and Gemini's thoughtsTokenCount into completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens — these are the one category that mostly survives the pivot, modulo the per-provider field-name mapping in concerns/usage.js's USAGE_EXTRACTORS
  - Responses-API continuity: the Responses->Chat request translator stashes a turn's encrypted_content (the store=false reasoning-continuity token) on the assistant message so a LATER openai->responses hop can restore it; chatCore's stripContinuityFields then deletes encrypted_content/reasoning_encrypted_content from every outbound message before ANY non-Responses upstream call, so that continuity token never reaches a chat-native provider — Chat-native proxies would otherwise 400 on the unknown field
  - Gemini/Antigravity thoughtSignature: Gemini requires a per-function-call cryptographic thoughtSignature for multi-turn tool continuity that an OpenAI- or Claude-native client never sends. openai-to-gemini.js fabricates one from a hardcoded constant (DEFAULT_THINKING_AG_SIGNATURE) when no real signature is cached for that tool_call id/session; openai-to-vertex.js additionally overwrites ANY signature (real or fabricated) with a Vertex-specific constant and strips `id` from functionCall/functionResponse parts entirely because 'Vertex rejects these' — so on the Vertex leg the tool-call id itself does not survive, not just the signature
  - Thinking CONFIGURATION (effort level / token budget) is a separate concern from thinking CONTENT: applyThinking (thinkingUnified.js) reconstructs the effort/budget setting fresh for whatever target format is chosen on every request — it is not something that round-trips, it is recomputed each time from the client's current intent, so the effort setting itself is not 'lost' the way historical thinking content is

### api/translator/console-logs and console-logs/stream — buffered + live console output for the playground UI

- **id:** `translator.playground-console-logs` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard playground polling or SSE-subscribing to server console output while stepping through a translation
- **Input:** None (GET/DELETE take no body; /stream takes no query params)
- **Output:** GET returns the buffered log array; DELETE clears it; GET on /stream opens an SSE connection emitting new lines/clears as they happen
- **Rules:**
  - Both routes call initConsoleLogCapture() at module load (an idempotent hook installer) so any console.* call anywhere in the process while these modules are loaded gets captured into a shared in-memory ring buffer, not just output from translator requests
  - The stream route replays the full current buffer as one 'init' SSE event on connect, then subscribes to 'line'/'lines'/'clear' events from a shared emitter for the process lifetime of the connection, plus a 25s keepalive ping comment to hold the SSE connection through idle proxies
  - Cleanup is made idempotent and triggered from three places (request.signal abort, controller.cancel(), or a failed enqueue) specifically because Next.js's ReadableStream.cancel() is not always invoked on client disconnect — the abort listener is the reliable path
- **Streaming:** yes
- **Errors:** `INTERNAL_ERROR` (getConsoleLogs/clearConsoleLogs throw (500))
- **Note:** 9router's mechanism here is an accident of its stack. Behavior required, mechanism not.

### api/translator/translate, load, save, send — step through and manually fire the pivot

- **id:** `translator.playground-pipeline-debug` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard developer tool for inspecting/replaying the translation pipeline outside a real client request
- **Input:** step (1-3) + body for /translate; file+content for /load and /save; provider+model+body for /send
- **Output:** Intermediate translation results per step, or a live upstream SSE response
- **Rules:**
  - POST /translate step 1 detects {provider, model, sourceFormat, targetFormat} via detectFormat/getTargetFormat/getModelInfo without translating anything
  - Step 2 runs only the source->openai half of translateRequest (targetFormat forced to FORMATS.OPENAI) and strips _toolNameMap before returning, mirroring 3_req_openai.json in the on-disk log naming scheme
  - Step 3 runs only the openai->target half, then goes further than a pure translation step: it looks up an active connection for the provider, builds real credentials, and calls the executor's buildUrl/buildHeaders/transformRequest to show the exact URL/headers/body that would be sent — this is read-only (no request is actually fired) until /send is called separately
  - POST /send performs a real executor.execute() call against the live provider (including the same 401/403 refresh-and-retry pattern as chatCore.js) and streams the raw upstream SSE body straight back to the caller — this is the only one of the 4 routes that reaches an actual provider
  - GET /load and POST /save are a matched pair restricted to an explicit allowedFiles whitelist of 8 filenames (1_req_client.json … 7_res_client.json/.txt) under logs/translator/ — arbitrary filenames are rejected with 400 before any filesystem path is built
- **Streaming:** yes
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (/translate: missing step/body (400), invalid step outside 1-3 (400)), `INVALID_REQUEST` (/load or /save: file not in the 8-entry allowedFiles whitelist (400)), `INVALID_REQUEST` (/send or /translate step 3: no active connection found for the provider (400)), `INTERNAL_ERROR` (any uncaught error in these handlers (500 with error.message))

### Every registered source:target request/response pair

- **id:** `translator.registered-format-pairs` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** Module load — each translator file self-registers via register() as an import side effect
- **Input:** None — registration is a side effect of importing each translator module
- **Output:** requestRegistry and responseRegistry Maps keyed `${from}:${to}`
- **Rules:**
  - Request pairs (12 files register 16 keys): antigravity:openai, claude:kiro (direct), claude:openai, gemini:openai, gemini-cli:openai, openai-responses:openai, openai:openai-responses, openai:claude, openai:commandcode, openai:cursor, openai:gemini, openai:gemini-cli (wrapped in a Cloud Code envelope), openai:antigravity, openai:kiro, openai:ollama, openai:vertex
  - Response pairs (10 files register 14 keys, read as upstream-format:client-format): claude:openai, commandcode:openai, cursor:openai, gemini:openai, gemini-cli:openai, antigravity:openai, vertex:openai, kiro:claude (direct), kiro:openai, ollama:openai, openai:openai-responses, openai-responses:openai, openai:antigravity, openai:claude
  - Every provider that is not natively OpenAI-shaped has an X:openai response leg (so any client format can be reached via the OpenAI pivot) but most providers have only ONE request leg (openai:X) — a client sending X-native requests for cursor/kiro/ollama/vertex/commandcode/gemini(-cli)/antigravity must still go through the OpenAI pivot on the way out, only the way back can shortcut
  - claude:kiro / kiro:claude is the only pair registered as a genuine bidirectional direct route (see translator.direct-route-claude-kiro)

### translateResponse — per-chunk direct route or two-hop pivot, and per-format stream state

- **id:** `translator.response-pivot-dispatch` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** Each streamed chunk (or the single non-streaming body) coming back from the executor
- **Input:** targetFormat (upstream wire format), sourceFormat (client format), one chunk, mutable per-request state
- **Output:** Array of client-format chunks (may be empty)
- **Rules:**
  - Same format short-circuits to decloakStreamChunk only (tool-name decloak still needed even with zero translation, since translateRequest may have cloaked tool names for an OAuth Claude target with no format change)
  - Direct route: responseRegistry.get(`${targetFormat}:${sourceFormat}`) is tried first (mirrors the request-side direct-route check); only kiro:claude is currently registered this way
  - Otherwise: Step 1 targetFormat->openai (skipped if target is already openai), Step 2 openai->sourceFormat (skipped if source is already openai); the openai-shaped intermediate results are stashed on `results._openaiIntermediate` only when BOTH hops actually ran, for logging
  - initState builds format-specific streaming state: a shared base (toolCalls Map, finishReason, usage, block indices) plus, only for openai-responses sources, a large additional set of per-item/per-reasoning/per-function-call tracking fields (msgTextBuf, reasoningBuf, funcArgsBuf, etc.) not needed by any other format
- **Streaming:** yes

### responsesTransformer.js — Chat Completions SSE to Codex Responses-API SSE, and its dead call path

- **id:** `translator.responses-format-transformer` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** Intended for POST /v1/responses when the client wants a streaming Responses-API reply
- **Input:** OpenAI Chat Completions SSE stream
- **Output:** Responses-API SSE events (response.output_item.added, response.output_text.delta, etc.) with sequence_number per event
- **Rules:**
  - createResponsesApiTransformStream is a TransformStream, not a request/response registry function — it reshapes one wire format into another at the SSE-event-shape level (both sides use the openai family), not between two client protocols, which is why it lives in transformer/ rather than translator/request or translator/response
  - Its only caller in the codebase is handleResponsesCore in open-sse/handlers/responsesHandler.js, Case 2 (client wants streaming, provider forced SSE)
  - handleResponsesCore itself has zero callers anywhere in the codebase: the live POST /v1/responses route (src/app/api/v1/responses/route.js) calls handleChat directly, whose own comment states the route is 'now handled by translator pattern (openai-responses format auto-detected)' via the registered openai:openai-responses / openai-responses:openai pair instead
- **Streaming:** yes
- **AIGate required behavior:** createResponsesApiTransformStream is exercised by the live /v1/responses streaming lane, since it exists specifically to shape Codex Responses-API SSE events

### Shared schema enums and config constants translators must use instead of literal strings

- **id:** `translator.schema-config-constants` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** Any translator file, at import time and per-call
- **Input:** None — these are static imports, not request data
- **Output:** Role/block/finish-reason enums and per-provider config values imported from schema/ and config/, per open-sse/AGENTS.md convention
- **Rules:**
  - schema/index.js is a pure-data barrel re-exporting ROLE/GEMINI_ROLE (roles.js), OPENAI_BLOCK/CLAUDE_BLOCK/RESPONSES_ITEM/VALID_OPENAI_CONTENT_TYPES/VALID_OPENAI_MESSAGE_TYPES (blocks.js), OPENAI_FINISH/CLAUDE_STOP/GEMINI_FINISH (finishReasons.js), and MODEL_FALLBACK/DEFAULT_IMAGE_MIME (defaults.js) — none of these files contain logic, only fixed discriminator strings, so a translator that hardcodes e.g. 'tool_use' instead of CLAUDE_BLOCK.TOOL_USE bypasses the single source of truth
  - Mapping LOGIC is kept separate from the enums: concerns/finishReason.js (toOpenAIFinish/fromOpenAIFinish) and concerns/usage.js (USAGE_EXTRACTORS/toOpenAIUsage) both import the schema enums but hold the actual per-provider translation tables, matching the convention split
  - Per-provider magic values that are NOT format-structural (fabricated thinking signatures, Kiro target constants, provider display metadata) live under config/ instead of schema/ — e.g. config/defaultThinkingSignature.js holds the 4 hardcoded DEFAULT_THINKING_*_SIGNATURE base64 blobs consumed by openai-to-gemini.js/openai-to-vertex.js (see translator.pivot-loss)

### streamToJsonConverter.js — collapse a Responses-API SSE stream into one JSON object

- **id:** `translator.stream-to-json-converter` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** A forceStream provider (e.g. Codex) streams even though the client requested non-streaming JSON
- **Input:** Responses-API SSE ReadableStream from the provider
- **Output:** Single JSON object: { id, object: response, created_at, status, output[], usage }
- **Rules:**
  - Unlike responsesTransformer.js, this one is on a live path: chatCore's handleForcedSSEToJson calls it whenever the upstream format is openai-responses (or the provider is flagged isResponsesProvider) and the response content-type is text/event-stream, regardless of whether the client itself used the /v1/responses route
  - processSSEMessage only reacts to 4 event types (response.created, response.output_item.done, response.completed/response.done, response.failed) — every other Responses-API SSE event type (deltas, other item-added events) is silently ignored because only the DONE item snapshot per output_index is kept, not incremental deltas
  - output[] is rebuilt by index from a Map, filling any gap up to the max seen index with an empty `{type: message, content: [], role: assistant}` placeholder — a provider that skips an index never produces a genuinely empty array slot
- **Errors:** `INTERNAL_ERROR` (stream is not a ReadableStream (no getReader) — returns a status: failed JSON object rather than throwing)

### Tool-call id validation, regeneration, and missing-response repair

- **id:** `translator.tool-id-normalization` · **module:** `routing`
- **Trigger:** Every translateRequest call, before format-specific conversion runs (and again inside claude-to-openai.js on the OpenAI leg)
- **Input:** body.messages with tool_calls / tool_use / tool_result blocks in any source shape
- **Output:** body mutated in place: ids sanitized/regenerated, missing tool responses inserted, default tool `type` filled for Claude-format tools
- **Rules:**
  - ensureToolCallIds enforces Anthropic's `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$` id pattern on tool_calls[].id, tool messages' tool_call_id, and Claude-shaped tool_use/tool_result ids found anywhere in the body — every id runs through this check regardless of target format, not only when translating toward Claude
  - An id that fails the pattern is first stripped of invalid characters (sanitizeToolId); if that leaves an empty string, a brand-new deterministic id is generated from `call_msg<i>_tc<j>_<toolName>` — the original id string is not recoverable from the new one
  - fixMissingToolResponses (the generic, format-agnostic version — distinct from claude-to-openai.js's own fixMissingToolResponsesOpenAI local variant) inserts an empty-content tool response immediately after an assistant tool-call message when the very next message does not already answer every tool_call id; it is skipped for kiro targets (translateRequest's `if (targetFormat !== FORMATS.KIRO)` guard) because Kiro's own session-replay canonicalizer performs stricter, source-aware reconciliation that a generic OpenAI role:tool insertion would break
  - defaultClaudeToolType fills `type: custom` onto any Claude-format tool declaration missing a `type`, using spread-first-then-override so a falsy existing type (null/undefined/empty string) does not survive — required because strict Anthropic-compatible gateways (e.g. MiniMax) 400 on tools with no explicit type

## Usage

### calculateCost — pricing lookup and cache-inclusive token math

- **id:** `pricing.cost-calculation-cache-inclusive` · **module:** `usage`
- **Trigger:** Inside saveRequestUsage(), before the usageHistory INSERT
- **Input:** provider, model, canonicalized tokens {prompt_tokens (cache-inclusive), completion_tokens, cached_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens}
- **Output:** cost in dollars (0 if tokens/provider/model/pricing missing)
- **Rules:**
  - calculateCost() looks up pricing via pricingRepo.getPricingForModel(provider, model) — user overrides (KV store) first, then open-sse/providers/pricing.js's built-in table — and delegates the actual arithmetic to calculateCostFromTokens() in open-sse so there is one source of truth for the formula
  - canonicalizeUsage() folds cached_tokens and cache_creation_input_tokens INTO prompt_tokens ahead of time (the cache-inclusive convention) — calculateCostFromTokens then subtracts them back out (nonCachedInput = inputTokens - cachedTokens - cacheCreationTokens) so cached tokens are billed at pricing.cached (falling back to pricing.input) instead of double-counting them at full input rate
  - Any failure (missing provider, missing model, missing pricing, thrown error) resolves to cost = 0, not an error — calculateCost wraps the whole lookup in try/catch and logs to console.error

### /api/pricing — GET merged pricing, PATCH validated overrides, DELETE reset-to-default

- **id:** `pricing.crud-api` · **module:** `usage`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard pricing editor
- **Input:** PATCH body: {provider: {model: {input, output, cached, reasoning, cache_creation}}}; DELETE query: ?provider=&model=
- **Output:** Merged pricing object (built-in PROVIDER_PRICING + user KV overrides)
- **Rules:**
  - GET merges: for every built-in provider/model, a matching user override (if any) is spread over it; for user-only providers/models with no built-in counterpart, the user entry is added as-is
  - PATCH validates before writing: every field key must be one of input/output/cached/reasoning/cache_creation, and every value must be a non-negative finite number, or the whole request 400s before any write happens
  - updatePricing() does a per-provider read-modify-write inside one db.transaction() so concurrent PATCHes to different providers cannot clobber each other's KV rows
  - DELETE resets one model (provider+model given), one whole provider (provider only), or all pricing (neither) back to defaults by removing the corresponding KV override(s)
  - Every write (PATCH or DELETE) calls invalidate() to clear the 5000ms (CACHE_TTL_MS) in-process pricing cache so the next getPricing()/getPricingForModel() call re-reads from the KV store
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (PATCH body has an unknown pricing field or a negative/non-numeric value)
- **AIGate required behavior:** GET /api/pricing/defaults returns the built-in default pricing table over HTTP, matching the route's own doc comment

### getActiveRequests — active counters plus a deduped recent-request ring buffer

- **id:** `usage.active-requests-and-recent-ring` · **module:** `usage`
- **Trigger:** Called by getUsageStats(), by /api/usage/stream's pending-refresh push, and directly for lightweight polling
- **Input:** global._pendingRequests, global._recentRing
- **Output:** { activeRequests: [...], recentRequests: [...], errorProvider }
- **Rules:**
  - recentRing is a 50-item (RING_CAP) in-memory ring, lazily hydrated once per process from the last 50 usageHistory rows on first read (ensureRingInitialized), then appended to on every saveRequestUsage insert
  - recentRequests are deduped by `${model}|${provider}|${promptTokens}|${completionTokens}|${minuteTimestamp}` and rows with zero prompt AND zero completion tokens are dropped entirely, capped at 20 after dedup
  - errorProvider surfaces the last provider that errored, but only within a 10-second window of the error (Date.now() - lastErrorProvider.ts < 10000) — it self-clears by staleness, not by an explicit reset

### getChartData — time-bucketed tokens+cost series

- **id:** `usage.chart-data-buckets` · **module:** `usage`
- **Trigger:** GET /api/usage/chart?period=...
- **Input:** period: today|24h|7d|30d|60d
- **Output:** Array of {label, tokens, cost} buckets
- **Rules:**
  - today: 24 hourly buckets anchored at local midnight, scanning live usageHistory
  - 24h: 24 hourly buckets trailing backward from now, scanning live usageHistory
  - 7d/30d/60d: one bucket per day sourced from pre-aggregated usageDaily rows (loadDaysInRange), not raw history
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (period is not one of the VALID_PERIODS set at the route layer)

### aggregateEntryToDay — per-day rollup by provider/model/account/apiKey/endpoint

- **id:** `usage.daily-rollup-aggregation` · **module:** `usage`
- **Trigger:** Inside the saveRequestUsage transaction, once per new row
- **Input:** The usageDaily row for today's dateKey (or a fresh zeroed one) plus the new entry
- **Output:** Updated usageDaily.data JSON blob with requests/promptTokens/completionTokens/cachedTokens/cost totals and 5 breakdown maps
- **Rules:**
  - dateKey is computed by getLocalDateKey() using the server process's local timezone (new Date().getFullYear/Month/Date), not UTC
  - byApiKey buckets missing apiKey under the literal key 'local-no-key' rather than omitting the request from that breakdown
  - Each breakdown key embeds enough context to redisplay later without re-joining (rawModel, provider) via addToCounter's `meta` merge

### Why live counters live on global.* instead of module-scope state

- **id:** `usage.global-state-next-reeval` · **module:** `usage`
- **Trigger:** usageRepo.js module load
- **Input:** None — this is a module-initialization-time decision, not a per-request input
- **Output:** global._pendingRequests, global._lastErrorProvider, global._statsEmitter, global._pendingTimers, global._recentRing, global._connectionMapCache, global._statsEmitTimers
- **Rules:**
  - All 7 pieces of live, in-memory usage state are guarded with `if (!global._x) global._x = ...` instead of being declared as module-scope `let`/`const`
  - The in-source comment states the reason directly: 'In-memory state shared across Next.js modules'
  - Next.js can evaluate a given source module more than once within the same server process (dev-mode HMR, and the route-handler module graph in general); module-scope state would silently re-initialize on each re-evaluation — a fresh EventEmitter with no subscribers, a reset pending-counter map — breaking the pending-request badge and dropping in-flight SSE listeners. Attaching to the single process-wide `global` object survives re-evaluation because it is not tied to any one module instance.
- **Note:** 9router's mechanism here is an accident of its stack. Behavior required, mechanism not.

### /api/usage/history is not a history-rows endpoint — it returns the same aggregate shape as /api/usage/stats

- **id:** `usage.history-route-returns-aggregate-not-rows` · **module:** `usage`
- **Trigger:** GET /api/usage/history
- **Input:** none
- **Output:** The full getUsageStats() aggregate object (period defaults to 'all')
- **Rules:**
  - history/route.js calls `await getUsageStats()` with no period argument, which defaults to 'all' inside getUsageStats — an aggregate stats object identical in shape to what /api/usage/stats?period=all returns
  - The function that actually returns per-request rows with provider/model/date-range filtering — getUsageHistory(filter) — is exported from usageRepo.js and re-exported through both src/lib/db/index.js and src/lib/usageDb.js, but has zero callers anywhere in the checkout (verified: the only matches for 'getUsageHistory' are its own definition and the two re-export barrel lines)
- **AIGate required behavior:** A route named /api/usage/history returns per-request usage history rows — the sibling getUsageHistory(filter) function (provider/model/date-range filterable) appears purpose-built to back exactly this route

### saveRequestUsage — dedup check, single-transaction 3-way write

- **id:** `usage.history-write-dedup-transaction` · **module:** `usage`
- **Trigger:** Any fire-and-forget saveRequestUsage(entry) call
- **Input:** {provider, model, tokens, connectionId, apiKey, endpoint, timestamp?}
- **Output:** One usageHistory row, one usageDaily upsert, one _meta lifetime counter increment — or a no-op endpoint patch if a matching row already exists
- **Rules:**
  - Before inserting, a SELECT looks for an existing usageHistory row with the same timestamp (ISO string, millisecond precision), provider, model, connectionId, apiKey, promptTokens and completionTokens
  - If found, no new row is written — at most the existing row's endpoint is backfilled if it was previously null
  - If not found, all three writes (history insert, usageDaily upsert via aggregateEntryToDay, _meta.totalRequestsLifetime increment) happen inside one db.transaction(), justified in-source by better-sqlite3 being synchronous so no other JS runs mid-transaction in the same process
  - pushToRing() and the debounced stats-event only fire when a new row was actually inserted (inserted === true)
- **Errors:** `INTERNAL_ERROR` (the transaction throws (e.g. adapter failure))
- **AIGate required behavior:** Every completed request that calls saveRequestUsage produces its own usageHistory row

### trackPendingRequest and the PENDING_TIMEOUT_MS watchdog

- **id:** `usage.pending-request-orphan-timeout` · **module:** `usage`
- **Trigger:** trackPendingRequest(model, provider, connectionId, started, error) called at request dispatch, completion, disconnect and error points
- **Input:** model, provider, connectionId, started (bool), error (bool)
- **Output:** In-memory pending counters (global._pendingRequests) used to render the 'active requests' widget
- **Rules:**
  - started=true increments byModel[modelKey] and byAccount[connectionId][modelKey], then (re)arms a 60000ms (PENDING_TIMEOUT_MS) setTimeout keyed by `${connectionId}|${modelKey}`
  - started=false decrements both counters (clamped to >= 0 via Math.max) and clears the timer — this is the normal 'request finished' signal, called from success, error, disconnect and stream-complete paths
  - If the timer fires before a matching started=false ever arrives (unhandled exception before onError/onDisconnect wiring, process anomaly), it force-resets the counter to 0 for that model/account and deletes itself — a watchdog against a permanently-stuck 'N active requests' badge, not a request-level timeout that cancels anything
  - The timer is a plain Node setTimeout, not unref'd, scoped per connectionId+modelKey so a second started=true for the same pair replaces (clearTimeout + reschedule) rather than stacking timers

### GET /api/usage/providers — distinct-provider filter list for the request-details tab

- **id:** `usage.providers-distinct-api` · **module:** `usage`
- **Trigger:** RequestDetailsTab.js loads its provider filter dropdown
- **Input:** none
- **Output:** {providers: [{id, name}]}
- **Rules:**
  - Sources DISTINCT provider from the requestDetails table, not usageHistory — the in-source comment explains this avoids parsing every row's full JSON blob (usageHistory rows can total hundreds of MB), which previously caused OOM
  - Display name resolution: providerNodes.name first, then getProviderByAlias/AI_PROVIDERS config name, else the raw provider id
  - This list is scoped to the request-details table specifically (it is the filter for that tab), so it naturally returns an empty array whenever requestDetails is empty — which is the default state, since observability is off by default (see usage.request-details-buffered-persistence)

### appendRequestLog is an empty no-op; the log view is derived read-side from usageHistory

- **id:** `usage.recent-logs-and-noop-append` · **module:** `usage`
- **Trigger:** GET /api/usage/logs or /api/usage/request-logs
- **Input:** none
- **Output:** Array of formatted log lines: 'DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm:ss | model | PROVIDER | account | sent | received | status'
- **Rules:**
  - appendRequestLog() takes any arguments and does nothing — it is `export async function appendRequestLog() {}`, per an in-source comment: 'request log is now derived from usageHistory table on read'
  - Every one of its 5+ call sites (chatCore.js PENDING/FAILED lines, stream.js) invokes it as `appendRequestLog({...}).catch(() => {})` and never inspects the resolved value or branches on it — nothing depends on it having an effect
  - getRecentLogs(limit=200) instead reads the last N usageHistory rows directly and formats them for display, resolving connectionId -> account name via a fresh (uncached) connectionsRepo call every invocation — unlike getActiveRequests' 30s-TTL connectionMapCache

### GET /api/usage/request-details — pagination plus mandatory content redaction

- **id:** `usage.request-details-api-redaction` · **module:** `usage`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard's request-details tab fetches a page of detail rows
- **Input:** page, pageSize (1-100), provider, model, connectionId, status, startDate, endDate
- **Output:** {details: [...], pagination}, with request/providerRequest/providerResponse/response fields replaced by {redacted: true}
- **Rules:**
  - page must be >= 1 and pageSize must be 1-100, both validated with an explicit 400 before querying
  - Every returned detail has its request, providerRequest, providerResponse and response fields overwritten with {redacted: true} — the in-source comment states this is deliberate: those fields hold full user prompts, tool calls and provider responses, and any dashboard-authenticated user (or anyone, if requireLogin is disabled) could otherwise read every user's conversation history through this endpoint
  - Only metadata (model, tokens, latency, status, timestamps) survives redaction
- **Errors:** `INVALID_REQUEST` (page < 1 or pageSize outside 1-100)

### requestDetailsRepo — disabled by default, buffered batch writes, capped and sanitized

- **id:** `usage.request-details-buffered-persistence` · **module:** `usage`
- **Trigger:** saveRequestDetail(detail) called from chatCore's success/error paths
- **Input:** The full buildRequestDetail() object, including request/providerRequest/providerResponse/response bodies
- **Output:** requestDetails row (or nothing, if observability is disabled)
- **Rules:**
  - The write is a no-op unless config.enabled resolves to true. getObservabilityConfig()'s resolution order: (1) if ENABLE_REQUEST_LOGS is set to anything (not undefined), enabled = that value.toLowerCase() === 'true' and settings/OBSERVABILITY_ENABLED are never consulted; (2) otherwise, uiFlag = typeof settings.enableObservability === 'boolean' — when true, enabled is settings.enableObservability itself (DEFAULT_SETTINGS.enableObservability is false, which is why the feature is off by default in practice); when settings.enableObservability is NOT strictly a boolean, enabled instead falls back to envFallback = process.env.OBSERVABILITY_ENABLED !== 'false' (true unless that env var is the exact string 'false', so an unset OBSERVABILITY_ENABLED in this fallback branch defaults enabled to true); (3) if getSettings() throws or any step in the try block throws, the outer catch hardcodes enabled: false regardless of any env var
  - Enabled writes are buffered in a module-scope array and flushed either when the buffer reaches batchSize (default 20) or on a flushIntervalMs timer (default 5000ms) — whichever comes first
  - flushToDatabase() drains the entire buffer in a while-loop so pushes that happen during the async flush are still captured, and writes all buffered items inside one db.transaction()
  - After each flush, rows beyond maxRecords (default 200 in this file's own fallback; 1000 in settingsRepo's DEFAULT_SETTINGS) are deleted, oldest-timestamp-first
  - sanitizeHeaders() strips authorization/x-api-key/cookie/token/api-key headers from item.request.headers before it is ever written to disk
  - truncateField() replaces any request/providerRequest/providerResponse/response field larger than maxJsonSize (default 5KB) with a {_truncated, _originalSize, _preview} stub instead of storing it whole
  - beforeExit/SIGINT/SIGTERM/exit handlers force a final flush of any buffered-but-unflushed items so a graceful shutdown doesn't lose the tail of the buffer
- **Errors:** `INTERNAL_ERROR` (flushToDatabase's transaction throws)

### Every field recorded for one request, in the order it becomes known

- **id:** `usage.request-field-trace-order` · **module:** `usage`
- **Trigger:** A chat request reaches a success or error return point inside handleChatCore (or the embeddings/other modality equivalents)
- **Input:** modelInfo {provider, model}, credentials.connectionId, the translated request body, the upstream response body, and wall-clock marks
- **Output:** A buildRequestDetail() object persisted via saveRequestDetail, and a canonicalized {provider, model, tokens, connectionId, apiKey, endpoint, cost, status} object persisted via saveRequestUsage
- **Rules:**
  - provider and model are known first — they come from modelInfo at handler entry, before any network call
  - account (connectionId) is known next — it is set on credentials before dispatch and threaded through as connectionId
  - input/output/cached tokens are known only after the upstream response returns: extractUsageFromResponse() branches on Claude (usage.input_tokens), OpenAI (usage.prompt_tokens) or Gemini (usageMetadata) response shapes to pull them out
  - cached tokens are folded into prompt_tokens by canonicalizeUsage() before storage (the cache-inclusive convention), not stored as a separate additive field
  - cost is computed last and lazily: saveUsageStats()/saveRequestUsage() receive raw tokens and provider/model; calculateCost() looks up pricing and multiplies inside saveRequestUsage itself, not by the caller
  - latency.total = Date.now() - requestStartTime, computed once the outcome (success or error) is known; latency.ttft is only ever set by the streaming path (buildOnStreamComplete) — every non-streaming and forced-JSON error/success path hardcodes ttft: 0
  - status is 'success' (buildRequestDetail default) or explicitly 'error'; the error message is stored under response.error, not as a separate field
  - fallback attempts are NOT part of the usage row: a single request may try several accounts/providers before one succeeds, but only the account/provider that finally answered (or the account whose failure ended the loop) is passed into saveRequestUsage/saveRequestDetail — see edgeCases
- **Streaming:** yes

### GET /api/usage/stream — SSE push of usage stats

- **id:** `usage.sse-live-stream` · **module:** `usage`
- **Trigger:** Dashboard opens the usage/quota view
- **Input:** none (long-lived GET)
- **Output:** text/event-stream of JSON stats payloads
- **Rules:**
  - On connect: sends one full stats payload immediately (state.send)
  - Subscribes to statsEmitter's 'update' event (full getUsageStats() recalculation) and 'pending' event (lightweight activeRequests+recentRequests+errorProvider refresh merged onto the last cached full stats)
  - Both events are debounced at the source: scheduleStatsEvent('update', 250) and scheduleStatsEvent('pending', 150-default) in usageRepo.js collapse bursts of writes into one emit per 150ms/250ms window
  - A 25000ms keepalive comment ping (`: ping\n\n`) is sent on an interval independent of the event-driven pushes, to hold the connection through idle periods
- **Streaming:** yes

### getUsageStats — live-history path vs pre-aggregated usageDaily path

- **id:** `usage.stats-query-dual-path` · **module:** `usage`
- **Trigger:** GET /api/usage/stats?period=... or /api/usage/history (no period)
- **Input:** period: today|24h|7d|30d|60d|all
- **Output:** {totalRequests, totalPromptTokens, ..., byProvider, byModel, byAccount, byApiKey, byEndpoint, last10Minutes, pending, activeRequests, recentRequests, errorProvider}
- **Rules:**
  - period in {today, 24h} scans usageHistory rows directly for the window (useDailySummary = false)
  - period in {7d, 30d, 60d, all} sums pre-aggregated usageDaily rows instead (useDailySummary = true), then does a second pass over raw usageHistory (bounded to the same window) purely to overlay precise lastUsed timestamps onto each breakdown entry
  - Provider/connection/API-key display names are enriched via 3 parallel repo imports (connectionsRepo, apiKeysRepo, nodesRepo) at the top of the function, each independently wrapped in try/catch so one repo failing degrades to raw ids instead of failing the whole stats call
  - last10Minutes is always computed from live usageHistory regardless of period, as a fixed 10-bucket-per-minute series

### Whether the usage write blocks the HTTP response

- **id:** `usage.write-not-synchronous` · **module:** `usage`
- **Trigger:** saveUsageStats()/saveRequestUsage() called from any chat/embeddings success or error path
- **Input:** {provider, model, tokens, connectionId, apiKey, endpoint}
- **Output:** A pending usageHistory write that races the HTTP response instead of gating it
- **Rules:**
  - Every call site invokes saveRequestUsage(...).catch(() => {}) without awaiting it — the promise is fired and its rejection swallowed, the caller moves on immediately
  - saveRequestUsage's own function body starts with `const db = await getAdapter();` — even the portion of the function that runs before the caller regains control is minimal; the DB work happens after a yield to the event loop
  - Because the write is unawaited and off the critical path, it is NOT synchronous with the response and does not sit on the hot path — the condition stated for labeling this IMPLEMENTATION_ACCIDENT does not hold here
- **Streaming:** yes

## Suspected bugs — do NOT reproduce

| id | Expected | Actual | Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| `apikey.list-keys` | A key-management list endpoint masks or omits the secret value after initial issuance (standard practice, and consistent with GET /api/settings stripping password/oidcClientSecret) | rowToKey() copies row.key verbatim into every list/get response with no masking | Any surface that can read GET /api/keys (dashboard XSS, an over-permissioned session, a logging/proxy layer that captures response bodies) leaks every currently-active API key in plaintext, not just the one just-created key |
| `apikey.legacy-format-unenforced` | Given generateCrc/parseApiKey/verifyApiKeyCrc exist specifically to bind a key to a machineId and detect tampering, the request-time auth path (validateApiKey / isValidApiKey) calls verifyApiKeyCrc (or parseApiKey) to reject a key whose embedded CRC doesn't match its machineId+keyId before or in addition to the DB lookup | validateApiKey performs only a raw string equality lookup against the stored apiKeys.key column; parseApiKey/verifyApiKeyCrc/isNewFormatKey are dead code outside of key generation and are never invoked on the read/auth path | The CRC provides no security property at request time — it cannot be used to detect a corrupted/tampered key independent of the DB, and the legacy sk-{random8} format is accepted with exactly the same trust as the new format purely because both are opaque strings to validateApiKey; anyone who can insert or copy a row into apiKeys (backup restore, DB access, export leak) gets a working key regardless of format |
| `settings.patch-password-change` | The first-time password-change gate in PATCH /api/settings checks currentPassword against the operator's actual configured initial password, i.e. `process.env.INITIAL_PASSWORD \|\| "123456"`, mirroring the check already implemented in src/app/api/auth/login/route.js line 58 for the same purpose | settings/route.js line 62 compares currentPassword only against the hardcoded literal "123456", never consulting process.env.INITIAL_PASSWORD | An operator who sets INITIAL_PASSWORD to a non-default value (as CLAUDE.md instructs: 'must override') cannot use that real initial password to complete their first password change through the dashboard/API — currentPassword !== '123456' is rejected with 401 even though it is the correct, configured initial password. Worse, the well-known literal '123456' still satisfies this specific check regardless of what INITIAL_PASSWORD was set to, so on an install that changed the env var specifically to move off the public default, a local caller who still knows the old default can pass this gate anyway. |
